Coimbatore | January 11, 2026 | The cyber crime wing of the Coimbatore City Police has busted an organised online fraud network allegedly operating out of Gujarat’s Surat, arresting 10 persons in connection with the cheating of a senior citizen of ₹16.49 lakh through a fake traffic challan message sent on WhatsApp.
According to the police, the accused targeted a 71-year-old resident of Kavundampalayam by impersonating transport authorities and inducing him to download a malicious mobile application, which ultimately gave them access to his bank account.
Certified Cyber Crime Investigator Course Launched by Centre for Police Technology
The complainant, Samuel Chandrabose, stated that in September 2025 he received a WhatsApp message claiming that a traffic fine had been imposed on him and required immediate payment. The message carried a link and instructions to download an application to complete the transaction. Believing the message to be genuine, he followed the instructions.
Soon after the application was installed, his mobile phone became non-functional. Within a short span of time, ₹16.49 lakh was fraudulently withdrawn from his bank account through 12 separate transactions. The victim later realised that he had been duped and approached the cyber crime wing of the Coimbatore City Police.
Given the magnitude of the fraud, a detailed investigation was launched involving technical analysis, digital forensics and tracking of banking transaction trails. The probe revealed that the money had been routed through multiple accounts and ultimately led investigators to Surat, where the fraud network was being operated.
A special team was constituted by the cyber crime wing, which conducted a swift operation in Surat and apprehended all 10 accused involved in the racket. Police officials said the arrests were made following coordinated efforts and based on credible digital evidence.
The arrested persons have been identified as Badlia Rajnibai Thalsibai (37), Vishwabai Himmatbai Rattadio (36), Rattadio Savan (34), Koshilvijay Dayal Singh (37), Rathore Jithendrasingh Sharvansingh (26), Kirase Mahendrasingh Thakesingh (35), Shovadia Miral Manojbai (22), Kabil Rajubai Gotre (36), Sovadia Meet Manojbai (25) and Balasanthan Jeynath (34).
During the searches conducted as part of the operation, the police seized 311 debit and credit cards, 10 mobile phones, a card swiping machine and a cheque book from the accused. Preliminary investigations suggest that the group used mule accounts and multiple bank cards to launder the cheated money and withdraw it in small tranches to avoid detection.
All the accused have been produced before a judicial magistrate and remanded to judicial custody. Further investigation is under way to ascertain whether the group was involved in similar frauds across other States.
In a significant development, the Coimbatore City Police has managed to freeze and recover ₹6.39 lakh from the bank accounts linked to the accused. Officials said the recovered amount would be handed over to the complainant after completion of the required legal formalities. Efforts are ongoing to trace and recover the remaining amount.
Commissioner of Police N. Kannan felicitated the special team for the successful operation. He commended Assistant Commissioner of Police M.P. Divya, Inspector of Cyber Crime Wing Alaguraj, and 10 other personnel for their prompt action and effective coordination in cracking an inter-State cyber fraud case.
The police have reiterated their warning to the public against clicking on unknown or suspicious links received via WhatsApp or other messaging platforms. Officials stressed that government departments do not send messages asking citizens to download applications for payment of fines, KYC updates or bank-related alerts, and advised people to verify such messages and report them immediately to the cyber crime helpline or the nearest police station.

The accused, identified as Pritesh Prajapati, is said to have posed as school staff or known contacts to gain the confidence of victims before asking them to share one-time passwords (OTPs) or transfer money for supposed emergencies. How did it all start?

The scammers, under the guise of TRAI, demanded he either travel to the Lucknow police station or register his statement via video call on WhatsApp. “Any normal person will choose the second option (video call over WhatsApp)," adding, “After receiving a WhatsApp call, I found a scammer in a police uniform and set up like a police station."
The setup was so convincing that anyone could have fallen for this “digital arrest" scam. The impersonator, posing as a police officer, asked Patel to switch to his rear camera and give a 360-degree view of his surroundings. This was meant to confirm that he was alone, ensuring there would be no interruptions as he provided his “statement" to the supposed officer.
Aadhaar details and phone number linked to illegal activites
The scammers informed him that his Aadhaar details had been used to purchase a SIM card linked to illegal activities and urged him to file a complaint immediately. Throughout this, Patel was kept on the call. Soon after, he received a fake document purportedly issued by the Supreme Court of India, stating that he had provided information to a wanted criminal, Mohammed Islam Malik Nawab, to open accounts at ICICI Bank, HDFC Bank, and SBI. According to the forged document, these accounts were implicated in a large-scale money laundering and investment fraud case.
“Next step is very interesting, he used walky talky to inquire about me in the police headquarters. His tone changed, and he started to threaten me after the headquarter informed him to arrest me!" Patel added.
They linked Patel to money laundering case to find out “how many bank accounts the victim has and how much money was in each one".
Patel further said that the scammers began asking if he used UPI apps or online banking, likely intending to use these methods to transfer the funds.
Towards the end of an hour-long scam, the fake police officer transfers the case to fake DCP. “He (fake DCP) informed me that I needed to transfer all the money I had in my bank accounts, which would be returned if I was found innocent, and they would give me a certificate!"

ECI), asserting they have not violated any laws. Last September witnessed a sweeping search operation by the I-T department, targeting the offices of 23 such RUPPs, 35 intermediaries, and three exit providers in Gujarat.
"The extensive operation was prompted by compelling evidence pointing to a pervasive scam involving political party donations, employed to claim phoney deductions under Sections 80GGC/80GGB of the Income Tax Act. Subsequently, the funds were illicitly rerouted back to the donors through cash, RTGS, NEFT, or other banking channels," said a source in the I-T department.

Subsequently, the funds were illicitly rerouted back to the donors through cash, RTGS, NEFT, or other banking channels," said a source in the I-T department.
Unrecognised political parties can be newly registered parties or those that have not secured enough percentage of votes in the assembly or general elections to fulfil the criteria to become a state party. They can also be parties that have never contested elections since their registration.
Some office-bearers of the RUPPs in Gujarat have admitted to engaging in fraudulent donation activities, charging commissions ranging from 4.50% to 5%, said sources in the department. "The I-T raids uncovered incriminating evidence, including bogus donation receipts, diaries containing commission details, and WhatsApp chats on the mobile phones of RUPP office-bearers and their key handlers, confirming the allegations," said a source.
The department also found that after receiving donations, the parties transferred money in the name of political activities or social welfare to their intermediaries, which were shell companies, said sources.
Further investigation revealed the involvement of certain chartered accountants, accountants, and tax consultants in the scam. "These professionals played a significant role in soliciting donors on behalf of the RUPPs, earning higher commissions than the office-bearers themselves. Agents involved in such activities also earned commissions ranging from 0.50% to 0.80%," revealed the source.
It was discovered that most of these political parties were not filing timely annual contribution reports with the ECI, as mandated by the Representation of People's Act, 1951. Such reports are a prerequisite for claiming exemption under Section 13A of the Income Tax Act, 1961.
Karim Lakhani, a chartered accountant, emphasized the dire need for stringent checks on such nefarious activities. "The government should implement regulations for donations to political parties. It can be similar to charitable trusts, where donations are limited to 10% of an individual's annual income, and the deductible amount is 50% of the donation made," he said.
The I-T department has issued notices to over 4,000 donors, primarily salaried individuals, regarding their involvement in bogus donations to these RUPPs.
Sulabh Padshah, a chartered accountant, said, "Most donors have responded to the department, stating that at the time of their donations, these parties were active on the ECI website"

title: IIM Ahmedabad employee fooled in Rs 50 lakh bogus SME IPO pitch via WhatsApp trading scam - The Economic Times

According to The Times of India, the 49-year-old victim, who resides in Chandkheda, filed a complaint with the Cybercrime police on Monday after discovering that his in-app trading account had been blocked and his phone number cut off from further contact with the fraudsters.
Lured through Facebook, hooked by fake profits
The incident began on February 19, when the complainant clicked on a WhatsApp group link titled “E-28 ASK Capital Circle” while browsing Facebook. Group administrators began offering investment “tips” and instructed him to download a mobile application named “ASKICPRO.”
He initially observed the group’s discussions but was soon persuaded to make a small investment. On March 19, he deposited Rs 25,000 to buy shares of “CLARA Industries Ltd” and was asked to sell them shortly after. The next day, his in-app wallet reflected Rs 28,800, encouraging further trades.
By March 27, his wallet balance had grown to Rs 5 lakh, with the app displaying consistent “profits” and the fraudsters urging him to participate in “OTC trading.” This pattern of fake gains appeared to cement the victim’s trust in the platform.
Fake SME IPO allotment letter, Rs 42 lakh sunk
The group’s administrators later convinced him to apply for an IPO in the name of “Informative Solution SME.” After applying through the ASKICPRO app, he received a seemingly official IPO allotment letter and was asked to deposit Rs 42,80,640.
When he expressed concern about the high amount, the scammers offered to facilitate a loan of Rs 18 lakh if he deposited Rs 20 lakh upfront. He agreed, and eventually paid the full amount in installments.
Upon attempting to withdraw the funds, he was told to make an additional Rs 15 lakh deposit for “capital verification.” After negotiating, he deposited Rs 10 lakh more, according to The Times of India.
Blocked and vanished
The final blow came when he tried to withdraw Rs 45 lakh from his app wallet, only to find the transaction had failed. His account was promptly blocked, he was removed from the WhatsApp group, and his mobile number was blacklisted by the fraudsters.
The case is now under investigation by Ahmedabad Cybercrime police.

title: Bank manager in Ahmedabad loses Rs 6.6 lakh in trading scam - The Times of India

In a significant breakthrough, the Cyber Police Station of North District, under the leadership of DCP North Delhi, has busted a cyber fraud syndicate operating out of Surat, Gujarat, which orchestrated a ₹44.6 lakh scam through fake stock trading schemes and forged banking identities.
The operation was initiated following a complaint from a Delhi resident who was duped of ₹44.6 lakhs through a fraudulent share market scheme. According to police officials, the accused created a counterfeit WhatsApp group impersonating a legitimate stock trading platform. Promising exorbitant returns, they lured the unsuspecting victim into transferring large sums of money.
Forged identities used to open bank accounts
Investigations revealed that the fraudsters used forged identities to open multiple current bank accounts. These accounts, while appearing legitimate, were under the complete control of the syndicate, which retained all access credentials.
The accused then sold these accounts to handlers for commission many of whom were linked to a wider international cybercrime network, including a Chinese national.
The scam followed a classic digital fraud route: funds deposited into fake accounts were quickly withdrawn in cash and rerouted through hawala channels to foreign destinations, bypassing regulatory checks.
Technical surveillance leads police to Surat
A breakthrough came through detailed technical surveillance and call detail record (CDR) analysis. Armed with digital evidence, the police team conducted a swift raid in Surat. The operation led to the arrest of two accused individuals and the seizure of incriminating materials, including mobile phones and a SIM card.
In a photograph released by the Delhi Police, the arrested individuals can be seen seated with their faces covered, surrounded by officers of the Cyber Cell. Behind them, the signage of the Cyber Police Station, North District stands prominently, reinforcing the dedication of the force in tackling digital crime.
Authorities have confirmed that the investigation is ongoing, with further arrests likely as more links to the international racket are uncovered.

title: Gujarat: Pharma group in GST net over flagged transactions of Rs 115cr - The Times of India
article_text:
Ahmedabad: The State Goods and Services Tax (SGST) department recently detected a major case of GST evasion involving a pharmaceutical group in the city operating through 11 related entities. Investigators flagged taxable transactions of Rs 114.89 crore and fraudulent input tax credit (ITC) of Rs 20.68 crore.
Two persons were arrested and produced before the additional chief judicial magistrate in Ahmedabad, who remanded them to judicial custody for 14 days until Feb 3.
The crackdown followed coordinated search operations at 32 premises across 14 locations, largely in and around Ahmedabad. Officials found that several entities functioned from common premises in Makarba, while many declared places of business were either non-functional or existed only on paper, according to the SGST department.
Investigators said some group entities amended their GST registrations to include iron and steel/ingots trading, allegedly to facilitate bogus billing. The probe revealed fraudulent availment of ITC through fake invoices and e-way bills, without any actual movement of goods.
Using advanced data analytics, including RFID tracking and toll plaza verification, the department determined that the transactions were purely paper-based. Scrutiny of records so far has pegged the evasion well above the Rs 5 crore threshold, which makes the offence cognisable and non-bailable under Section 132 of the CGST and GGST Acts.
Officials said further investigation is underway, including scrutiny of seized documents, digital evidence, financial trails, and possible inter-state linkages.

title: 'FCI Director' turns out to be a conman: Gujarat police bust Rs 68 Lakh in government job scam - The New Indian Express
article_text:
AHMEDABAD: Halol Rural Police in Panchmahal district of Gujarat have arrested Bharat Parmar, a man accused of masquerading as a high-ranking Food Corporation of India (FCI) official while allegedly running a statewide government job scam worth lakhs of rupees.
Investigators believe the fraud may extend far beyond the Rs 68 lakh unearthed so far, with the possibility that several more victims across Gujarat could have been duped.
The accused, despite having studied only up to Class VII, allegedly built an elaborate web of deception.
Presenting himself as an FCI director with deep connections across government departments, Parmar reportedly targeted unemployed youth and their families, exploiting their aspirations for stable government employment.
Preliminary investigations indicate that Parmar had allegedly established a network of agents across Gujarat who identified job seekers and convinced them that government appointments could be secured through his influence.
The accused allegedly promised recruitment in prestigious government organizations, including ONGC and other public sector entities.
To make the fraud appear genuine, candidates were provided with fake interview call letters, forged appointment-related documents, and fabricated correspondence bearing the names of government institutions.
The scam began to unravel after multiple victims approached police with similar allegations.
Halol DySP V.J. Rathod said the breakthrough came after retired railway employee Manubhai Patel filed a detailed complaint.
"Manu Patel informed us that he came in contact with Bharat Parmar in 2020. During their meeting, Parmar introduced himself as a director in FCI and claimed that he had influence and contacts across various government departments. He assured the complainant that securing a government job would be easy through his network," Rathod said.
The officer further explained that Patel was persuaded to arrange a job for his son in ONGC.
"To secure the promised appointment, Bharat Parmar allegedly collected Rs 7,78,950 through RTGS transactions as well as cash payments. He subsequently handed over what appeared to be an official call letter. However, despite receiving the document, no interview process, verification procedure or recruitment activity ever took place," Rathod stated.
As doubts grew, Patel repeatedly demanded his money back. "The accused returned approximately Rs 3 lakh, but failed to repay the remaining amount. During further inquiries, it emerged that several other individuals had allegedly been cheated in a similar manner. Based on the evidence gathered so far, complaints indicate that the accused has defrauded multiple victims of nearly ₹68 lakh," the DySP added.
Armed with the evidence, Halol Rural Police launched a surveillance operation and laid a trap.
The accused was eventually apprehended from a guest hotel located on the Halol-Godhra bypass road. The arrest opened the door to a trove of incriminating material.
Police recovered more than 15 bank passbooks belonging to different accounts, eight mobile phones, duplicate FCI letterheads, forged appointment letters, and numerous documents suspected to have been used in the recruitment racket.
Investigators are now examining financial transactions, communication records and the identities of individuals connected to the network.
Authorities suspect that the scam may have operated for years and spread across multiple districts.
Even more significantly, investigators have not ruled out the possibility that influential intermediaries or politically connected individuals may surface during the probe.
Police sources indicate that several leads are being examined to determine whether others facilitated introductions, collected money or helped create the illusion of official influence.
Halol Rural Police have circulated detailed information about the accused to law enforcement agencies across Gujarat to identify additional complaints and possible links to similar fraud cases.
Following his arrest, Bharat Parmar was produced before a court and remanded for further interrogation.
Investigators believe the custodial questioning could reveal the full scale of the recruitment racket, uncover additional victims and expose others who may have played a role in the operation.
Police are also planning a deeper probe into the role of the accused's driver and close associates, suspecting that fresh revelations could emerge as the investigation progresses.

To make the recruitment offers appear completely genuine, the syndicate provided victims with fabricated interview call letters, forged appointment-related documents, and fabricated official correspondence. What looked like a fast track into the police force turned into a costly deception in Gujarat after a man posing as a senior IPS officer was arrested for allegedly cheating multiple families of Rs 2.36 crore by promising government jobs.
The Gujarat Crime Branch has arrested Vivek Dave in connection with the scam, which unfolded in Rajkot and involved elaborate impersonation, false assurances and staged confidence-building tactics. Police said Dave worked with an accomplice, Hari Gamara, who is currently absconding.
PROMISE OF POLICE JOBS FOR MONEY
The case came to light after a complainant approached the police, alleging that Dave and Gamara offered to secure his son a Police Sub Inspector post for Rs 50 lakh. An advance of Rs 15 lakh was paid, with the remaining amount to be handed over once the appointment order was issued.
When the son’s name did not appear in the list, the family demanded their money back. Dave returned Rs 14 lakh, keeping Rs 1 lakh with him.

A few months later, the complainant received another call with a more ambitious proposal. He was told his son could be appointed Deputy Superintendent of Police for Rs 2.36 crore. Trusting the offer, the family paid Rs 1.89 crore in instalments.
No appointment order followed. After repeated demands, Rs 88 lakh was returned, but the remaining amount was never repaid, prompting the family to file a police complaint.
KHAKI UNIFORM AND SOCIAL APPEARANCES
Investigators said Dave went to great lengths to project himself as a senior police officer. He attended social events wearing a khaki uniform similar to that of an IPS officer, introducing himself as a high-ranking official. The uniform and confident demeanour helped him gain credibility and draw families into the scheme.
Police believe several youths and their families were targeted with similar promises of PSI and DSP appointments, with money collected in phases.
VIDEO EVIDENCE CRACKS THE CASE
The investigation gathered momentum after police obtained a video that allegedly showed money being handed over to the accused. Based on this evidence, the Crime Branch laid a trap and arrested Dave.
He is currently being questioned, with investigators examining financial trails and possible links to other victims. Efforts are ongoing to trace and arrest Hari Gamara, who is believed to have played a key role in negotiating deals and collecting funds.

At first, it seemed like a dream job — “earn ₹60,000 a month doing online work overseas.” But that dream turned into a nightmare for over 100 Gujarati youths now trapped in Myanmar, enslaved in cybercrime compounds run by transnational scam syndicates.
The haunting plea of 26-year-old Kunjan Shah from Savli, Vadodara, has now gone viral across social media: “We escaped the scam centre, but we’re starving and hiding in the jungle. Please help us.”
A Digital Job Scam Turns to Human Trafficking
According to sources, human traffickers lured jobless graduates from Gujarat with promises of positions in Bangkok. But after landing in Thailand, the men were smuggled across the Moei River into Myanmar’s infamous KK Park and Myawaddy regions — the epicentres of Southeast Asia’s cyber-slavery trade.
Once inside, everything changed. Their passports were seized, and they were forced to run online fraud operations — love scams, fake trading apps, digital arrests — under threats, beatings, and surveillance by armed guards. Resisting meant torture or being sold to another gang.
“They Treat Us Like Machines”
Back home, families are in turmoil. Jayesh Shah, Kunjan’s father, told reporters, “We sold land to send our son abroad. Now we don’t even know if he’s alive.” Villagers from Desar and Savli have approached Gujarat Police and local politicians in desperation.
Savli MLA Ketan Inamdar has written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Home Minister Amit Shah, and EAM Dr. S. Jaishankar, requesting urgent intervention. Videos from at least 10 stranded Gujaratis have surfaced, showing them pleading from NGO-run safe houses in Myanmar, awaiting rescue.
A Larger Web of Exploitation
This is not an isolated case. Over the past year, Ahmedabad and Surat police have busted trafficking modules tied to Chinese syndicates. Investigations revealed that recruiters, operating from Delhi and Gujarat, charged youths ₹1.5–₹2 lakh for “placement packages” before disappearing.
In September, the CBI arrested two agents linked to a Myanmar-based network that trafficked over 500 Indians. Earlier in November, the Indian Air Force rescued 270 such victims and repatriated them from Thailand.
The Harsh Truth
Myanmar’s cyber-slavery hubs have emerged as the dark underbelly of the digital economy. The United Nations estimates that over 100,000 people are trapped across similar compounds across Southeast Asia — mostly victims of deceitful job offers.
As families in Gujarat wait for a miracle, one thing is clear: India’s growing cyber slavery crisis demands faster diplomatic and law-enforcement coordination before more youths vanish behind the screens of global scam factories.

title: Surat Police uncover man behind massive job scam: Used three companies to cheat 1,200 people & extort ₹9 cr... - Bhaskar English
article_text:

Surat Police uncover man behind massive job scam:Used three companies to cheat 1,200 people & extort ₹9 crore through fake data entry jobs
- Copy link
Surat Cyber Cell has exposed a white-collar fraudster who misused his higher education (B.Sc. Mathematics) and prestigious job as Chief Financial Officer for criminal activities. This person trapped people by luring them with simple data entry work and loans. He bought a loss-making company and used it as part of the conspiracy. This young man cheated more than 1200 innocent people and swindled over 9 crores rupees.
Monthly salary of Rs. 65,000 and 20% stake in the company
Surat Cyber Crime Cell recently uncovered a high-profile scam whose modus operandi has shocked even the police. The person who held a responsible position like Chief Financial Officer in a Pune company, with a monthly salary of Rs. 65,000 and 20% stake in the company, has cheated more than 1200 people. The mastermind behind the entire case is Nitesh Govani.
Swindled 9 crores by cheating over 1200 innocent people
Can a person who studied B.Sc. Mathematics, holds a high position like Chief Financial Officer in a prestigious Pune company, and earns a white-collar salary of Rs. 65,000 per month be a criminal? The Surat Cyber Cell has exposed a cunning fraudster who used his degree and corporate experience not for company development, but to cheat over 1200 innocent people. The number is not small - this white-collar fraudster extorted more than 9 crores from people by luring them with promises of jobs and loans.
Who is this mastermind Nitesh?
Anyone could be envious looking at Nitesh Govani's profile. He completed his BSc in Mathematics. He had a strong grasp of mathematics and numbers. With this skill, he was working as a CFO in a reputed private company in Pune. Not just the job, he had also purchased 20% shares in that company. Every month, a salary of Rs 65,000 was credited to his account. In society's eyes, he was a successful and well-educated person, but the calculations running in his mind were quite different. For him, 65 thousand was not enough, because he had the greed to earn crores in a short time.
Trapping people by luring them with data entry work This was not Nitesh's first encounter with crime. In 2021, he was arrested in Ahmedabad for cheating people in the name of data entry work. At that time, he would trap people by offering them work-from-home data entry jobs and then extort money by finding faults in their work and threatening them with legal notices. For this crime, he spent 6 months in Ahmedabad's Sabarmati Jail.
He made a new plan after coming out of jail
Usually jail reforms people, but in Nitesh's case jail proved to be a 'Crime School'. While sitting in jail, he thought about what was wrong with his previous failed trick? He realized that doing direct fraud leads to getting caught. Therefore, as soon as he came out of jail, he made a new foolproof plan - "To appear legal, but do illegal work."
Loss making company purchased in Surat
After being released from jail, Nitesh started working as a CFO in Pune, but his mind kept remembering the 20-30 lakh rupees per month he used to make from old frauds. He used his 'mathematical' intelligence to weave a complex web. He knew that subscription model was the best way to deduct money from people's accounts, but for that banks require a 1-year-old company. So he came to Surat and bought a loss-making company called Global Index from a person named Sanket Mangrola.
Company registered in Dubai found to exist only on paper upon investigation
After that, in 2024, he registered a company called Connecting All India in Dubai. This company had no existence, no infrastructure, it was only on paper. He created a third company called White Solver to collect data. This company would offer jobs to people. What was the target? Get people to download the Connecting All India app. He would pay 20 rupees for each download.
Extorting money by threatening people with legal notices
He worked as an HR consultancy through Global Index. He would get job seekers to provide 'e-signatures' and make them sign contracts. Later, under the pretext of contract breach or incomplete work, he would extort money from people by threatening them with legal notices.
Accused's masterstroke to deceive police
Nitesh was so clever that he kept all documents legal. He filed GST, IT returns on time so that no one would suspect. The biggest thing was that he had sold the Surat company Global Index on paper to a person named Satyendra Pal, so that if there was ever an investigation, his name would not appear on record.
However, in reality, Nitesh himself handled all the bank login IDs, passwords and operational control.
Brilliant math student caught in crime subtraction
When Surat Cyber Cell DCP Bishakha Jain and her team began investigating the call center racket, the face hidden behind this complex corporate structure emerged. The investigation revealed that Nitesh's plan was not just to loot money, but also to collect digital data and increase his company's valuation for bigger profits. Finally, this brilliant math student got caught in the subtraction of crime. Using his jail experience and misuse of corporate knowledge, he played games with the lives of 1200 people.
Was demanding ransom
Surat Cyber Cell DCP Bishakha Jain said that after creating his own company, he was making people download apps of other companies. He had set up a third company called Global Index Services to provide jobs in WhiteSolver, which he had purchased from Sanket.
The DCP further said that, additionally, he sold Global Index Services to a third person named Satyendra Pal this year. However, he continued to handle all the logins, passwords, and operations himself. He sold it to someone else just to keep his name off the legal records and had the documents made in their name, but he himself continued to manage everything as the director.

Gujarat man posed as RAW agent, scammed people with fake 'secret posting' jobs
The accused, who impersonated a RAW officer, lured jobseekers with "secret posting" offers and scammed them.
A Gujarat man was arrested for posing as an officer of India’s intelligence agency, the Research and Analysis Wing (RAW), and tricking people by promising them jobs. He allegedly told the jobseekers to keep the details of the employment secret as it was a “secret posting”.
The Botad Local Crime Branch (LCB) arrested a man named Mahesh Ismalia, who allegedly used a fake RAW identity card to lure people with job offers. A complaint has also been registered against Ankit Parmar, the person accused of printing the forged card.
Police said Ismalia pretended to be a RAW agent and approached people with false promises of employment. Acting on information that he was offering jobs near Nagalpur Gate in Botad city, the LCB reached the spot and caught him.
During the investigation, officers found an identity card with a defence agency logo and another card identifying him as a journalist. Police explained that no complaint had been filed against Ismalia previously as he had told jobseekers that this was a “secret posting” and that they should not reveal it to anyone, otherwise the job would be cancelled.
The Deputy Superintendent of Police in Botad made an appeal to the public and urged them to contact police if the accused has defrauded them.
Legal action has been initiated against Ismalia, and police are questioning the person who printed the fake cards. Investigators are now trying to determine how many people were cheated in the name of RAW jobs.

title: Gujarat MGNREGA mess: Jobs shrink, Rs 4.37 crore wages unpaid, corruption FIRs pile up - The New Indian Express
article_text:
AHMEDABAD: In a damning admission, the Central Government has confirmed in the Rajya Sabha that large-scale corruption has marred the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGA) in Gujarat’s Dahod district, triggering three FIRs. The disclosure comes amid a steady fall in beneficiaries, mounting wage liabilities of over Rs 4 crore, and a high-profile Rs 71 crore scam case involving the sons of a state minister.
Corruption in Gujarat’s flagship rural jobs scheme has moved from whispers to official record. On Friday, the Central Government admitted in the Rajya Sabha that MGNREGA in Dahod district is riddled with irregularities, with three separate FIRs already lodged by government officers BM Patel, SV Bambharoliya, and JG Ravat.
The revelation, made in response to a question by Congress MP Shaktisinh Gohil, comes on the back of simmering outrage over alleged embezzlement by politically connected figures. Only months ago, Balwant and Kiran Khabad, sons of Gujarat Minister Bachu Khabad, were arrested for their alleged role in siphoning off Rs 71 crore from MGNREGA funds in Devgadh Baria and Dhanpur talukas. Both are currently out on bail.
Gohil wasted no time in framing the issue as a political scandal, accusing BJP leaders and their associates of “corruption worth crores” while the state’s chief minister “threatens sarpanchs” to keep the system pliable.
"In reply to my question in the Rajya Sabha today, the central government has admitted there is massive corruption in MGNREGA in Gujarat, corruption worth crores by BJP leaders and their cronies. In Dahod alone, three government officers have been forced to file FIRs, and 10 investigation teams are already at work. Instead of acting, the Chief Minister is threatening sarpanchs, while his own ministers and bigwigs are looting crores. I demand strict action against them," said Gohil.
But the problem runs deeper than criminal charges. The same Rajya Sabha data shows a steady erosion of MGNREGA’s reach in Gujarat from 0.16 crore beneficiaries in 2022–23, to 0.15 crore in 2023–24, and just 0.13 crore in 2024–25. On top of that, as of July 28, 2025, the state is staring at Rs 4.37 crore in pending wage liabilities.
The corruption complaints are not limited to Dahod; similar allegations have surfaced in districts like Bharuch and Devgadh Baria, but Dahod now stands as the epicentre of a scandal that fuses political muscle, public money, and vanishing rural entitlements into one grim picture.

Rs 7.3 crore MGNREGA scam uncovered in Bharuch amid growing Gujarat rural job scheme crisis - The New Indian Express
article_text:
AHMEDABAD: The corruption in the implementation of the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) continues to deepen in Gujarat. Following massive irregularities unearthed in Dahod, Panchmahal, and Narmada districts, Bharuch has now been added to the list exposing yet another multi-crore scam under the Central government’s flagship employment scheme for the rural poor.
According to a police complaint filed at Bharuch A Division, a staggering Rs 7.30 crore has been siphoned off through fraudulent practices across 56 villages in the talukas of Amod, Jambusar, and Hansot. Officials say the fraud stems from collusion between contractors and government personnel.
The First Information Report (FIR), lodged at Bharuch A Division Police Station on Friday, 30 May 2025, names two firms Muralidhar Enterprise and Jalaram Enterprise accused of gross irregularities in executing clay-metal road works across 11 villages, covering projects from January 20, 2023, to the present.
Citing a technical audit, the FIR notes, “In each of the 11 villages, despite road lengths being consistent, the agencies arbitrarily segmented the roads into different parts averaging 236 metres per segment violating Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and government-prescribed criteria.”
The complaint further alleges that the contractors failed to meet material specifications. According to the FIR, “They did not use metal of the required thickness, failed to incorporate quarry spoil, and did not supply the approved construction materials. Instead, they fraudulently inflated material usage figures and generated bogus bills.”
The scale of the fraud was significant. “Knowing the bills were fabricated,” the FIR states, “Muralidhar Enterprise claimed Rs 13,05,676.51 and Jalaram Enterprise claimed Rs 6,58,898.89. Both amounts were processed and disbursed as genuine, leading to wrongful gains totalling Rs 19,64,575.40 by the contractors.”
However, the fraud was not limited to private entities alone. The FIR delivers damning accusations against government personnel, asserting a broader, premeditated conspiracy. “Although both agencies were only authorised to supply materials,” the complaint reads, “government officers, employees, and contractual staff colluded with them, bypassing MGNREGA’s e-Gram Panchayat protocols. They undertook mechanical construction of roads and submitted fake work proposals.”
The fallout, as revealed in the FIR, is massive: “This collusion led to the embezzlement of public property, submission of fraudulent proposals, misappropriation of funds, and ultimately, a loss of Rs 7.3 crore to the state exchequer across 56 villages in Bharuch taluka.”
The FIR concludes by framing the act as “a breach of trust and criminal deception against the government,” accusing all involved of orchestrating deep-rooted financial irregularities under the pretense of rural development.
The Congress party has launched a fierce attack on BJP leaders and the ruling government, directly linking them to the widening MGNREGA scam in Gujarat.
“We submitted a written plea to the TDO and DDO two years ago, but it was ignored,” said GPCC State General Secretary Sandeep Singh Mangrola. “BJP leaders are involved, so no fair probe is happening. If a real investigation takes place, it will reach Gandhinagar. We demand a SIT under judicial oversight to probe MGNREGA scams across Gujarat.”
Opposition Leader Amit Chavda first exposed a Rs 250 crore MGNREGA scam in Devgadhbaria and Dhanpur, Dahod. Subsequent probes confirmed Rs 71 crore siphoned off, implicating firms linked to Minister Bachu Khabar’s sons, both arrested. Next, Congress revealed a Rs 109 crore fraud in Jambughoda, implicating BJP-linked agencies. Then came AAP MLA Chaitar Vasava, uncovering a scam in Narmada, tied to a Congress leader from Junagadh. Now, Bharuch joins the growing list of districts tainted by the MGNREGA scam trail.

title: Ahmedabad youth duped with ₹1 lakh job offer: Held captive 33 days in Myanmar, tortured, forced into cyber ... - Bhaskar English

A youth from Ahmedabad was lured by an agent of a Vadodara visa consultancy sitting in Dubai with a promise of a 1 lakh salary and called to Bangkok. Offered salary of 1 lakh in Bangkok IT company An Ahmedabad youth wanted to go to Dubai on a work permit, so he went to Vadodara for a passport query. There, he came in contact with Kinjal Shah, who works on visas and work permits. Kinjal told the youth that instead of Dubai, go to Bangkok, where you will get a good job. My friend is in an IT company there, and through their reference, you can get a good job. After that, Kinjal Shah connected the youth with his friend Abhishek Singh. Abhishek Singh told the youth that he is in an IT company in Bangkok, Thailand. If the youth wanted to work there, the company would pay a monthly salary of 1 lakh and cover other expenses, so the youth agreed.
Chinese agent took 15 people including youth illegally to Myanmar The youth was asked to come to Bangkok from India on a tourist visa. He was told he would be given a work permit after arriving there. So the youth went to Bangkok on a tourist visa. Upon reaching there, the youth contacted Abhishek Singh. Then Abhishek Singh said to give your selfie and passport to the person I tell you to. So the youth met a Chinese person there whom he gave his passport and selfie to. This Chinese agent took the youth to a hotel 300 KM away from Thailand's border. There were 15 other people like the youth in this hotel. One person among them had escaped. The remaining 15 people including the youth were illegally taken by this Chinese person to K.K. Park in Myanmar through moving vehicles and boats.
Chinese agent demanded Rs 3.50 lakh when asked to return to India 15 people including a youth were held captive in Myanmar. If broken, he would have to pay Rs 3.50 lakh. The youth agreed to pay this money.
Chinese agent left youth back in Thailand after receiving money The youth informed his uncle about this, after which his mother transferred Rs 3.50 lakh to the scanner sent by the Chinese agent. After receiving the money, the Chinese agent illegally brought the youth back to Thailand from Myanmar. After that, the youth was left alone in Thailand and was told to go wherever he wanted. The youth then returned to India with the help of his uncle by booking a ticket.
Cyber Crime arrested Vadodara agent Kinjal in this case The youth's uncle had filed a complaint at the Cyber Crime Police Station. title: Another scam in government recruitment surfaces in Gujarat - The Hindu
article_text:
Another scam in government recruitment has surfaced in Gujarat when the State government on Tuesday ordered an inquiry into the allegations of irregularities in an online exam being held for the recruitment of engineers for the Gujarat Energy Transmission Corporation (GETCO).
The exam began on Tuesday and will continue for the next three days at many centres.
The administration was forced to order the probe after State Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) youth wing leader Yuvrajsinh Jadeja alleged that some middlemen, in connivance with some officials and a private agency which is conducting the online exam, were helping candidates by taking a huge amount of money.
Mr. Jadeja also produced a series of documents to substantiate his charges.
As soon as Mr. Jadeja’s media briefing got over, the State government announced that all allegations would be probed to ascertain the facts.
Education Minister and Cabinet spokesman Jitu Vaghani told reporters in Gandhinagar that Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel has ordered an inquiry.
“Our government believes in transparency. Nearly 35,000 young aspirants are appearing in this online exam. Our CM has ordered an inquiry into the allegations. Strict action would follow if anyone is found guilty,” he said.
As per the AAP leader, the role of a Maharashtra-headquartered firm, which has been given the contract by GETCO to conduct the recruitment test, is also under the radar.
The government has defended the agency contending that it was hired earlier for the recruitment of the railway police and also by some central PSUs.
The Minister ruled out cancelling the exam. “Let the probe bring out the truth.”
The online test, which began at 12 noon on Tuesday, is being conducted for the recruitment of 300 electrical and 53 civil engineers.
“The entire scam is being run by people based in Bayad town of Arvalli district. The candidates who have paid an advance only pretend to appear in the exam but will not answer any question. Instead, people sitting in a control room will click answers for them,” Mr. Jadeja claimed.
“This agency’s name had surfaced in a similar scam in the past. The middlemen usually charge ₹20 lakh from each candidate and take ₹1 lakh to ₹2 lakh as advance. With the help of this agency and officials, right answers are clicked from the control room on behalf of the candidates,” he alleged, explaining how the exam was being gamed.
He also named around a dozen persons who are actively involved in the malpractice.
In Gujarat, this is the second instance of serious allegations of fraud and irregularities in the government recruitment process. Last month, the State government had to cancel the exam for the recruitment of head clerks after the police had found substance about paper leak before the exam was conducted.

Surat girl reveals entire system of Dubai call center In this matter, the Surat girl stated that she went to Dubai for a job through an agent in January 2024. title: Job scam: Ex-armyman, 2 others held for duping 81 in Ahmedabad - The Times of India
article_text:
AHMEDABAD: The city crime branch on Monday arrested three persons including a retired armyman and a woman for allegedly cheating 81 aspirants of Rs 3.25 crore on the pretext of getting them government jobs. The victims belong to Gujarat,
Rajasthan and
Uttar Pradesh.
Those arrested are: Harish Prajapati, 45, the ex-armyman who ran a coaching centre named Swami Vivekanand Talim Kendra in Dehgam, his friend Pooja Thakor, 25, and Ravi Ravat, 25, owner of a coaching centre in Ajmer.
They had been allegedly cheating people by promising them jobs in the police, army, revenue department and civic bodies since 2020.
Several application forms, fake admit cards, fee receipts, passport-size photos, photocopies of original documents and certificates have been recovered from Prajapati and Thakor.
Joint commissioner of police, city crime branch, Premvir Singh, said the accused persons used fake documents and stamps to convince the candidates that they had cleared the physical test stage of the recruitment process.
"They would then demand Rs 10 lakh for the post of police sub-inspector (PSI), Rs 5 lakh each for posts of constable and talati-cum-mantri, Rs 2.5 lakh for junior clerk post, Rs 3.5 lakh for recruitment to the army, and Rs 1.5 lakh for appointment as municipal corporation clerk," he said.
"Among the 81 victims, 60 are from Rajasthan, four from Uttar Pradesh, and 17 from Gujarat. The accused would create fake domicile certificates to make the victims eligible for job openings in the state," he added.
The documents recovered from them revealed that 10 candidates were shown as having cleared the physical test for LRD (constable) recruitment even though they had not filled in any form.
Three others were shown as having cleared the physical test using a fake "pass" stamp even though they had failed the test, Singh said.
Prajapati retired as havildar in the army in 2010 and started the coaching centre to train the youth for army, police and other government jobs. Two men identified as Shahrukh Khan from Uttar Pradesh and Kulwindar Singh from Rajasthan are yet to be nabbed.
The accused have been booked for criminal breach of trust, cheating and forgery and under sections of the Information Technology Act.
From coaching class student to tutor:Pooja Thakor, 25, who hails from Mehsana, had joined Prajapati’s coaching institute in 2018 as a PSI aspirant. She trained at the institute for two years but could not crack the exam. She became good friends with Prajapati and later joined his coaching institute as a faculty member. Sources in the police said that Thakor had been coordinating with government officials to invite them to the coaching institute as visiting faculty members. A police official said that Prajapati and Thakor used to bait candidates with the promise of a permanent job in the government and take money from them.
Colonel, jawan on the run:Sources in the city crime branch said that one of the accused, Kulwindar Singh, a resident of Ajmer in Rajasthan, was posted as a colonel in the army while another accused, Sharukh Khan, is an army jawan. Prajapati, the kingpin of the scam, was in touch with Singh and Khan to lure aspirants from Rajasthan and UP. “We have traced the location of Singh and Khan and will seek sanction from the army for their arrest,” said the officer.

Ahmedabad man duped of ₹48 lakh in fake UK job visa scam by Mumbai couple

An Ahmedabad resident has complained to the city’s Crime Branch, alleging that he and his wife were defrauded of ₹48 lakh by a Mumbai-based couple who promised to secure them employment and permanent residency in the United Kingdom.
According to the FIR, the complainant, Pratik Gade (26), a resident of Shahibaug, stated that the accused, identified as Vaibhav Shinde and his wife Dhanal Shinde, residents of Mumbai, approached him in June 2023, claiming to run a visa consultancy firm named Fortune International. The couple allegedly promised to arrange five-year UK permanent residency visas, flight tickets, and jobs for Gade and his wife, Muskan, in exchange for ₹36 lakh.
Gade alleged that over several months, the couple gained the family’s trust, frequently visiting their Ahmedabad residence and maintaining regular contact. He said he transferred the money through RTGS and online banking to Fortune International’s account between June and November 2023.
Later, the complainant received what appeared to be official 'offer letters' from UK-based companies 4 Seasons Food Store and Belle Communique Ltd, along with what were purportedly genuine UK work visas. Believing the documents to be authentic, Gade and his wife travelled to London on December 22, 2024.
However, upon arrival, the couple discovered that the companies mentioned in the offer letters did not exist at the stated addresses. When confronted, Shinde allegedly assured them he would 'correct' the situation and provide new employment details. But after repeated failed attempts to contact him, the couple learnt that their visas had been revoked.
Gade stated in his complaint that UK police detained him and his wife in May 2025 after discovering that the company listed on their documents no longer had a valid licence. The two were reportedly kept in custody for two weeks before being deported to India.
Upon returning to Ahmedabad, Gade contacted an acquaintance in Mumbai who revealed that the job offer letters had been forged using details from unrelated companies. Further inquiries showed that Belle Communique Ltd had already lost its licence before the couple left India.
The complainant alleged that the Shindes had taken a total of ₹48 lakh — including an additional ₹12 lakh borrowed from his elder brother — under the pretext of visa processing and permanent residency charges. When confronted about delays, the accused allegedly demanded another ₹15 lakh, threatening to implicate the couple in false police cases if they persisted.
Based on the complaint, the Ahmedabad Crime Branch has booked Vaibhav and Dhanal Shinde under sections of cheating, criminal breach of trust, and criminal intimidation. Police officials said efforts are underway to trace the accused, who are believed to be absconding from Mumbai.
A senior official from the Crime Branch said, “Preliminary investigation suggests the couple operated a fake visa consultancy racket targeting people seeking overseas jobs. More victims may surface as the probe progresses.”

title: Vyapam rerun? How dummy candidate scam has rattled Gujarat - India Today
article_text:
Vyapam rerun? How dummy candidate scam has rattled Gujarat
Whistleblower-turned-accused AAP leader Yuvrajsinh Jadeja has been arrested in a scam that stretches from Class X boards to multiple government recruitment exams
A decade ago, national headlines were dominated by the 'Vyapam' scam in Madhya Pradesh, which was linked to several murders and other crimes. The scam was about recruitment for government jobs using dummy candidates, who appeared for entrance exams, rigging seating arrangements in examination centres and rigging answer sheets submitted in these competitive exams. While a trial in the case is pending, the investigation into the scam resulted into dozens of deaths, and arrests of senior politicians and bureaucrats, including a minister and IPS officers. Â
Cut to 2023. In neighbouring Gujarat, a similar scam has unravelled over the last fortnight by a whistleblower named Yuvrajsinh Jadeja. Nearly four dozen people have been arrested so far, including government officials, in a scam where dummy candidates appeared for competitive government exams like the Sanitation Inspector, Lok Rakkshak Dal, Forest Guard, junior clerk, etc. Â
Interrogations later revealed that the scam had been in operation since 2012. But it came to light only earlier this month when the accused were sending dummy candidates for the junior clerk exam held in mid-April in Bhavnagar. Based on a tip-off from Jadeja, the local police crime branch were able to bust the racket and arrested four people to begin with, who are accused of forging hall tickets to get entry for dummy candidates. Shockingly, some instances of dummy candidates being used to appear for students in Class X and Class XII board exams also emerged. Â
A week into the racket being busted, Jadeja himself turned into an accused. The police claimed that one of the arrested accused had revealed that Jadeja and his relatives and friends had extorted Rs 1 crore from other accused for not mentioning their names in the press conference where he made the announcement of the dummy candidate scam. Jadeja was arrested on April 21, and since then his two brothers-in-law have also been arrested with lakhs of rupees purportedly received as extortion. Â
The whistleblower and his relatives claim they have been falsely accused in the case as their revelations were getting embarrassing for the state government. Jadeja has also said that the dummy candidate racket has spread its tentacles into almost all government recruitment exams and has been operating under the auspices of several powerful political leaders. The brothers-in-law Kanbha and Shivubha have alleged that the money has been planted to show guilt for arrest, so that they don't reveal further details of the scam. Â
Who is Yuvrajsinh Jadeja?
Jadeja, 34, is a native of Gondal town near Rajkot. In 2012, he came to Gandhinagar to visit the Vibrant Gujarat Global Investors' Summit to explore a new business idea. Meanwhile, he was also helping students prepare for entrance exams for government jobs. He claimed significant success in this line of work and gained popularity as a student leader campaigning for transparency when papers for government entrance exams started leaking. He then brought to light two paper leaks of government entrance exams, following which the exams had to be cancelled, leading to significant embarrassment to the government. Â
Of late, he has emerged as an influential leader with the youth across the state, as he mirrors their anger when the papers leak and much awaited government recruitment exams are postponed indefinitely. He has garnered a massive following on social media through which he actively connects with the masses.Â
In February 2023, Jadeja revealed a dummy candidate case in Karai Police Training Academy, where a person taking training for the job was not the person who had cleared the entrance examination. It was a shocking case of impersonation. Â
In 2022, he became active with the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), which also named him as a candidate for Dehgam seat to contest the assembly election. He, however, did not contest from the seat but remained affiliated with the party. Jadeja insists his activism for action against the guilty in paper leaks and now dummy candidates scams are not being fought from a political platform. Â
Jadeja's arrest has brought the Congress and AAP together to lend support to him. Congress Gujarat chief Amit Chavda and AAP state president Isudan Gadhvi have both criticised the government for arresting Jadeja, who was the whistleblower and led to the busting of these rackets. "Jadeja was about to reveal names of senior people under whose auspices this racket was going on, so he was arrested," Gadhvi said.Â
Over the last decade, 13 question papers for entrance exams for government jobs have leaked, causing irreversible damage to hundreds of thousands of aspirants, who prepare for years for these posts. In addition to the loss of expenses incurred for preparation, these youth also lose that precious time of their life and become ineligible for these jobs owing to the age criteria. On the other hand, thousands of positions are lying vacant in various government departments, hampering government operations. Â Â
Amidst this crisis, an end doesn't seem to be in sight. But as Lok Sabha elections approach, the BJP government in Gujarat will need to set its recruitment process in order as students' frustration has been simmering for quite some time now.

title: Rs 71 crore MGNREGA scam uncovered in Gujarat; minister’s son arrested, another absconding - The New Indian Express
article_text:
AHMEDABAD: A Rs 71-crore MGNREGA scam has rocked Gujarat’s rural development system, with the arrested accused including Balwant Khabad, son of State Panchayat and Agriculture Minister Bachu Khabad.
The scam, linked to massive irregularities in the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act scheme, has surfaced in Dahod district's Dhanpur and Devgadh Baria talukas.
Confirming the arrest, Dahod Dy SP Jagdish Bhandari told local media, “Balwant Khabad and then Taluka Development Officer (TDO) Darshan Patel have been arrested in connection with the MGNREGA scam in Dhanpur and Devgadh Baria. Further investigation is underway.”
Meanwhile, the minister’s younger son, Kiran Khabad, is absconding. Police said further investigation into the multi-crore fraud is ongoing.
At the centre of the scam is a well-organised network of fictitious infrastructure projects, roads, bunds, and other public works, that existed only on paper. Funds meant for tribal employment under MGNREGA were allegedly siphoned off through forged certificates and fake invoices, with the money reportedly diverted to agencies linked to the minister’s sons.
The scandal surfaced after B M Patel, Director of the District Rural Development Agency (DRDA), flagged major irregularities in project execution in Devgadh Baria and Dhanpur talukas. An audit that followed uncovered the fraud, tracing it to Raj Construction and Raj Traders, firms run by Balwant and Kiran Khabad, both of whom had sought anticipatory bail amid mounting evidence.
Between 2021 and 2025, villages like Kuva, Redhana, and Simamoi were falsely marked as beneficiaries of completed MGNREGA projects. On the ground, there was little to no work, only forged completion reports and a trail of diverted payments. As the investigation widened, authorities uncovered that 35 material suppliers, 28 from Devgadh Baria and seven from Dhanpur, were involved in routing fake claims with the help of complicit local officials.
Senior officers allegedly turned a blind eye, allowing the fraud to fester across multiple administrative levels. In response, the District Development Officer (DDO) froze all ongoing MGNREGA payments. Audits revealed missing logs, non-existent work sites, and widespread document forgery.
An estimated Rs 160 crore in fraudulent claims remain under scrutiny. A Special Investigation Team (SIT) has been formed to dig deeper. So far, Rs 60.90 crore in fake bills have been tracked in Devgadh Baria and Rs 10.10 crore in Dhanpur. Investigators believe these numbers are only the beginning, as more talukas come under the scanner.
Leader of Opposition Amit Chavda had earlier warned of the scandal in a letter to the Chief Minister, estimating the fraud at around Rs 250 crore.
Slamming the government’s silence, Chavda alleged that the Khabad-linked firms received unchecked payments for years. “This is daylight robbery of Gujarat’s poorest,” he said, demanding the minister’s resignation and a criminal probe at the state level.
Despite the mounting pressure, Minister Bachu Khabad has remained silent, and the ruling BJP has offered no official response, drawing sharp criticism from the opposition and civil society. What began as a routine audit has exploded into one of Gujarat’s biggest welfare scams, exposing entrenched corruption and leaving public confidence in government accountability in shambles.

title: Fake job scam busted, two men, one woman arrested - Ahmedabad Mirror
Gujarat continues to see recruitment exam scams - The Hindu
article_text:
The Gujarat government has recently scrapped the written test for recruitment of head clerks following question paper leak a day before the exam on December 12.
A total of 88,000 aspirants took the exam to select 186 head clerks for the State administration.
The police have so far arrested 14 persons, including alleged mastermind Jayesh Patel, in the case that has triggered a major controversy.
Minister of State for Home Harsh Sanghavi said the paper leak case would be tried in a fast-track court to “set an example.”
Cancelled 9 times
However, the latest paper leak and malpractices in the government recruitment process are not isolated incidents in the State. In fact, since 2014, the recruitment exams for various categories have been cancelled for as many as nine times following paper leak or allegations of malpractices.
Earlier, the recruitment exams were cancelled for chief officer of municipality, teachers in government schools, clerks for district panchayats and even nurses.
‘Entire process rigged’
“Every year, in any recruitment for the State administration, question papers are leaked ahead of the exam. The entire process to recruit the government staff is rigged,” said Gujarat Congress spokesman Manish Doshi.
“In Gujarat, people linked to the RSS and BJP are appointed heads of various recruitment agencies. They are also involved in the rigging. All recruitment agencies are epicentres of corruption in the State,” Mr. Doshi alleged.
Giving the example of RSS/BJP affiliated people manning the recruitment agencies, the Congress spokesman said former Ahmedabad Mayor Asit Vora was the chairman of the Gujarat Subordinate Services Selection Board (GSSSB), which conducted the exam for head clerks in which the paper was leaked.
According to a senior bureaucrat in the State administration, in recent years, the recruitment process has been marred with controversies and allegations of corruption and rigging, which was never the case earlier.
“There is rampant corruption and rigging in the recruitment process in Gujarat and therefore the State saw violent agitations by Patidars and counter-agitation by the OBCs. Both agitations were led by youth searching for jobs,” a retired bureaucrat told The Hindu .
‘Won’t resign’
In another development, Mr. Asit Vora, after meeting the Chief Minister, ruled out resigning his post. He insisted that the process would be made fool-proof during the re-test in March next year.
In the latest case, the police investigation so far revealed that Mr. Jayesh Patel and other accused had allegedly managed to acquire the question paper from the manager of a printing press where the paper was set to be printed before the exam.
Subsequently, they allegedly sold it to over 15 candidates and helped them in solving the paper at various locations a day before the exam.
The paper then reached various candidates, who were divided into three groups and taken to three locations near an exam centre in north Gujarat on December 11 by Mr. Jayesh Patel and others to solve the question paper.
On the examination day, the accused arranged transportation to drop these candidates to their examination centres.
Notably, the issue of paper leak surfaced a day after the exam was conducted when Gujarat Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) unit’s youth wing leader Yuvrajsinh Jadeja alleged that the question paper was leaked prior to the exam. As a proof, he had shared a photograph of a notebook page having handwritten answers of some of the questions asked in the exam.
Congress leaders also brought in more evidence about paper leak, forcing the State authorities to first lodge an FIR and then scrap the exam itself.

title: WFH scam: Cops identify 456 accounts targeting people in Gujarat - The Times of India
article_text:
AHMEDABAD: The sunken job market has driven a number of seekers, across all ages, towards alternative employment opportunities. This has also led the online marketplaces getting flooded with fake 'job works' tasks and 'work from home' that promise anything from Rs 30,000 a month to anything to the tune of Rs 1.2 lakh a month.
The Gujarat state cybercell of the CID (crime) has pin-pointed that on two major online marketplaces - one running on a popular social media website - to be fishing for vulnerable job seekers.
In the past two months some 456 such cybercrook accounts have been identified by the CID, who have been fleecing victims across Gujarat by offering just packing jobs. Of these, 128 accounts have been taken off from online marketplaces by the Gujarat CID (crime).
"The online jobwork and Work From Home (WHF) job works which are quite popular now include packing pencils, chocolates and biscuits of popular brands in the country in boxes.
People don't realise that such big brands already have their automatic packing machines," says inspector cyber cell, prevention and forensics wing at CID, Manish Bhankharia. Constable Bharat Patel, who has been tracking the gangs warns that the gang seeks images of aadhaar cards and bank account details of individuals who approach them after watching their promotional videos. "They use these images to create fake credentials and based on these credentials they buy anything from sim cards or open fake bank accounts," says Patel.

title: Dummy candidate scam: Three masterminds are govt employees in Gujarat - The Times of India
article_text:
RAJKOT: Three out of the four people, who were arrested for running a dummy candidates racket in Bhavnagar since 2012, are themselves working as government employees.
On Friday, the Bhavnagar LCB had busted this massive racket and booked 36 people that included the four masterminds, dummy candidates and aspirants who got jobs without taking the competitive and departmental exams for various government posts.
The masterminds are Sharad Kumar Panot, Prakash alias PK Dave, Baldev Rathod and Pradeep Baraiya. Of these, Panot is a teacher in a government school near Bhavnagar, Dave is a block resource cluster (BRC) coordinator for a cluster of schools, and Baraiya is a clerk working in a court in Jesar town.
Interestingly, Baraiya worked as a clerk in the same court where the four were produced for remand on Saturday. They were remanded to seven days of police custody by additional senior civil judge HN Ramavat.
It's not immediately known what action the government has taken agains them after their arrest.
Police are investigating if the trio got these jobs by putting up dummy candidates or they themselves took the exams. Police told the court that the number of people who got jobs as government employees by hiring dummy candidates could be much higher and the questioning of the masterminds is required to find out their names.
Government pleader JM Chudasama submitted that some of the candidates, who passed exams using dummies are even working as bailiffs and peons in the Gujarat high court.
Among the 36 booked, two are sanitary inspectors who hired dummy candidates to pass the departmental exam and they had paid Rs 12 lakh each to Baraiya for this purpose. The four were allegedly tampering with the exam receipts and hall tickets and creating fake Aadhar cards of job aspirants willing to pay a hefty sum for hiring dummy candidates. They used to charge Rs 10 lakh to Rs 15 lakh per candidate while the person appearing as a dummy got R 25,000.
The prosecution submitted that more skeletons are likely to tumble out of the closet as the investigation proceeds and there are many people directly or indirectly involved in the racket. "It is strongly suspected that the accused are also involved in leaking exam papers and the police need to collect evidence for this," Chudasama said.
The probe till now has revealed that at least 70-80 dummy candidates were arranged and recovering the laptop used for forging documents will reveal more details. The remand application states that cops will also probe the money trail too.
