title: Gujarat: Lawyer, brother pose as IAS officers, held - The Times of India
article_text:
RAJKOT: A lawyer and his brother from Chhatisgarh were arrested for posing as IAS officers to seek VIP treatment while visiting Somnath temple in Gir Somnath district on Tuesday.
The accused were identified as practicing advocate Sharad Pande, a resident of Korba district in Chhattisgarh and his brother Ravi Pande.
According to police, Sharad called up Gir Somnath collector and sub-divisional magistrate identifying himself as a deputy secretary of law in Delhi on December 26. Sharat told the collector that a high court judge, who will soon be promoted to Supreme Court and two advocates were coming to Somnath temple. He asked the collector to make arrangements for VIP rooms, protocol officers and vehicles.
Sharad also made a similar call to the sub-divisional magistrate Saryu Zankar. However, when there was no message from Gandhinagar, Zankar got suspicious and informed the police.
On investigation, police came to know that Sharad, along with his brother Ravi and judicial magistrate first class (JMFC), Korba, Anjali Singh had come to Gujarat.
They had boarded a flight from Raipur to Ahmedabad and also asked DCM railways to arrange rooms in the railway guest house. Sharad and Ravi had visited temple town Dwarka and there too they had introduced themselves as IAS officers.
Assistant superintendent of police Gir Somnath, Om Prakash Jat, told TOI “After getting information from Dwarka police, who had found the accused to be suspicious, we booked the room for them. We also called them to inform them that all arrangements had been made as per protocol. When they came, we asked for their ID card but they refused to show it. During the interrogation, they admitted to their crime.”
Sharad and his brother Ravi were booked under IPC section 170, 419 and 114, while no case could be filed against Anjali Singh as she did not call anybody and did not show fake identification.

title: We crashed AI 171 in Ahmedabad: Lovelorn Chennai techie creates hundreds of fake email IDs, uses VPN and - The Times of India
article_text:
A 30-year-old robotics engineer from Chennai has been arrested for sending hoax bomb threats across 11 states in an attempt to frame a former colleague who reportedly did not reciprocate her feelings. The accused, Rene Joshlida created hundreds of fake email IDs, used VPNs and dark webs to stay under the radar for months. As per a police investigation, Joshilda sent fake emails, targeting schools, hospitals, and stadiums in 21 different locations. The techie also sent an email claiming responsibility behind the recent Air India clash in Ahmedabad on June 12 that killed atleast 274. Investigators across states were stumped until a single digital error helped trace the threats back to her.
Rene Joshlida: Unhappy over one-sided love
Rene Joshilda is an engineer trained in Robotics. She has been working as a senior consultant at Deloitte in Chennai since 2022. Joshilda met Divij Prabhakar during a project in Bengaluru and fell in love with him. However, the interest was not mutual. Divij did not reciprocate Rene’s feelings and got married to someone else earlier this year in February.
Enraged by the rejection, Rene Joshilda allegedly devised an elaborate revenge plan. She created several fake email accounts using variations of Divij Prabhakar’s name and began sending bomb threats to schools, hospitals, and public venues in an attempt to frame him, police investigation said.
"When they were working together, she used to create fake email accounts and harass any woman who showed any interest in her secret lover. In one case, she harassed a woman colleague suspecting her to be interested in the male colleague to the extent that she quit her job," the police said.
Claimed responsibility for Air India plane crash
The unfortunate
Air India plane crash on June 12 killed at least 274 people, including crew members, passengers and civilians on ground. Rene Joshilda, as per police, claimed fake responsibility for the crash. She sent out a hoax email to BJ Medical College administration, saying “I think now you know power. Like we sent you mail yesterday, we crashed the Air India plane with our former CM (Vijay Rupani). We know the police would have thought that the plane crash was a hoax and ignored it. Well done to our pilot. Now you know we are not playing. Now you know.”
Threatened to blow 21 spots in Ahmedabad alone
Using her technical knowledge and expertise, Rene Joshilda used fake email IDs and virtual private networks (VPNs) to send hoax bomb threats. According to Joint CP (Crime) Ahmedabad Sharad Singhal, in the emails – Joshilda threatened to blow up as many as 21 spots in and around Ahmedabad. These included the Narendra Modi stadium in Motera, the Geneva Liberal School in Sarkhej and a civil hospital, among others.
Joshilda’s fake bomb threats did not confide to Gujarat alone. As per police, she sent threat emails to 11 states, including Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Delhi, Karnataka, Kerala, Bihar, Telangana, Punjab, Madhya Pradesh, and Haryana.
How was Rene Joshilda arrested
Police say that Joshilda bought at least 80 numbers through VPN in the past two years and sent hundreds of fake emails. “The number she would use to create email IDs would be virtual. She sent threat emails through Tor browser (a network for anonymous communication) and the Dark Web. She took a lot of precautions. She was very smart and never revealed her digital trail. But she made a small mistake and our cyber crime wing and crime branch tracked her down,” Singhal told the media.
She managed to hide her identity and location using the dark web and VPNs, until one time she tipped off her location with a single error. As per an Ahmedabad Mirror report, Joshilda logged into her real and fake email accounts from the same device on one occasion. This helped police in tracing her IP address. "That one careless login gave her away," a police officer said.

title: From fake IB calls to cheating and sexual exploitation allegations: Controversies mount around AAP Vadodara president Ashok Ozha - opindia.com
article_text:
Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) Vadodara city president Ashok Ozha has found himself at the centre of multiple controversies in recent months, ranging from a fake Intelligence Bureau (IB) call scandal to allegations of cheating, criminal intimidation, and sexual exploitation. The developments have drawn significant attention in Gujarat’s political circles, particularly as some of the cases involve complaints from individuals associated with the party itself.
Fake IB call case turns against AAP’s own leader
The most politically significant controversy emerged from allegations that AAP workers and office-bearers in Gujarat were receiving threatening phone calls from individuals claiming to be officers of the Intelligence Bureau (IB). Senior AAP leaders, including Arvind Kejriwal and Durgesh Pathak, publicly raised concerns over the calls and questioned whether government agencies were being misused to target opposition workers.
The issue gained prominence after AAP leaders alleged that party workers were being contacted from a specific mobile number by a person identifying himself as an IB officer. Arvind Kejriwal himself claimed that he had called the number and that the caller disconnected after learning his identity. The episode was projected as an instance of alleged political surveillance and intimidation.
However, the police investigation took an unexpected turn. Following a complaint filed by an AAP worker in Anand, the Anand Cyber Crime Police traced the controversial phone number to a local resident, Nitin Dobariya. During questioning, Dobariya allegedly revealed that he had made the calls on the instructions of Ashok Ozha and had falsely introduced himself as an IB officer on several occasions.
According to the investigation, the alleged fake IB-call operation was linked not to any government agency but to internal factionalism within the Aam Aadmi Party. Investigators reportedly believe that the calls were part of an effort to exert pressure on certain party leaders and influence internal organisational dynamics. The development transformed what began as allegations against government agencies into a controversy involving one of AAP’s own senior office-bearers.
Notably, Ashok Ozha is considered a prominent figure within AAP’s Gujarat unit and has frequently been seen alongside top party leaders, including Arvind Kejriwal, Bhagwant Mann, Manish Sisodia, Gopal Italia, Isudan Gadhvi, and other senior functionaries.
Woman accuses Ozha of cheating her out of Rs 20 Lakh
Amid the fallout from the fake IB-call controversy, another complaint surfaced against Ashok Ozha. A woman from Vadodara submitted a written representation to the Police Commissioner, accusing Ozha of cheating, breach of trust, and criminal intimidation.
According to the complainant, she had developed family-like relations with Ozha and his wife while living in the same residential building. She alleged that Ozha offered to help her purchase a house belonging to a person residing abroad. Under the pretext of documentation procedures and related expenses, he allegedly collected approximately ₹20 lakh from her in multiple instalments.
The woman claimed that when the promised property transaction failed to materialise, and she sought the return of her money, Ozha allegedly began threatening her instead of refunding the amount. She further alleged that threats were issued regarding the kidnapping of her nine-year-old son if she continued demanding repayment.
According to the complaint, Ozha also attempted to leverage his political position and influence within the Aam Aadmi Party to pressure her. The woman additionally alleged that inappropriate demands were made when she insisted on the return of her money.
The complainant later reportedly contacted the overseas property owner directly and was informed that no money had been received on his behalf. This strengthened her suspicion that she had been defrauded, following which she approached the police.
Earlier Sexual Exploitation and Blackmail Allegations
Even before the latest cheating complaint surfaced, Ashok Ozha and his son Anand Ozha had faced serious allegations from a woman office-bearer associated with the Aam Aadmi Party.
In her complaint, the woman accused both father and son of rape, blackmail, and prolonged sexual exploitation. She alleged that Ashok Ozha initially established contact by promising to help her husband secure employment. According to the complaint, he later invited her to his residence, made her consume alcohol, and established physical relations with her while secretly recording the encounter.
The woman alleged that the video was subsequently used to blackmail her into repeated sexual relations at various hotels and other locations. She further claimed that Anand Ozha later used the same video to threaten her and sexually exploit her as well.
The complaint also alleged that when she informed Ashok Ozha’s wife about the matter, she was threatened and told to stay away. According to the complainant, pressure was also exerted through other family members.
Ashok Ozha has denied all allegations. In a written submission to the police, he claimed that he had merely provided accommodation and financial assistance to the woman on humanitarian grounds. He alleged that she was demanding ₹20 lakh in exchange for vacating the property and had threatened to implicate him in a false sexual harassment case if her demands were not met.

CBI extradites Rs 3.66 crore Gujarat fraud accused Upavan Pavan Jain from UAE - IBTimes India
article_text:
The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), with assistance from INTERPOL and law enforcement authorities in the United Arab Emirates (UAE), has successfully secured the return of Upavan Pavan Jain, a key accused in a multi-crore cheating and forgery case registered in Gujarat.
According to an official statement, Jain, who was wanted by Gujarat Police in connection with a high-value real estate fraud, was deported from Dubai and landed in India on June 20.
He arrived at Ahmedabad International Airport, marking the culmination of a months-long international operation.
The International Police Cooperation Unit (IPCU) of the CBI, in coordination with the National Central Bureau (NCB) in Abu Dhabi, tracked down Jain's location in the UAE and facilitated his return. The Red Notice subject was returned to India on June 20, following his deportation from Dubai.
Jain is accused in a case registered at Adajan Police Station in Surat, Gujarat, on the charges of criminal conspiracy, cheating by impersonation, dishonestly inducing delivery of property, and forgery of valuable security.
The CBI stated that Jain, who was working as a real estate agent at the time, hatched a criminal conspiracy with his co-accused to defraud a complainant by forging documents and impersonating property owners.
He showed the victim four different properties and persuaded him to purchase them.
Jain and his accomplices then impersonated the actual property owners using false identities and forged documents.
They also opened bank accounts in the names of genuine property owners using fake identification documents.
Through this elaborate scheme, the group succeeded in cheating the complainant out of a total sum of Rs 3,66,73,000.
Based on a request from the Gujarat Police, a Red Notice was issued against Jain by INTERPOL on March 6, 2023. After his arrest in the UAE, the Government of India formally submitted an extradition request through the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) and the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA).
Red Notices issued by INTERPOL are disseminated to all law enforcement agencies worldwide to track and apprehend wanted fugitives.
The CBI, functioning as the National Central Bureau for INTERPOL in India, works closely with domestic law enforcement through the BHARATPOL platform to utilise INTERPOL's global network.
More than 100 wanted criminals have been returned to India in the last few years through coordination via INTERPOL channels, according to the official data.

Medical assistance teams have also been stationed at centres to address any emergencies or health-related issues faced by candidates. The examination is currently underway peacefully under tight security supervision across the state.
AI-powered verification and biometric checks deployed to prevent impersonation
Authorities have introduced advanced digital security measures for this year's examination to eliminate the possibility of impersonation and the use of dummy candidates. "The ministry of education has requested the CBI to conduct a comprehensive investigation into the entire gamut of alleged irregularities, including conspiracy, cheating, impersonation, breach of trust and destruction of evidence by candidates, institutes and middlemen," a CBI spokesperson said earlier.
The role of public servants, if any, connected with the conduct of the examination and also into the entire gamut of events and the larger conspiracy will also be under the scanner, officials have said.

title: Bogus PSI held for cheating 20 women using dating apps in Ahmedabad - The Times of India
article_text:
Ahmedabad: A 27-year-old man, who allegedly posed as a sub-inspector with Gujarat Police using AI-generated photographs, forged identity cards and fabricated cybercrime credentials, was arrested by the crime branch for allegedly cheating more than 20 women through dating and matrimonial applications.
Police sources said the accused, Himanshu alias Rocky Panchal, resumed his fraud spree immediately after securing bail last year in a rape and impersonation case registered in Maharashtra and is suspected to have cheated at least 15 women thereafter.
Crime Branch officials said Panchal, a Class X dropout from Udaipur, had been living in the Sabarmati area of the city. He never held a regular job and allegedly survived entirely on the money he extracted from women he emotionally manipulated through dating and matrimonial websites.
He allegedly projected himself as a PSI posted with the cybersecurity wing of the crime branch and used AI-generated images of himself in a khaki uniform to establish credibility.
Police recovered a mobile phone, Rs 40,000 cash, forged identity cards bearing the words “Govt of India” and “Crime Branch cybersecurity”, Gujarat Police logos, police belts, badges and Ashoka emblem stickers from his possession. Officials said he used AI, digital signature tools, and online stamp-making applications to create forged documents and letterheads that resembled official police stationery.
According to police, Panchal first built trust among his targets through conversations and carefully curated social media profiles. He allegedly convinced several women that he was facing legal troubles, departmental inquiries or urgent official expenses and sought money under various pretexts.
In one case, a Naroda woman allegedly gave him nearly Rs 1.8 lakh and even allowed him to use her bank account and sim card after he promised marriage. Another woman from Navrangpura allegedly transferred Rs 79,700 after he claimed he needed money for the house that was being constructed.
Police said Panchal’s first known offence dates to 2019, when a woman from the city accused him of impersonation and cheating.
Since 2023, he has allegedly refined his methods using AI-assisted conversations and fabricated police credentials. In 2024, a woman from Virar in Maharashtra lodged a rape and impersonation complaint against him, after which he spent nearly three months in jail before securing bail.
“He resumed targeting women almost immediately after his release. Many victims may still not have approached police due to fear of stigma and social scrutiny,” a senior officer said. Women from Ahmedabad, Kheda, Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh were among those allegedly targeted, police said.
Mother ‘aware’ of his activitiesCrime Branch officials suspect Panchal’s mother was aware of his fraudulent activities and may have actively helped sustain the deception. Officers said several women, including one from Naroda, had visited the family and discussed marriage proposals, believing Panchal was a police official.
“His mother behaved as though she were searching for a suitable bride for her PSI son. At no point did she indicate that he was lying about his profession,” a senior officer said. Police are now examining whether she knowingly facilitated his wrongdoing.
Swagger first, sympathy laterPolice said Panchal projected himself as a confident, stylish police officer in photographs uploaded on dating and social media platforms. Once a woman got comfortable speaking to him, he shifted to portraying himself as a troubled officer burdened by legal disputes, financial stress or departmental issues. Police said he frequently claimed that court cases or inquiries had exhausted his savings and sought financial assistance from his targets.
In one instance, he reportedly met a woman’s father and convinced him that he had been falsely implicated in an Income Tax case but had emerged “clean”.
Police recovered forged letterheads bearing the names of senior police officials and Income Tax authorities, which he allegedly used to strengthen his claims.
From cybercrime accused to ‘PSI’Police said Panchal’s familiarity with cybercrime investigations may have ironically helped him impersonate law enforcement more convincingly. After being questioned in the 2019 impersonation case, he became fascinated by how cybercrime units operate. Over time, he allegedly began presenting himself as an officer attached to the crime branch cybersecurity. “He realized that most civilians would hesitate to question someone claiming to be from cybercrime or intelligence units. He exploited that psychological advantage,” an officer said.
Lived as ‘future son-in-law’ with Kheda familyIn one of the more unusual episodes uncovered during the investigation, Panchal allegedly stayed with a family in the village of Dabhan in Kheda district for nearly two months after convincing them that he intended to marry their daughter.
Police said Panchal and his mother approached the family seeking temporary accommodation after claiming they were facing housing difficulties. His soft-spoken manner and convincing communication reportedly earned the family’s trust quickly, and he began living with them almost as a member of the household.
“He behaved respectfully, participated in family activities and projected himself as a responsible police officer preparing for marriage,” a police official said. Over time, villagers noticed discrepancies in his personal story and employment profile.
As suspicions grew and the family became uncomfortable with gossip surrounding the arrangement, Panchal quietly left the village. Police believe the episode reflects the extent to which he embedded himself into victims’ personal lives before exploiting them.

title: India’s Gujarat State Passes New Anti-Conversion Law - International Christian Concern
article_text:
India’s Gujarat State Passes New Anti-Conversion Law
BJP-Led Government Tightens Restrictions on Religious Conversions
04/06/2021 Washington D.C. (International Christian Concern) – International Christian Concern (ICC) learned that the Bharathiya Janatha Party (BJP) led government of Gujarat has passed a new law regulating religious conversions and criminalizing forced religious conversions. The new law amends the Gujarat Freedom of Religion Act 2003 and has been championed by local BJP politicians as the state’s ‘Love Jihad’ law.
On April 1, the anti-conversion law, entitled the Gujarat Freedom of Religion Act 2021, was passed by Gujarat’s Legislative Assembly. The new law has amended Gujarat’s original anti-conversion law by criminalizing marriages done for the sole purpose of religious conversions and defining fraudulent allurements as promises of a better lifestyle, divine blessings, or impersonation.
According to the law, individuals seeking to change their religion will need to apply to the district administration 60 days in advance. Religious leaders facilitating religious conversions will also need to inform the district administration 60 days in advance. If the previsions of the law are not followed, violators could face a sentence of three to five years in jail and a financial penalty of 50,000 rupees.
The law also criminalizes forceful religious conversions with a jail term of three to ten years and fine of 500,000 rupees. The law specifically criminalized marriages done solely for the purpose of religious conversion and expanded the definition of what is considered illegal allurement when identifying forced religious conversions.
“Gujarat has done it once again,” Father Cedric Parkash, a human right activist, told local media. “The additional amendments to the already draconian law of 2003 enhanced its unconstitutionality. Such an unconstitutional law should be withdrawn immediately.”
Radical Hindu nationalists use the specter of mass religious conversions to Christianity and Islam as justification to pass similar laws limiting religious freedom. According to these nationalists, Indian Christians and Muslims are accused of converting poor Hindus to Christianity and Islam in mass by fraudulent means.
In regards to Christianity, India’s own population data does not support this conspiracy. In 1951, the first census after independence, Christians made up 2.3% of India’s population. According to the 2011 census, the most recent census data available, Christians still make up 2.3% of the population.
In states where similar anti-conversion laws are currently enacted, including Odisha, Uttar Pradesh, Arunachal Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand, Himachal Pradesh, and Uttarakhand, they are widely abused. Radical nationalists falsely accuse Christians of forcefully converting individuals to Christianity to justify harassment and assault. Local police often overlook violence perpetrated against Christians due to false accusations of forced conversion.
To date, no individual has been convicted of forced conversions in India. This is in spite of the fact that some of the anti-conversion laws have been on the books since 1967.
William Stark, ICC’s Regional Manager, said, “We here at International Christian Concern are deeply disappointed to see Gujarat pass this expanded anti-conversion law. Similar laws are widely abused by radical Hindu nationalists due to their legal ambiguity. Ultimately, anti-conversion laws provide legal cover for radical nationalists to attack India’s Christians and Muslims with impunity. One simply needs to claim someone was engaged in forceful conversions to justify an assault. With the expanded definition of allurement, it is hard to see how one could share their faith without risking legal consequences. With attacks on Indian Christians and other minorities continuing to escalate, the passage of another anti-conversion ordinance will only incite more religiously motivated violence.”

title: Gujarat: Railway job aspirant removes thumb skin and puts it on proxy candidate's hand in a bid to pass t - The Times of India
article_text:
VADODARA: In a desperate attempt to secure a railway job, a candidate allegedly removed his thumb skin and pasted it on his friend's thumb so that the latter could clear biometric verification and sit for the recruitment exam here in his place, police said.
But the crude attempt to trick the biometric machine was exposed when the transferred piece of skin fell off, an official said on Thursday.
The candidate and the 'proxy', both hailing from Bihar, have been arrested.
A senior doctor said they would have never been able to pull off the trickery even if the transferred piece of skin had stuck on.
On Wednesday, city police arrested candidate Manish Kumar and his friend Rajyaguru Gupta, both natives of Munger district in Bihar, for alleged cheating, said additional commissioner of police S M Varotariya.
Both are in their mid-20s and have cleared Class 12 exam, he said.
A private company authorised by the railways conducted a recruitment test for 'D' group vacancies in Laxmipura area here on August 22 for which more than 600 candidates appeared, the police official said.
"To prevent cheating (through impersonation), all the candidates were required to give their thumb impression which was matched with their Aadhaar data through a biometric device," said Varotariya.
When a candidate who identified himself as Manish Kumar gave his thumb impression, verification failed despite repeated attempts, he said.
The exam supervisor grew suspicious when he noticed that the candidate was trying to hide his left hand by putting it in the pocket of his pants.
"When the supervisor sprayed sanitiser on his left thumb, the skin pasted on it came off," the police official said.
After questioning him and finding out that his real name was Rajyaguru Gupta, a case was registered under Indian Penal Code sections 465 (forgery), 419 (cheating by impersonation) and 120-B (criminal conspiracy) against him and Kumar. Gupta told police that as he was good in studies, Kumar came up with the idea of sending Gupta to take the railway test in his place.
"A day before the test, Kumar put his left thumb on a hot cooking pan which created a blister. He then removed the skin using a blade and pasted it on Gupta's left thumb as he knew that there would be biometric verification before the test," the police officer said.
An Ahmedabad-based doctor said such 'transfer' of fingerprint skin will never work.
"The skin and ridges on the fingerprint are made up of protein. When a blister is formed due to excessive burning, these ridges get defaced. So even if someone tries to paste such piece of skin on another person's thumb, the biometric machine will never recognise it as the skin would have lost its original structure," said Dr Rajnish Patel, additional superintendent at the Ahmedabad civil hospital.

title: Now, Rs 31 lakh cheating plaint filed against Kiran Patel in Gujarat - The Times of India

title: Fake PMO official booked in three cases in Gujarat - The Times of India
article_text:
A day after a conman from Ahmedabad was arrested for posing as a top official of the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), it has come to light that this isn’t the first time he duped people and the government machinery in the name of the PM.
He has allegedly duped several people of Rs 3. 25 crore according to three cheating cases registered in Gujarat, s aid police. Patel was arrested on his third ‘VVIP’ visit to Jammu and Kashmir. He passed himself off as an additional director (strategy and campaigns) in the PMO each time. The Gujarat Police said he has been visiting the valley “for review of development projects” since 2015.
“Kiran Patel visited various areas in Jammu and Kashmir allegedly to monitor development projects like the Pir Pan jal tunnel project and redevelopment of Lal Chowk in Srinagar. He also claimed to have been tasked by the PMO to instil confidence in the people of Kashmir and to motivate them to believe in the Union government,” said a police officer close to the investigation.
The Gujarat Police also suspect him of having visited four other states – Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Delhi and Uttar Pradesh – posing as a bureaucrat. Kiran Patel, a resident of Ghodasar, runs Modified Concept Private Limited, an audit firm on CG Road in Navrangpura area of Ahmedabad.
The first case against him was filed in Naroda of Ahmedabad in 2017. Later, a complaint was filed in Aravalli’s Bayad area and another in Vadodara’s Raopura area in August 2019.
On February 23, 2017, a DJ from Naroda named Rahul Parmar filed a complaint of cheating, breach of trust, and criminal conspiracy against Patel and four of his family members for allegedly duping him of Rs 1 crore by taking 16 cars from him and failing to return them. The second complaint was filed by Paritosh Shah, a businessman from Paldi in Ahmeda bad. He alleged that Patel and his two aides engaged him to install lights and other decorations for a garba event at Navlakhi ground in Vadodara but failed to pay Rs 1 crore. A schoolteacher named Ashish Patel from Radodara village in Bayad filed a complaint of cheating against Kiran Patel and his three family members on August 22, 2019. Ashish told police the a ccused lured him by promising hefty profit if he invested in their tobacco and cattle-feed business. He paid them a total of Rs1. 25 crore between April 1, 2014, and May 19, 2016, but did not get any returns.
Attended meetings held for BJP workersKiran Patel usually attended meetings for BJP workers. He was seen roaming around Kamalam, the BJP’s headquarters in Koba, the CMO, and the secretariat to establish his links with bigwigs in the government and the saffron party. A party leader claimed that Patel had taken Rs 25 lakh from him. Patel held a precursor for an international event hosted in the state. He also shared his family members’ pictures with several senior BJP leaders. He floated a group named after PM Narendra Modi and charged registration fees from those who wanted to join the group.
Conman sent to judicial custodyOn Friday, a Srinagar court remanded Kiran Patel to judicial custody for 15 days. Patel had been arrested from The Lalit hotel in Srinagar on March 3, following a tipoff by Jammu and Kashmir CID. At least 10 fake visiting cards and two mobile phones were seized from him.
The details of his con act became public after he was produced in court on Thursday. According to police sources, there were three more persons accompanying Patel, but they managed to escape.
Patel was taken to Nishat police station, where an FIR was registered for cheating, forgery and impersonation. A team led by SP, east Srinagar, is investigating the case.
Impersonating a high-ranking PMO official, Patel moved around in a bulletproof vehicle with Z-plus security, enjoyed five-star st ay, and threatened bureaucrats and cops with transfers during several trips to Jammu and Kashmir, before his cover was blown up.
Gave ‘updates’ on development projects in KashmirIn a bid to project himself as an officer of the PMO, Kiran Patel gave important updates and reviewed various development projects in the Kashmir Valley. In certain posts, he gave updates about the renovation of Lal Chowk in Srinagar and announced that Srinagar would be developed as a smart city.
He also gave updates about the Pir Panjal tunnel work and stressed how the government is serious about the development of Kashmir. Apart from Kashmir, he also shared various government notifications and photographs purportedly showing the new building of the Parliament under the Central Vista project.
Holds fake PhD degree from the USPosting a photograph of his certificate, Kiran Patel, in February this year, announced he had been awarded a doctorate from a university in Virginia, US.
He claimed he had been awarded a PhD for his “Projecting Human as Brand” thesis. Apart from this, he also claimed in several social media posts that he had been honoured with a PhD from a university in the Kingdom of Tonga, a Polynesian country. His other posts show he had got an engineering degree from LD Engineering College and then did his MBA from the Indian Institute of Management, Tiruchirappalli. Gujarat police officers said he did not have any of the degrees he claimed on social media.
Paldi resident was Patel’s first victimComplaint 1
Kiran Patel’s alleged first victim was Paritosh Shah, a Paldi resident who runs an event management company. Kiran and his aides — a couple from the Satellite area — allegedly duped him of Rs 1 crore.
Shah, who lives in Sparsh Aspire, told police, “Kiran Patel and his aides — Dipesh and Dhara Sheth from Sanjay Tower near Shyamal Crossroads — first gained his confidence by awarding him a sub-contract of two Gujarat government contracts. They gave me a lighting and decorating contract at the Statue of Unity in Kevadia. They also gave me contracts for different government krushi mahotsavs for which I received timely payments. ”
Later, in September 2018, Patel and the Sheths asked Shah to provide lighting and decoration for a garba event at Navlakhi ground in Vadodara. Since he did not face payment issues for the SoU and krushi mahostav events, Shah decided to work for them as a sub-contractor during the Navratri festival from October 10 to October 18, 2018.
“They gave me Rs 20 lakh in instalments. However, despite several requests, they did not give me the remaining Rs 1 crore,” he told police.
When Shah asked Patel for the money, the latter allegedly threatened him. “Patel said he had connections in Delhi. He threatened to abduct and kill me if I ever sought money again,” Shah told police.
The Raopura police of Vadod ara then filed a complaint of breach of trust, cheating, criminal intimidation, using abusive words and abetment against Patel and the Sheths.
Kiran Patel first posed as PMO official in 2017Complaint 2
The first record of Kiran Patel posing as an official at the Prime Minister’s Office was in 2017 when he and his family members conned a retired PSI’s son of Rs 1 crore. He invoked the PMO’s powers to evade legal action.
Rahul Parmar, a resident of Naroda whose father Mitha Parmar had retired as a sub-inspector from Vatva police, filed a complaint of cheating aga inst Kiran, his brother and other family members.
He said Kiran’s brother Manish and other family members convinced him to join their business of renting cars to the Vadtal Swaminarayan temple.
Parmar said he and his friends gave Manish 16 cars worth Rs 1 crore in January and February 2017, following which Manish an d his family members wentincommunicado.
Later, Kiran assured Parmar that he would return the cars or the money. “Kiran said he was a youth wing leader of the BJP and had connections to politicians in 20 states. He claimed he was a Class 1 officer with
the PMO and managed its social media accounts. Kiran also gave me his phone number, allegedly allotted by the Guj arat government,” Parmar told police. Interestingly, the phone number was from a series used only by the state’s senior ministers, IPS and IAS officers.
Parmar said Kiran claimed to know senior bureaucrats personally and boasted that he would be given a ticket for the Daskroi assembly seat.
Govt teacher in Bayad cheated of Rs 1.25 croreComplaint 3
A resident of Bayad in Aravalli had on August 22, 2017 filed a complaint of cheating against Kiran Patel, his brother Manish Patel, wife Darshana Patel and their maternal uncle Vitthal Patel for cheating him of Rs 1. 25 crore by luring him with a “profitable” business. Ashish Patel, a resident of Radodara village in Bayad, was teaching in a government primary school in Shivpura village i n Kapadwanj taluka of Kheda when he met Vitthal.
Ashish said that Vitthal told him that his nephew Jagdish ran a business of tobacco and cattle-feed trading in Anand. Vitthal told Ashish that he would get g ood returns if he invested in the business.
Convinced by Vitthal, a retired bank employee, Ashish gave money to Manish and his wife Darshana as and when they asked for it. In 2015-16, Ashish ended up pay ing Rs 1. 75 crore for which Kiran was a guarantor.
Later, Kiran’s family members returned Rs 50 lakh to Ashish and whenever he demanded the rest of the money, they refused. Ashish alleged that Kiran had given an advertisement in a newspaper saying that he did not have any relation with Manish and Darshana so that he is not held liable.
Ashish then filed a complaint of che ating, breach of trust and criminal conspiracy against Kiran, Manish, Darshana and Vitthal.

title: CBI takes charge of NEET-UG malpractice cases from Gujarat, Rajasthan, and Bihar - Mint
article_text:
NEET-UG Exam 2024 row: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has taken over investigation into five new cases of alleged malpractices in the NEET-UG medical entrance exam, previously under police scrutiny in Gujarat, Rajasthan, and Bihar. Officials confirmed that the central agency has re-registered one case each from Gujarat and Bihar, along with three cases from Rajasthan, as its own FIR. Additionally, there are plans to take up another case from Maharashtra's Latur.
These cases primarily involve instances of impersonation and cheating by local officials, invigilators, and candidates, except for the Bihar case, officials noted. The CBI's involvement follows a directive from the Union education ministry to conduct a comprehensive probe into the matter.
With these new cases, the CBI is now handling a total of six investigations related to alleged irregularities in NEET-UG. The exam, conducted by the National Testing Agency (NTA), is critical for admissions to MBBS, BDS, AYUSH, and other medical courses across India. Held on May 5 at 4,750 centers in 571 cities (including 14 abroad), the test saw participation from over 23 lakh candidates.
The decision to transfer the probe to the CBI came after widespread protests by students across various cities, prompting the education ministry to intervene. The ministry's request to the CBI specifies a thorough investigation into potential offenses like conspiracy, cheating, impersonation, breach of trust, and evidence tampering involving candidates, institutes, and intermediaries.
CBI officials have indicated that the scope of the investigation will extend to scrutinizing the roles of public servants associated with exam conduct, as well as examining the broader chain of events and possible conspiracies.
Opposition MPs said on the first day of the 18th Lok Sabha that the government will have to answer on the controversy in Parliament.
Several newly-elected members who took oath in the Lok Sabha on Monday said the government is not considering the hardship of students who are feeling stuck in limbo.
As Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan proceeded to take his oath, members of the opposition raised "NEET, NEET" slogans, as the controversy over alleged irregularities in competitive exams, including the medical entrance exam National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test Undergraduate (NEET-UG) and the the University Grants Commission–National Eligibility Test (UGC-NET) continues to rage.

title: Gujarat: SOS from father-in-law exposed fake policeman - The Times of India
article_text:
AHMEDABAD: When Kanu Patel was detained recently, he called his son-in-law, a cop, to bail him out of trouble — but Patel was shocked to learn that his saviour was a mere pretender. The police team at the scene had quickly determined that Patel’s son-in-law, Jagatsinh Bihola, was a fake cop. For Patel, that knowledge had dawned after five years.
On Friday, the full extent of Bihola’s deception became clear to police.
He had not only fooled his father-in-law with his uniform but had also drawn daily salutes from his neighbour, a crime branch constable.
B R Bhati, the sub-inspector investigating the case, said that Bihola had crafted a series of stories about himself. To some, Bihola would identify himself as a sub-inspector with an armed unit. To others, he would say that he was a sub-inspector under suspension. Bhati said it appears that Patel was not aware of Bihola’s impersonation. title: Driver switched, identity faked, affidavit forged: Fresh FIR filed in fatal hit and run in Kheda Gujarat - The Times of India
article_text:
Ahmedabad: A road accident that claimed the life of a highway patrol worker in Kheda has now morphed into a full-blown criminal investigation. What began as a hit-and-run incident on March 23 took a dramatic turn after police discovered a web of impersonation and forgery. Multiple individuals stand accused of conspiring to shield the identity of the real truck driver. Authorities are now searching for the actual driver, Deepak Rajput, who remains missing.
The incident dates back to March 23, 2025, when 28-year-old Sagar Chauhan, deployed on highway patrol duty, was putting up safety barricades near a broken-down SUV close to Modaj overbridge on the Ahmedabad-Vadodara expressway. A speeding truck rammed into him, causing severe head injuries that led to his death during treatment.
The SUV's driver, Yogesh Deshpande, sustained injuries in the crash while the truck driver fled the scene. Mahemdavad police then registered an FIR against an unknown driver based on the complaint by the victim's relative, Kuldeepsinh Chauhan.
In the days that followed, the truck's owner, Jabbar Gagan from Surat, appeared before police on April 4.
"He named Sultan Ayub Diwan as the driver and submitted an affidavit and a photocopy of Sultan's driving licence, although the photo was unclear. Sultan himself also appeared and handed in a notarised affidavit affirming he was behind the wheel during the accident," revealed police.
But the story soon began to unravel.
As the investigation progressed, pushed by insurance company officials seeking clarification, suspicions grew. "A new twist emerged when the transport manager, Hardik Rana, from Ahmedabad revealed that the actual driver on the day of the accident was not Sultan, but one Deepak Rajput, a native of Bihar, who had been hired to drive the truck from Ahmedabad to Surat with a goods consignment," said police.
Further inquiry allegedly exposed an elaborate cover-up. "Instead of reporting Deepak as the driver, Gagan allegedly approached his associate, Rafik Malek, who then arranged for a man named Sarfaraz Malek to pose as Sultan. Sarfaraz submitted a fake affidavit and falsely identified himself as the driver of the truck during police proceedings," said police.
Mahemdavad police filed a fresh FIR on Tuesday and booked the truck owner, Jabbar Gagan, Sarfaraz Malek (who impersonated Sultan), Rafik Malek (who facilitated the arrangement), and Salim Malek (who acted as a witness) under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita Sections (BNS) related to criminal conspiracy, impersonation, forgery, and misleading investigation. Officials said: "All four acted in concert to mislead the police, suppress the identity of the actual driver, Deepak Rajput, and obstruct justice in a fatal crash."
A fresh probe is ongoing. The real driver is yet to be located.

title: Gujarat Assembly Passes Love Jihad Bill Penalising Fraudulent Religious Conversion By Marriage - ABP News
article_text:
Gujarat Assembly Passes 'Love Jihad' Bill Penalising Fraudulent Religious Conversion By Marriage
The amendment seeks to prohibit and punish religious conversion promising a better lifestyle, divine blessings, and impersonation on the pretext of marriage. The Bill was tabled in the state assembly by Legislative Affairs Minister Pradeepsinh Jadeja.
Gandhinagar: Following suit with Uttar Pardesh, the Gujarat Government passed a bill to amend the 'Dharma Swatantrya' (Freedom of Religion) Act, 2003 which aims to combat forceful religious conversions, better known as `Love Jihad`, on the concluding day of the ongoing Budget session on Thursday.
Tabled by the ruling BJP, the amendment seeks to prohibit and punish religious conversion promising a better lifestyle, divine blessings, and impersonation on the pretext of marriage. The Bill was tabled in the state assembly by Legislative Affairs Minister Pradeepsinh Jadeja.
The Gujarat Freedom of Religion Act, 2003 sought to deal with religious conversion through allurement, force or by misrepresentation, or by any other fraudulent means. However, the state government felt that there were episodes of religious conversion promising a better lifestyle, divine blessings, and impersonation.
The Bill witnessed a massive uproar in the house from the opposition and a Congress leader Imran Khedawala even tore the copy of the Bill.
Speaking about the provisions of the amendment Bill, Khedawala said, "Home Minister Pradeepsinh Jadeja has only mentioned that the daughters of the Hindu community are targeted by men from a specific community. Daughters, be it from any religious community, will always be our daughters. I too have over hundred testimonies of Muslim girls marrying into other religion. I am deeply hurt by the words of the minister".
The Speaker of the House, Rajendra Trivedi, interrupted Khedawala but he continued speaking.
"Nobody can force anybody to marry into a specific religion and in no religion, it is written to forcibly convert anyone to accept that. In this Bill, only one community is specifically targeted with words like 'Jihadi'. I opposite this Bill and I'm tearing down its copy," Khedawala said as he tore the copy of the Bill which he had in his hand.
This was followed by an uproar from BJP members in the House.
BJP-ruled Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh recently enacted similar laws banning `fraudulent' conversions through marriage.
What does the Bill against 'Love Jihad' Say?
As per the amendment, a forcible "conversion by marriage, or by getting a person married, or by aiding a person to get married" shall invite imprisonment of three to five years and a fine of up to Rs 2 lakh.
If the victim is a minor, woman, Dalit or tribal, the offender may be punished with a jail term of four to seven years and a fine of not less than Rs 3 lakh.
If an organisation violates the law, the person in charge can be sentenced to a minimum of three years and a maximum of ten years in jail. A fine of upto Rs 5 lakh can also be imposed in such cases.
The amendment also provides that a marriage solemnised for the purpose of unlawful conversion shall be declared void by a court.
The burden of proving innocence shall lie on the accused person.
Any aggrieved person, his/her parents, siblings, or any other person related by blood, marriage or adoption may lodge an FIR under the law.
The offences under the Act will be cognisable and non-bailable and shall not be investigated by an officer below the rank of a Deputy Superintendent of Police.
The amendment also defines "allurement" as promising "better lifestyle, divine blessings, or otherwise".
The BJP government had said it was necessary to prohibit "forcible conversion by marriage" and hence section 3 of the Act needed to be amended.

title: Shock and disbelief in Gujarat as idol seller slapped with Rs 20 cr I-T notice - The New Indian Express

AHMEDABAD: A shocking incident has come to light in Gujarat’s Dakor town, where a poor idol seller Chirag Jagdish Bhaiya has been slapped with an income tax notice of nearly Rs 19.84 crore, which could be a case of possible misuse of his identity credentials or plain administrative failure. Ironically, the small-time vendor struggles to earn Rs 200 a day.
Chirag sells idols made of plastic and fiber in Dakor’s Gomati Ghat area. He got a surprise when he received a letter through registered post from the Income Tax Department at his rented accommodation. It contained a notice which stated that transactions worth Rs 19.84 crore have been recorded in his name. It showed that transactions worth Rs 11.86 crore took place in 2021-22, followed by another Rs 7.98 crore in 2022–23.
The notice Chirag received from the department bore postage stamp worth Rs 5,500, which could very well match Chirag’s monthly earnings. Chirag said, “I make small idols and earn just Rs 100 to Rs 200 a day. If I cannot run my house properly, how will I hire a lawyer to reply to the IT department?”
Chirag was compelled to seek counsel of his neighbours to understand the implication of the notice. They were surprised to see that a small-time vendor with no assets, no stable income and no financial footprints ended up with crores of rupees worth of transactions in his name. They cautioned him about the possibility of identity theft where his documents could have been misused or a technical glitch within the system of the I-T Department.
Chirag is yet to hear from the I-T authorities in this matter.

title: Love marriage? Gujarat govt to alert parents via WhatsApp - The New Indian Express
article_text:
AHMEDABAD: Gujarat plans to tighten marriage registration rules: parents to be alerted via WhatsApp for love marriages, 40-day certification window proposed, and stricter identity, witness and notary checks introduced to boost transparency and prevent fraud.
In a move that blends administrative reform with social signalling, the Gujarat government has initiated amendments to the Gujarat Registration of Marriages Rules, triggering a sharp political and social debate over privacy, parental consent and safeguards against identity fraud.
The proposal, announced in the Gujarat Legislative Assembly, seeks public objections and suggestions first, before finalising a framework designed to make the marriage registration process “transparent, secure and legally robust”.
At the core of the proposed overhaul lies a controversial provision: once a couple applies for a love marriage registration, the girl’s parents will automatically receive the submitted details through WhatsApp, while the marriage certificate would be issued on the 40th day after application.
The government argues this delay window creates a verification buffer to detect coercion, misrepresentation or forged identity claims. Defending the move with hard language, Home Minister Harsh Sanghvi told the House, “We are not against love. But if someone becomes ‘Salim Suresh’ to trap a daughter with a fake identity, the state will not allow such deceit to succeed.”
He asserted that genuine couples with parental approval would face no hurdles, but those hiding identities would be subjected to strict scrutiny.
Linking safety with process reform, Sanghvi said notary validation must now occur in the presence of all concerned parties, warning of “strict action” if documentation is executed in absentia.
The proposed system also mandates full disclosure of witnesses’ identities, photographs and Aadhaar copies, while court-based government registration would become compulsory to prevent manipulation through informal channels.
Crucially, the government plans a dedicated online portal where every application becomes digitally trackable; the moment a registration request is filed, parents would receive real-time details shared by their Children. The administration insists the amendments are not moral policing but a calibrated legal shield one that seeks to balance personal choice with protection against fraud, coercion and identity deception in marriage registrations across the state.

title: Gujarat HC seeks government response on AI and deepfake: Advocate General says, 'Platforms ignore takedown ... - Bhaskar English

Gujarat HC seeks government response on AI and deepfake:Advocate General says, 'Platforms ignore takedown requests'
- Copy link
Applicant Vikas V. Nair from Ahmedabad has filed a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) before the Gujarat High Court through advocate Amit Panchal, raising concerns over artificial intelligence (AI) and deepfake content.
The matter was heard today before the Chief Justice’s Bench. It was submitted that AI-generated and deepfake videos and photographs of constitutional office-holders are being created on a large scale. Such content, it was argued, undermines their position and prestige and erodes public trust in institutions. The petitioner contended that the State Government should frame specific rules under the Information Technology Act to address the issue. These rules, it was suggested, could be notified through official gazettes and government notifications.
Government’s powers under the IT Act
The Advocate General informed the court that, in cases involving AI-generated fake videos, the concerned authority must notify media platforms to secure their removal. However, when such content is uploaded using fake identities, identifying the perpetrators becomes difficult.
Reference was made to Section 69A of the IT Act, which empowers authorities to block public access to content in specified circumstances. Typically, directions may be issued to platform providers to block material relating to national security, international relations, public order, and similar concerns. It was stated that both the Central and State Governments have rule-making powers under the IT Act.
HC flags identity theft and harmful content
The applicant informed the court that the State Cyber Department had responded via email, stating that action would be taken upon receiving complaints of this nature.
The High Court observed that individuals are often portrayed negatively through manipulated photographs and videos. Content harmful to children and humanity has become widely accessible on social media platforms. The court noted that identities are being stolen, privacy is violated, and obscene or sexually explicit material is created and circulated online.
It was further highlighted that, even after instructions are issued, platform providers may take up to 36 hours to remove objectionable material.
Concerns over platform accountability
The Advocate General stated that China has implemented stringent regulations governing platform providers in relation to AI and deepfake content. However, he added that when removal requests are made to certain platforms, they do not always respond promptly.
The High Court remarked that platform providers sometimes fail to act decisively when objections are raised. Controversial posts often continue to attract engagement and ‘likes’, and as a result, are not removed from platforms despite complaints.
Live-streaming rules and viral court videos
The issue of videos related to the High Court’s live-streaming rules was also discussed. Despite copyright protections under the Gujarat High Court’s live-streaming framework, its proceedings are circulated widely on social media. Even after being notified, platforms do not consistently remove such content.
The petitioner further stated that numerous fake videos and images continue to be generated, making effective control difficult. He argued that such material can only be curtailed through real-time takedown mechanisms. In one instance, he claimed that an AI-generated trial court judgment, which did not exist in reality, had been presented before him.
The Gujarat High Court has sought a response from the government on the petition and scheduled further proceedings for 20 March. Following the government’s reply, responses may also be sought from the concerned platform providers.

title: Gujarat-Origin Businessman Convicted In US Immigration Fraud Case - Vibes Of India
article_text:
A federal investigation into immigration violations in the United States has exposed a web of unlawful employment, financial support and marriage fraud involving two men originally from Gujarat, culminating in convictions and prison sentences.
At the centre of the case is Rajesh Patel, 51, a businessman based in Ronceverte, West Virginia, who has been handed three years of federal probation along with a $10,000 fine.
According to media reports, prosecutors said Patel knowingly ignored US immigration and labour laws by employing an undocumented worker for nearly four years and actively helping him remain in the country.
The sentence was announced by federal authorities in Beckley on January 9 as part of a larger nationwide enforcement drive.
Media reports further said that the court filings show Patel employed Aakash Makwana, 30, a Gujarat native, at his Fairlea-based business from November 2020 through at least September 2024. Makwana had overstayed his visa, a fact Patel admitted he was fully aware of, yet the employment continued without interruption.
Investigators revealed that the relationship went far beyond that of employer and employee. Patel allegedly became a key support system for Makwana, providing daily transport due to his lack of a vehicle, paying for his accommodation, and supplying food.
To avoid detection, Makwana was paid in cash, and no payroll taxes were reported, effectively keeping his employment hidden from authorities.
The arrangement came under scrutiny only after Makwana was arrested in a separate federal probe into immigration fraud. On October 8, 2025, he was sentenced to two years in prison after admitting to aggravated identity theft. Federal officials said Makwana attempted to secure permanent residency by entering into a fraudulent marriage with a US citizen.
According to court records, the marriage was supported by forged documents and false claims, including a fabricated allegation of domestic violence aimed at strengthening Makwana’s green card application. The scheme unravelled during a federal investigation, leading to multiple convictions. Once he completes his prison term, Makwana is expected to be placed in deportation proceedings.
Patel also acknowledged in court that he was aware of the fake marriage arrangement and assisted in the conspiracy by making cash payments to others involved. His wife, Avani Patel, 44, has pleaded guilty to unlawfully employing an undocumented immigrant and is scheduled to be sentenced on January 13.
Others tied to the case have already faced punishment. Kaleo Ann Huff of Illinois, who married Makwana as part of the fraud, received five years of federal probation for perjury and marriage fraud. Her brother-in-law, Joseph Sanchez, who helped organise the arrangement, was also sentenced to five years of probation.
Federal agencies including Homeland Security Investigations and US Citizenship and Immigration Services conducted the probe under the Department of Justice’s “Operation Take Back America,” a programme targeting immigration-related offences across the country.
The case highlights a recurring pattern involving illegal migration from Gujarat to the United States. Over the years, US authorities have uncovered numerous instances of individuals overstaying visas, using forged identities or entering into sham marriages to regularise their status. Some migrants also undertake perilous journeys through multiple countries in Latin America, often paying exorbitant sums to human traffickers.
While Gujaratis form one of the most successful and law-abiding Indian diaspora communities in the US, law enforcement agencies say a growing number of fraud and immigration-related cases linked to illegal entry or overstays have triggered intensified monitoring. Officials warn that such violations not only carry severe legal consequences but also place migrants and their families at significant personal and financial risk.

Hotel guests in Gujarat will soon no longer need to submit photocopies of their Aadhaar cards during check-in. Instead, a secure digital check-in system—similar to digital payments—will allow guests to verify their identity by scanning a QR code and completing face authentication.
This move is expected to reduce paperwork, prevent misuse of personal identity documents, and streamline hotel check-ins across the state.

New Aadhaar app launched to strengthen privacy and security
Currently, Aadhaar cards are commonly used as identity proof at hotels and other places. However, physical copies can be misused if they fall into the wrong hands. To address this concern, the government is gradually shifting towards secure digital verification.
On January 28, 2026, the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI), which manages Aadhaar, launched a new Aadhaar mobile application in Delhi. The Ahmedabad Crime Branch was invited to participate in this launch.
Notably, the Ahmedabad Crime Branch has become the first government agency in the country to receive approval to integrate its Pathik software with the Aadhaar system.
Ahmedabad Crime Branch gets nationwide first approval
The Pathik application has been operational since 2017 and is used to record and monitor data of hotel guests. Until now, guest identity details were manually collected and uploaded to the Pathik system.
With the new integration, the entire process will become fully digital, ensuring better security and protecting user privacy. Sensitive identity information will no longer need to be physically shared or stored.
How the digital check-in system will work
The process will function similarly to UPI payments. When a hotel allots a room, a unique QR code will be generated for the guest.
The guest will scan this QR code using the Aadhaar app on their mobile phone. The app will then perform face authentication to verify the guest’s identity. Once verified, the guest’s authenticated details will be securely shared with the Pathik system and the hotel.
This eliminates the need to submit photocopies or physical ID documents.
The system will also help hotel operators ensure that guests are genuine and not using fake identities, while protecting guests from identity theft or misuse of their personal documents.
Rooms cannot be booked with fake documents PSI Dilip Thakor told Divya Bhaskar that the idea of linking with Aadhaar was from UIDAI. They had approached us for this. They said that we are launching an Aadhaar application which verifies concern-based users. If you add it to your Pathik software, hotel guests can be digitally verified. This will help eliminate problems like booking rooms using fake documents.
Hotels will get many benefits from this. Earlier, guest documents were collected at hotels. They had to be preserved, sometimes got misplaced, could be misused, and multiple accounts could be created. Now these types of crimes will be prevented.
Last 4 digits of Aadhaar will also not be visible Hotels will only be able to see the guest’s name, photograph and address. The Aadhaar number itself will remain completely hidden. Until now, the last four digits of the Aadhaar number were visible, but under the new system, not even a single digit will be shown. Aadhaar will simply verify whether the name and address provided by the guest are genuine. The Pathik platform will act as the secure medium for this verification.
Privacy law made digital verification necessary In 2023, India’s privacy law came into force, mandating that physical identity documents should not be collected and user privacy must be protected. However, due to the absence of a reliable alternative system, hotels continued collecting physical copies. This created a dilemma—without ID records, it became difficult to identify or track criminals who might use fake identities to stay in hotels and commit crimes. The digital system resolves this gap by enabling secure verification without collecting physical documents.
Digital verification will be done with user consent Ahmedabad Crime Branch PSI Dilip Thakor said the new system ensures full compliance with privacy laws. Guests will not be required to submit physical documents. Instead, their identity will be digitally verified through the Aadhaar app with their consent. Since verification happens directly through the official platform, it protects privacy while ensuring accuracy. This will make hotel check-ins faster, fully digital and error-free.
Stronger monitoring ahead of major international events With Ahmedabad set to host large-scale events such as the Commonwealth Games and major cricket matches, lakhs of visitors are expected. This system will prevent criminals from using fake identities to secure accommodation, significantly strengthening security and monitoring.
Aadhaar will digitally verify guest identity Thakor explained that Ahmedabad alone has thousands of hotels, PG accommodations and registered homestays. Criminals have often exploited fake identities and disappeared without leaving records. The new Aadhaar-based verification closes these loopholes. It confirms a person’s identity digitally, reducing dependence on manual checks and preventing misuse of forged or edited documents.
System can be extended to PGs, guest houses and homestays The Crime Branch has already integrated this system into the Pathik platform. It can now be expanded to cover PGs, guest houses, homestays, dharamshalas and other temporary accommodations. In the future, integration with DigiLocker and driving licence databases may also allow verification through additional government identity records.
Designed to prevent crime and misuse of fake documents The main objective of this system is to prevent criminals and anti-social elements from using fake identities. Since the Crime Branch is a government agency, digital verification through official platforms ensures both security and privacy compliance.
UIDAI selected Pathik as a model privacy-compliant platform The Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI), which manages Aadhaar, was looking for secure real-world applications for its newly launched Aadhaar app. Pathik was selected because it allows Aadhaar integration while fully protecting user privacy.
Ahmedabad Crime Branch stood alongside global tech giants During UIDAI Day celebrations on January 28, 2026, in Delhi, the Ahmedabad Crime Branch was invited to present its integration work. Alongside major technology companies such as Google, Samsung and DigiLocker, the Crime Branch demonstrated how Pathik could securely connect with Aadhaar for guest verification.
Separate verification system for foreign citizens For foreign nationals, passport and visa details are scanned and uploaded to the government portal, and a C-Form is submitted for central verification. This ensures authorities have accurate records of international visitors and their accommodation details.
Pathik system already covers thousands of hotels in Gujarat The Pathik platform was launched in Ahmedabad in 2017 and expanded across Gujarat in 2019 after its success. Currently, around 9,500 hotels are registered on the platform, and nearly 1.5 lakh guests check into hotels daily. With Aadhaar integration, the system will become even more secure while maintaining complete privacy protection.
POC (Proof of Consent) is obtained after completing all privacy compliances. This includes issues like how user privacy is maintained and so on. Only after this can such services be used. The Crime Branch has completed all these compliances.
What about someone who doesn't use a smartphone? In response to this question, they said that this system is only for technology-driven people. "What can we do if people don't use technology at all? said officials.

title: Gujarat techie steals company data, launches rival firm while working from home; booked under BNS, IT Act - The Times of India
article_text:
RAJKOT: Work-from-home might have helped IT companies save on overhead expenses, but in Jamnagar, it nearly cost a software company its business. A seasoned software engineer used the comfort of working from home as an excuse not just to steal sensitive company data but also to quietly launch a competing company.
On the complaint lodged by Rajesh Bhimani, proprietor of SNTG IT Services Pvt Ltd, the cybercrime police arrested Manish Bharadwa, an IT engineer with 10 years of industry experience. The investigation revealed that Bharadwa, a trusted employee of Bhimani, launched the company in connivance with the firm's former staffer. They registered the firm in the names of their wives.
Investigators said Bhimani's company developed special software to enable deaf people to do banking. The company also has an office in Ahmedabad with around 40 employees. Six months ago, Bhimani requested a work-from-home option, citing personal reasons and plans to relocate to Vadodara. Trusting his long service, the company allowed the request and provided him with a system containing sensitive data, including customer records spanning 10 years, proprietary software source codes, and design formulas.
However, Bhimani soon noticed irregularities in Bharadwa's work.
An internal probe revealed that he established a rival company, offering the same services as SNTG. When asked for an explanation via email about the status of the company-issued computer, including its location and any unauthorised access or data transfers, Bharadwa appeared at the Jamnagar office the next day. He returned the system without undergoing proper handover protocols or allowing the company's IT team to examine it on the spot.
Upon inspection, company engineers discovered that an external device was used on the system and sensitive data was copied. Further investigation revealed Bharadwa allegedly set up a proxy server, raising concerns of continued misuse. Inspector I A Ghasura of the Jamnagar cybercrime police said, "The complainant feared that Bharadwa could mentally or financially harm customers and damage the company's interests using stolen data."
Explaining the modus operandi, officials said, "Source code is like the blueprint of a customized software and mostly an intellectual property. Along with the data, the accused secretly copied the software's source code onto an external device. This is a serious cybersecurity fraud."
Bharadwa was booked under section 316(6) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) for criminal breach of trust, along with relevant sections of the Information Technology Act.

title: 'He was living illegally for the past 12 years': Man from Gujarat gets 12 years in US jail for scamming e - The Times of India
article_text:
AHMEDABAD: A Gujarati man living illegally in the US for 12 years was sentenced to 12 years in federal prison for his role in a fraud scheme that targeted elderly people in Illinois, Indiana and Wisconsin.
The punishment was announced by the US Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Illinois on Tuesday.
The 44-year-old man who hails from North Gujarat, was convicted in Feb by a federal jury.
The charges included one count of conspiracy to commit wire and mail fraud, three counts of wire fraud, and one count of illegal entry into the US, the officials said.
"This illegal alien admitted that he came to Illinois because the state would give him a driver's licence, and then he used that licence to steal from the elderly all across the Midwest," said US attorney Steven D Weinhoeft.
The fraud was carried out as an imposter scam. Victims received texts or emails saying their Amazon accounts were compromised.
When they responded, they were connected to fraudsters pretending to be federal agents.
The victims were told to withdraw their savings for protection against supposed identity theft and deposit the funds into fake US govt accounts.
In reality, the money was stolen and sent to accounts in India controlled by the scammers, the officials said.
The accused worked as a courier, personally collecting cash, gold, and other assets from the victims. According to trial evidence, he once picked up $177,000 worth of gold bars from an elderly woman using a walker and oxygen at her assisted living facility.
"These scams need people on the ground in the US in order to be successful, and those willing to help them should receive stiff sentences," the court said during sentencing.
The accused had entered the US illegally near Vancouver. He later connected with the fraud group in Georgia and moved to Chicago. There, he obtained a driver's licence illegally and travelled through Illinois, Wisconsin and Indiana to collect money on behalf of the network.
"This case highlights the serious public safety risks posed by individuals who enter the US illegally and exploit our systems to target some of the most vulnerable among us," said Matthew Scarpino, ICE Homeland Security Investigations Chicago special agent in charge.
The federal trade commission reported in March 2025 that imposter scams are now the most common type of consumer fraud in the US.

title: Gujarati Couple Charged With Employing Undocumented Worker, Aiding Fraud - Vibes Of India
article_text:
In Fairlea, West Virginia, an Indian man overstayed his visa. Not just that, he worked for nearly four years at a local business centre. All this while living under the radar. His undocumented status was no secret to the couple who hired him—Rajesh and Avani Patel. Not only did they employ him, but they also housed him, paid his rent, and personally drove him around.
Rajesh N Patel, 51, and Avani Patel, 44, have now pleaded guilty to federal charges related to aiding and employing Aakash Prakash Makwana, a 30-year-old Indian national. According to the US Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of West Virginia, Rajesh Patel admitted to knowingly transporting an illegal alien, while Avani Patel pleaded guilty to the unlawful employment of aliens.
Court records reveal that between November 2020 and September 2024, the Patels employed Makwana at their business in Greenbrier County. “The Patels admitted that they agreed to hire Makwana knowing that he was living in the United States illegally after his immigration visa expired,” prosecutors were quoted as saying.
Rajesh Patel went beyond offering him a job. He confessed to regularly driving Makwana to work and other destinations, as Makwana did not own a vehicle. He also admitted to covering Makwana’s rent, supplying groceries, and failing to collect or remit payroll taxes on his wages.
Makwana had previously pleaded guilty on May 14, 2025, to aggravated identity theft in connection with a fraudulent marriage scheme. Prosecutors stated, “In or around August 2021, Makwana conspired with others to marry a US citizen so he could apply for lawful permanent residence status.”
The plan reportedly failed, and Makwana is set to be sentenced on September 26. Rajesh Patel admitted to being aware of the sham marriage and even supporting it financially by making cash payments to co-conspirators.
As part of the same conspiracy, Illinois resident Kalee Ann Huff admitted to marrying Makwana and was sentenced in June to five years of federal probation. Her brother-in-law, Joseph Sanchez, who helped arrange the marriage, also received probation.
Reports added that Rajesh Patel will be sentenced on January 9 and faces up to five years in prison and a $250,000 (approximately Rs 2.2 crore) fine. Avani Patel’s sentencing is scheduled for January 5, with a maximum penalty of six months in prison and a $3,000 (approximately Rs 2.65 lakh) fine.

title: Stolen phones harder to hide as Gujarat Police step up digital tracking - The New Indian Express
article_text:
AHMEDABAD: In a significant crackdown on mobile theft networks, Gujarat has climbed to third place nationwide in recovering stolen mobile phones. Over the past year, police in the state have traced and returned 53,564 devices, achieving a recovery rate of 46.71%. This is well above the national average of 32.6%, highlighting a marked improvement in both efficiency and coordination.
At the heart of this success is a technology-driven approach. Working closely with the Department of Telecommunications, Gujarat Police has been using the Sanchar Saathi portal along with the Central Equipment Identity Register (CEIR) system. These tools enable authorities to track and block stolen devices across telecom networks using their unique IMEI numbers, effectively turning each handset into a traceable digital asset.
The scale of enforcement is equally notable. While more than 50 lakh mobile phones have been blocked across India so far, Gujarat alone accounts for 1,83,985 of those devices. However, officials point out that blocking is only part of the process—the real challenge lies in recovery.
District-level performance has played a key role in this achievement. Ahmedabad City led the effort with a strong recovery performance, followed by Dang district, which stood out for its high accuracy despite handling fewer cases. Bhavnagar also contributed significantly, maintaining consistent results.
The efforts of officers on the ground have not gone unrecognised. At a recent ceremony, State Police Chief K. L. N. Rao honoured nodal officers from top-performing districts, acknowledging their role in strengthening investigation, coordination, and execution.
Beyond the statistics, officials say the broader impact is clear. Recovering stolen phones not only returns property to citizens but also disrupts illegal resale networks and reduces the risk of cybercrime linked to stolen devices.
With recovery rates improving and systems becoming more robust, Gujarat’s approach signals a shift in how mobile theft is being addressed—no longer as a minor offence, but as a trackable and increasingly solvable crime.
