title: Gujarat’s roll call for electors is on: Here’s how to make sure you keep your right to vote during Specia - The Times of India
article_text:
Want to make sure your vote counts? You may want to start by checking your name and details in the voter list. The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) 2025 of the electoral roll — a house-to-house exercise to verify, update, and clean up the voter list — has begun across the state. Booth0level officers (BLOs) are already on the move, distributing enumeration forms and collecting updated information from voters.
Here's everything you need to know about the process.
What is an enumeration form?
The enumeration form is an official document used to create or update the list of eligible voters. The ongoing SIR uses the 2002 voter list as a reference point. About 5 crore forms are being prepared. Each voter will receive two copies: one to keep (with a stamped acknowledgement) and one for the Election Commission's records.
What is an EPIC number?
The EPIC number is a 10-digit unique voter identification number printed on every voter's ID card
How do I get an enumeration form?
BLOs will visit homes between Nov 4 and Dec 4 to deliver pre-filled enumeration forms and assist with any queries. If a house is locked, the form may be left with neighbours or society office-bearers.
If residents have shifted, the BLO will take back the forms. The BLOs are also responsible for collecting the enumeration form.
What will the BLO do?
BLOs will distribute and collect forms, guide voters, and verify information on the spot. They'll countersign your form, keep one copy for records, and return the stamped copy to you.
How to fill in the form?
The form will have pre-filled details such as your name, EPIC number, address, constituency, part number, serial number, and photo. You must verify these details and add your date of birth, mobile number, and parents' or spouse's name, and attach a photograph. Remember: signature on both forms are necessary. Unsigned forms may lead to deletion of your name from the roll.
What happens after submission of physical forms?
The BLO will countersign, keep one copy for ECI records, and return the second copy to you with a stamped acknowledgement. Keep this safely.
The details will be verified on the spot either by the BLO or subsequently by an official. The authorities may ask applicants to show or upload identification, proof of address, and proof of age etc. Registering voters might also be required to re-submit their details.
What if I live outside Gujarat or abroad?
If you are away for studies or work, a family member can fill and submit your form to the BLO. Or, you can fill the form online.
What if my previous address no longer exists due to redevelopment or demolition?
Go to the ECI website, click on 'search your name in the voter's list' tab. Once your details are filled in, go to the search results and click on 'View Details' link. It will take you to the page that lists the names and phone numbers of the ERO and BLO. You can call them for a solution.
You can also book a call with the BLO by clicking on the tab provided on the ECI portal. You will need to enter your EPIC number and captcha code for the same.
How do I fill the form online?
Log onto the Election Commission's official website, https://voters.eci.gov.in/ or use the ECINET app.
On the portal, select your state, and search using your EPIC number. The enumeration form will appear on the screen.
You need to link your mobile number with the EPIC card to fill in the form. The website has an option for the process.
The first section of the form will already have some pre-printed information. Download the form and verify the details against the current voter ID card
Once verified, fill the remaining sections of the form, put an e-signature on it before submitting online.
What needs to be considered while filling form online?
Voters must enter details such as name, address, constituency, part number, and serial number if their name appeared in the 2002 list. If not, the new form allows users to fill in fresh details in the same step-by-step manner as the offline version.
Aadhaar authentication will be mandatory. An OTP will be sent to the mobile number linked to the elector's Aadhaar number. The form will be submitted after you enter this OTP. Post-submission, you will get the option of downloading and printing a copy of the completed form.
NOTE: Your name must match the one mentioned on your Aadhaar card
What happens after online submission?
The applicant will receive an acknowledgement number. Use "Track Application Status" feature in the services column to monitor the progress of your application until the final decision is made.
What if I am a new voter?
The SIR primarily focuses on verifying existing voters. If you have turned 18 or are registering for the first time, fill Form 6 online or request a physical copy from your BLO. Aadhaar authentication is required for the online process.
What if my name is missing from the voter list?
Submit Form 6 online or through your BLO during the SIR process to add your name.
What happens next?
Following the verification process, authorities will publish a draft electoral roll. Check this to see if your name is on the list and if your details are correct. If not, the period for filing ‘claims and objections' online or offline is crucial. This will be your final opportunity to ensure your details are accurate before the final electoral roll is published.
Use Form 6 if your name is missing to ensure inclusion on electoral rolls. Use Form 8 for correction of particulars, e,g, wrongly spelt name, address, or age, entered in the electoral roll. You can use Form 7 to object to proposed inclusion or if you seek deletion of name from the roll.
—-————————
Key dates for SIR 2025
Nov 4 -Dec 4:House-to-house enumeration
Dec 9:Draft electoral roll publication
Dec 9-Jan 8: Claims and objections period
Dec 9-Jan 31:Hearing and verification (notice phase) of claims and objections
Feb 7:Final electoral roll publication
Eligibility criteria
Must be a citizen of India
Must be 18 years or older
Must be a resident of the area
Must not be disqualified under any law

title: Gujarat HC directs police to investigate fertility centre after man alleges child born through IVF is not his - The Indian Express
article_text:
Gujarat HC directs police to investigate fertility centre after man alleges child born through IVF is not his
The newborn’s hospitalisation and subsequent blood tests revealed that her blood group did not match either of the two parents
A Vadodara-based man ended up knocking on the doors of the Gujarat High Court seeking directions for Vadodara city police to initiate criminal action against a prominent fertility centre after his newborn’s hospitalisation and subsequent blood tests led to a paternity test that revealed that the petitioner is not the biological father of the baby.The Gujarat High court on Wednesday directed city police to “look into” his complaint and apprise about the outcome within four weeks.
The man moved the court, after Vadodara city police allegedly failed to register his complaint. Based on his plea, the HC on Wedenesday issued the directive to the city police. The man in his plea sought a criminal complaint against a fertility centre for alleged “cheating and forgery” after the DNA test confirmed that he was not the biological father of the IVF baby that he welcomed with his wife in April this year.
Advocate MB Gohil, representing the petitioners, told The Indian Express, “The couple had approached a prominent IVF franchise centre in Vadodara. They were assured that a lawful and ethical process would be followed. Initially, they tested the sperm samples of the husband and advised some fertility treatment to him. Thereafter, another sample was taken and he was found to be fertile. Then they told the couple to deposit a sum of Rs 5.5 lakh as they could undergo IVF…”
Gohil added that the hospital conducted the Intrauterine Insemination (IUI) procedure on his wife and she was successfully impregnated. “We have mentioned in the petition that it was in March 2024 that the petitioner’s semen was cryopreserved (freezed) and the wife underwent an egg retrieval procedure in April 2024. Thereafter, they processed the cryopreservation of five embryos and conducted the first IVF cycle in June 2024. The pregnancy was confirmed in September 2024.”
It was when the newborn was hospitalised for severe health issues after her birth in April 2025 that a medical report revealed that her blood group did not match either of the two parents. Gohil said, “While both parents have O positive blood group, the baby has a B positive blood group, which created a doubt in the mind of the petitioner. When he underwent a paternity test, the DNA did not match. Thus, it was proven that the petitioner is not the biological father of the child and the centre has cheated the couple by inseminating the wife’s fertile eggs with sperm of another person.”
Gohil added that the petitioner decided to move the High Court as the Vadodara city police did not register his complaint until the plea was filed.
Gohil said, “The petitioner had approached one police station in Vadodara city, which directed him to another police station. There, he visited multiple times and was made to wait but no complaint was taken. Exasperated, he moved a petition before the HC on June 10. On June 21, after learning about the petition, the Vadodara police issued the first summon to the petitioner to record his statement but there has been no update on the case,” Gohil said.
The lawyer added that a representative of the IVF center, who initially claimed in her police statement that she was “only an employee” had also filed an affidavit in the HC as a joining party and claimed to represent the IVF centre.
Gohil said, “We argued that the case in the HC was against the Vadodara city police, seeking directions for criminal action. The representative of the IVF centre has no locus in the case as they are not respondents in the petition… The court has accepted the argument and directed the Vadodara police to file an update in four weeks, failing which, we are at liberty to move a fresh petition.”
In an oral order on Wednesday, Justice HD Suthar of the Gujarat High Court directed the police to “look into the matter and inform about the outcome of the same, preferably in four weeks.” The court also said that it had “not gone into the merits of the case” and granted liberty to approach “the appropriate forum against any adverse direction passed by the police authority”.

title: Gujarat HC upholds Gujarat HC' decision cancelling Student's Result for Fake Mark-Sheets | SCC Blog - SCC Online
article_text:
Gujarat High Court: In a civil application filed by a student (‘petitioner’) against the decision of the Veer Narmad South Gujarat University (‘Respondent’) (hereinafter ‘University’) for cancelling the entire result of LLB Examination for all semesters of the petitioner, the Single Judge Bench of Nikhil S. Kariel, J., dismissed the petition and upheld the decision of the University.
Factual Background
In the matter at hand, the present petitioner had taken admission into LLB Course at the University and submitted his statement of grades of Graduation from Shridhar University, Pilani, Rajasthan. On 11-06-2015, the University had given eligibility certificate to pursue the LLB Course at D.D. Law College, Navsari. Subsequently, the University found that the certificates of Shridhar University which the petitioner had submitted for getting admission in the LLB Course were fake, therefore the entire LLB Course result of the petitioner was set aside.
Court’s Decision
The Court was of the considered opinion that the petitioner was attempting to take advantage of his own wrong. The Court also said that the submission on behalf of the petitioner that since the University while giving admission could not detect the fraud perpetrated by the petitioner, therefore at a later stage, the University ought not to be permitted to rectify their mistake was absurd. The Court added that the petitioner himself was guilty of submitting fraudulent documents and whereas in case, the fraudulent documents were verified by the University at first and treated as genuine documents, the benefit was ultimately been taken by the petitioner himself. The Court also stated that the University would not in any manner be liable for not detecting the fraud perpetrated by the petitioner and on the other hand the petitioner could not be permitted to take advantage of fraud in the first place.
The Court also perused the Section 47 of the Veer Narmad South Gujarat University Act, and said that protection under the said Section was available only in case where the student concerned, was facing withdrawal of degree or diploma on the ground of being convicted by a Court of law of any offence which in the opinion of the Syndicate or the Senate, is a serious offence involving moral turpitude or if he has been guilty of scandalous conduct. It was the considered opinion of the Court that such protection is given in order to ensure that every conviction does not automatically result in a student having his degree or diploma being revoked by the University. Therefore, the Court said that such protection would not be applicable in the case of a student like the present petitioner, who had got admission in the LLB Course by perpetrating a fraud.
Further, the Court said that before any adverse action is taken against any person by the State, or its instrumentalities, it is envisaged that such organization would adhere to the principle of natural justice, but in the present case, more particularly where the petitioner had not submitted any document from the University in question i.e., Shridhar University certifying that the petitioner had studied with the University and the mark lists were in fact genuine, then the purpose of giving an opportunity of hearing would be nothing but an empty formality, more particularly when the Shridhar University had already informed the University about the fraudulent nature of the mark-sheets submitted by the petitioner.
Thus, the Court dismissed the petition for lack of merits.
[Mehul Sureshkumar Champaneria v. Veer Narmad South Gujarat University Through the Secretary, 2023 SCC OnLine Guj 2175, Decided on 03-07-2023]

For the petitioner: Advocate NK Majmudar;
For the Respondent: Advocate Bhagirath N Patel.

title: 486 fake property cards made in Gujarat, 3 officials booked - The Times of India
article_text:
SURAT: The CID (crime) Surat unit lodged an FIR against three govt officers and partners of the reportedly fake real estate firm Samruddhi Corporation for allegedly making 486 bogus property cards of farmers to usurp their land parcels in Dumas, Gavier, and Vanta villages adjoining the city and developing a plotting scheme there.
The police booked deputy director KP Gamit, superintendent AD Patel, and a data entry operator of the City Survey Superintendent office on the complaint lodged by Azad Ramoliya (47), who owns a factory in Ankleshwar and is also engaged in farming.
Ramoliya alleged that the govt officers and promoters of Samruddhi Corporation connived to make 135 bogus property cards of his six plots in Dumas and one in Vanta village, and 351 of other plots between 2017 and 2022. He claimed that he made several applications of complaint to various authorities, including the district collector, but no offence was registered until now. He alleged that the names of farmers were entered in the 7/12 extract, and the plots were sold as farmhouses in the scheme named ‘Silent Zone.'
Investigation officer PB Sanghani told TOI: "We have booked three govt officials and partners of Samruddhi Corporation for cheating, forgery, and criminal conspiracy under IPC. We have started collecting evidence against the accused, but no arrests have been made yet."
Ramoliya told police that he bought the six plots during 2016 and 2017 from Rasik Lallubhai, a farmer in Magdalla. The names of Ramoliya and his family members were entered in the 7/12 extract of all the parcels. In 2022, a land broker came to him with a property card for plot number 803 to sell the land. As the land belonged to him, he checked various govt records and found that many property cards were registered on land parcels owned by him and his family members.
Ramoliya claimed he approached the collectorate, municipal commissioner, prant officer, mamlatdar, DILR, among others, on Aug 17, 2022. He claimed he submitted an application for complaint to the detection of crime branch (DCB) on July 23, but it was closed without any action on Aug 2 last year.
Ramoliya then sent a complaint to the office of the additional director general of police, CID Crime, Gandhinagar on June 24.
In his complaint, Ramoliya said neither he nor his family members applied for property cards online or offline, but 135 such cards were issued to various plot holders on the six land parcels. He also alleged that apart from him, 351 more cards were issued on land parcels of other farmers in Dumas, Gavier, and Vanta villages.
"In 2022, I applied to the district collector's office to cancel all the property cards, but no action was taken," he alleged.
Ramoliya alleged that separate lands were merged and sold as plots to several buyers by ‘Samruddhi Corporation' using fake power of attorneys.

title: Two beneficiaries of PMJAY die after angioplasty at private hospital in Ahmedabad - The Indian Express
article_text:
Two beneficiaries of PMJAY die after angioplasty at private hospital in Ahmedabad
Villagers vandalise hospital premises, allege consent for surgery not taken from kin; Gujarat government orders probe
Picked up from their village a day after a health check-up camp, two men from Mehsana district died at a private hospital in Ahmedabad following angioplasty procedures on Monday, police said.
Following the deaths, groups of relatives and neighbours of the deceased gathered on the premises of the Khyati Multispeciality Hospital on the SG highway on Tuesday morning and allegedly vandalised it.
The Gujarat government directed the anti-fraud unit of the Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PMJAY) to investigate the deaths of the two residents of Borisana village. The hospital is empanelled under the Central government scheme.
The Gujarat Medical Council (GMC) has also begun an investigation in the case.
The relatives of the deceased alleged the hospital authorities had conducted angiography on a number of people and carried out angioplasty surgeries on at least seven of them without the consent from their families.
The deceased persons have been identified as Mahesh Barot, 52, and Nagar Moti Senma, 75.
On Sunday, the hospital conducted a free health camp in Borisana village of Kadi Taluka in Mehsana district, about 35 km from Ahmedabad city.
Villagers gathered outside the hospital told The Indian Express that around 80 people had attended the camp. On Monday morning, a vehicle from the hospital arrived at the village and asked around 19 villagers, all of whom are said to be beneficiaries under the PMJAY, to board the vehicle and brought them to the hospital, they said.
“There was no communication until 10.30pm when they informed us that Maheshbhai had died. We were told only later that there had been complications after his angioplasty, which was carried out without the consent of our family,” said Kalpesh, a cousin of Barot, who is survived by a brother and four sisters. He was unmarried.
Bharat, one of the two sons of Senma, said, “We will not accept my father’s body unless they give us proper answers. They are still not telling us anything except that he died after an angioplasty surgery during which they installed stents. The man was fit enough to walk to the medical camp and now he is dead.” Bharat’s brother Praveen could be seen seated on the floor outside the hospital, still in shock at his father’s sudden death.
According to the PMJAY dashboard, Khyati Multispeciality Hospital is empanelled in the national health insurance scheme for MC (Cardiology), SU (Urology), and SV (Cardio-thoracic and Vascular surgery).
Meanwhile, the Ahmedabad City Police secured the hospital premises while a team of government doctors from Ahmedabad Civil Hospital were dispatched to check on the status of other patients, at least five of whom remained in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU).
Speaking on the alleged vandalism, Tushar Patel, the Chairman of Kadi Taluka Panchayat, told The Indian Express, “The families as well as the villagers were angry that the surgeries were conducted on their loved ones without securing consent from them. It appears that the hospital had just taken the thumb prints from the patients on the consent document. Even when we reached the hospital, nobody could be found. The women then went inside and some amount of damage was caused in their very justified grief and anger… We managed to stop them and bring them back out.”
Gujarat Health Minister Rushikesh Patel, who is also an MLA from Mehsana’s Visnagar seat, posted on X, “The alleged incident at Khyati Hospital is very serious. I have ordered an immediate inquiry by the State Anti-Fraud Unit (SAFU) of PMJAY. If there is any substance to the allegations or evidence of medical negligence, severe action will be taken against the hospital and the doctors involved.”
Patel, who is campaigning in Maharashtra for the Assembly elections, is expected to visit the hospital on Wednesday. Former Deputy CM and Health minister Nitin Patel, who is also the former MLA from Kadi constituency, reached the hospital in the afternoon and spoke to doctors and police officers present there.
Traffic DCP Neeta Desai, standing in for the Zone-1 DCP under whose jurisdiction the hospital falls, said, “We will send the bodies for a panel post-mortem examination. In the meantime, we will be investigating the medical camp in the village, the surgeries conducted on the people, and the allegations of medical negligence. We have currently filed an Accidental Death (AD) report but we will investigate the case thoroughly and file an FIR if deemed necessary.”
On Tuesday evening, the Gujarat Medical Council (GMC) began its investigation in the case. A letter by the registrar of the GMC to the hospital and its owners and doctors, accessed by The Indian Express, has asked them to provide all treatment papers, reports and hospital registration documents within seven days.
Mitesh Patel, the Sarpanch of Borisana village, who came to Ahmedabad along with the families of the deceased, said, “We want justice and will do all we can. The hospital management hasn’t spoken to me. Our main problem is that they conducted the surgeries without consent from the families. But their answer is that they took the consent from the patients themselves. I believe the main issue was that since all these patients had Ayushman cards, and the hospital didn’t need to bother about money, they carried out the seven surgeries in a single day. This would not have happened if payment had been taken from the families.”
Shaktisinh Gohil, Rajya Sabha MP and President of the Gujarat Congress, issued a statement on Tuesday evening, saying, “Even in 2022, three patients died (at the hospital) after stents were installed. If the government had taken strict action at the time and closed this hospital down, the lives of innocent people would have been saved today.”
Speaking to media persons, Chirag Rajput, the CEO of the hospital, said, “About 100 people attended the medical camp…Of these, around 20 were advised further tests in Ahmedabad. We carried out angiography and subsequently, angioplasty on seven of them of which two passed away due to their critical condition. We empathise with the families. The police are conducting a thorough investigation and we are bound to cooperate with them. We request the media to stand with us in this difficult time and report the truth.” However, he declined to answer the questions posed by the media personnel.

title: Nine from Gujarat indicted in US for running $9.5m illegal gambling biz - The Times of India
article_text:
AHMEDABAD: In a high-profile federal crackdown in the United States, nine men of Gujarati origin were indicted in a multi-million-dollar illegal gambling operation spread across six Missouri locations. The accused, all Indian nationals originally from Gujarat, allegedly operated skill game arcades as a front to run unlawful electronic gambling businesses, grossing over $9.5 million between 2022 and 2025.
The nine people, four from Georgia, two from New York, one each from Washington, Arkansas and Colorado, were charged in a 72-count superseding indictment returned under seal by a federal grand jury in Springfield on May 14, according to a statement from the US attorney in the western district of Missouri.
The superseding indictment replaces an indictment returned against one of them on Dec 10, 2024, and includes additional charges and defendants. The superseding indictment was unsealed and made public following the arrest of several defendants and in advance of certain defendants' arraignments on July 23 and 24, the statement added.
US attorney Jeff Ray emphasised the broader implications: "Illegal gambling operations affect the citizens of the neighbourhoods and communities where they are located as well as the local economy.
We worked closely with our law enforcement partners to shut down this criminal conspiracy and bring those responsible to justice."
"What began as a local investigation quickly expanded into a large, multi-jurisdictional case resulting in numerous indictments and a significant positive impact across our community," Springfield police chief Paul Williams said.
The defendants allegedly ran businesses with names such as Big Win Arcade, Spin Hitters and Vegas City Arcade, masking them as legitimate entertainment centres in cities including Springfield, Joplin and Branson West.
"This wasn't some low-level gambling scheme. It was an organised, multi-million-dollar criminal network that operated brazenly and believed it could stay one step ahead of law enforcement," said Mark Zito, special agent in charge, Homeland Security Investigations, Kansas City.
The indictment, unsealed just before arraignments on July 23-24, charges all nine with conspiracy to commit wire fraud, operating illegal gambling businesses and conspiracy to launder money. Some are also accused of depositing or transferring over $10,000 in illegal funds in single transactions.
"The federal indictment charges all nine defendants with one count each of participating in a conspiracy to commit wire fraud, conspiracy to operate an illegal gambling business, and operating illegal gambling businesses from July 1, 2022, to May 13, 2025. In addition to the conspiracy counts, all nine defendants were charged with at least one count of wire fraud, and eight defendants were charged with conspiracy to commit money laundering," the document states.
The Organized Crime Drug Enforcement Task Forces (OCDETF) of the US Department of Justice (DOJ) led the probe, working with the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Internal Revenue Service, Homeland Security, Missouri State Patrol and local police departments.
Modus operandiAccording to the indictment, the defendants ran illegal gambling businesses under the guise of internet amusement arcade games, skill game arcades and adult arcades. "Between April 24 and Aug 28, 2023, one of the defendants registered six businesses online with the Missouri Secretary of State: Big Win Arcade, LLC; Big Win Arcade 2023, LLC; Spin Hitters 1, LLC; Spin Hitters, LLC; Vegas City Arcade, LLC; and Vegas Arcade, LLC. The indictment alleges that the defendants then used these businesses to fraudulently apply for business licence applications filed with the cities of Springfield, Joplin, and Branson West, and to obtain utilities contracts, lease agreements and business incorporation documents filed with the State of Missouri," reads the document from the US Attorney's office.
The defendants hired local employees to work in their businesses, which operated contests of chance, gambling devices and slot machines in violation of Missouri and federal law. Five of the defendants participated in WhatsApp group chats where they communicated about the operation of the illegal gambling arcades from May 31, 2023, to March 11, 2024. The indictment alleges that the defendants transported the proceeds from the illegal gambling locations to several states to promote the ongoing illegal activity. They hid the proceeds of their gambling ring by depositing them in various personal bank accounts within the US and India. Over $9.5 million in US currency was laundered by this organisation in a little over three years, the document states.
What is Operation Take Back AmericaThis gambling bust was part of Operation Take Back America, a sweeping DOJ initiative to disrupt transnational criminal organisations. It unifies the resources of the OCDETF, Project ‘Safe Neighbourhoods' and immigration enforcement bodies. Aimed at dismantling drug cartels, fraud networks and illegal enterprises, the operation combines aggressive prosecution with intelligence-led policing. "Today's charges reflect the dedication of law enforcement, especially in Springfield, Joplin and across Southwest Missouri — to hold those who violate the law accountable," said FBI special agent in charge Stephen Cyrus. The Gujarat-origin gambling ring was one of the largest arcade-based frauds discovered under this national effort.
Details of the case- Suspected illegal immigration status among the nine accused
- Fraudulent business licences obtained in Missouri cities
- WhatsApp used for communication; cash moved between US and India
- Charged with wire fraud, illegal gambling, money laundering, racketeering
- Federal case under OCDETF & Operation Take Back America
- US attorney's office, FBI, ICE, IRS and local police departments involved in crackdown

Gujarat trader’s employees abducted, robbed of Rs 42 lakh in Kolkata after fake deal trap
Kolkata, May 19 (IANS) Two employees of a businessman from Gujarat were allegedly robbed by a gang on the pretext of carrying out a business transaction. After looting Rs 42 lakh from them, the accused allegedly abducted the two employees and forced them into a car.
However, it is alleged that the two men were later taken to the Kona Expressway in Howrah district and thrown out of the car. After learning about the incident, the businessman from Gujarat arrived in Kolkata and lodged a formal complaint, the police said on Tuesday.
The alleged robbery took place in the Survey Park area of South Kolkata. The businessman lodged a complaint at the Survey Park police station, following which a case of robbery and kidnapping was registered. The police launched an investigation and are examining CCTV footage from the area to identify the accused.
The police said that the incident took place in the first week of this month. The businessman from Gandhinagar in Gujarat was allegedly contacted by some people from Kolkata over a business deal. The suspects introduced themselves as businessmen and discussed sending certain goods from Kolkata to Gujarat.
The Gujarati businessman was allegedly told that the goods would be dispatched immediately if he paid Rs 42 lakh to the accused. Following the agreement, the businessman from Gandhinagar sent the money to Kolkata through two of his employees. They were taken to a house in the New Santoshpur area of south Kolkata. On reaching there, the employees were allegedly asked to hand over the cash, while they, in turn, demanded delivery of the goods.
It is alleged that the two employees were then confined in a room in the same house. Around six armed men allegedly held them at gunpoint and snatched the bag containing Rs 42 lakh from the employees. The victims reportedly kept banging on the door in an attempt to escape. Later, the accused allegedly took them out at gunpoint on the pretext of dropping them at Howrah station. The accused took the victims in a vehicle and abandoned them on the Kona Expressway before fleeing the scene.
The victims managed to reach the Howrah railway station and returned to Gujarat, where they informed the businessman about the entire incident. On Monday, the businessman reached Kolkata and lodged a complaint at the Survey Park police station regarding the robbery and abduction of his employees.
The Police are now trying to identify the house in the Survey Park area where the victims were kept. Investigators are trying to trace the vehicle and identify the accused through the contact numbers used to communicate with the businessman. The CCTV footage from Kolkata and Howrah is also being examined, the police said.

title: Patwaris, MSP staff linked to interstate scam: Fake farmers buy Gujarat groundnuts at ₹60, sell to Rajastha... - Bhaskar English

Bhaskar InvestigationPatwaris, MSP staff linked to interstate scam:Fake farmers buy Gujarat groundnuts at ₹60, sell to Rajasthan MSP centres for ₹72 per kg
- Copy link
The Minimum Support Price (MSP) system is designed to ensure fair prices for farmers’ produce nationwide. However, in Rajasthan’s Pali district, the same mechanism has turned into a major loss-making exercise for both the government and genuine farmers.
A 20-day ground investigation by Dainik Bhaskar has uncovered a large-scale scam in which traders and middlemen are buying groundnut already sold in Gujarat Mandis for Rs 55–60 per kilogram, and then reselling it at Rajasthan’s MSP centres for Rs 72.63 per kilogram by projecting it as locally grown produce.
60% groundnut at MSP centres not locally grown
At MSP procurement centres in the Sanchore and Raniwada areas of Jalore district, nearly 60 percent of the groundnut being weighed is neither grown in local fields nor belongs to local farmers. Most of it is coming from Nenava Mandi in Gujarat. On paper, however, everything appears legitimate. Through forged crop surveys (Girdawari), registration in farmers’ names, and collusion of MSP centre staff, the produce is being passed off as local. The Bhaskar team even tracked a tractor for 24 hours to verify the movement of goods.
Patwaris to MSP staff part of the interstate racket
The scam involves everyone from Patwaris to employees at MSP centres. Fields without any crop are shown as groundnut fields in Girdawari records. Based on these false entries, registrations are approved. Payments are deposited into farmers’ bank accounts, after which traders collect the money from them. A major red flag is the variety mismatch: areas known for RG-37 groundnut are reporting procurement of RG-20 at MSP centres—clearly indicating the produce is neither from local farms nor local farmers. This is not just a scam—it is the hijacking of the MSP system in the name of farmers.
₹42,000 direct profit per tractor
- Market price of groundnut: ₹55–60 per kg
- MSP procurement price: ₹72.63 per kg
- One tractor carries about 35 quintals
- Direct profit per tractor: around ₹42,000
With 40–50 tractors reaching MSP centres daily, the total gains during the procurement season could run into a large sum.
RG-20 groundnut comes from Bikaner, not Jalore
While the Raniwada and Sanchore regions traditionally produce the RG-37 variety, MSP centres here are procuring RG-20 groundnut. This variety is mainly grown in the Bikaner region and is supplied in large quantities to Gujarat’s Nenava mandi—further strengthening evidence of cross-border procurement fraud.
Bribes decide turn at MSP centres
The investigation also revealed that procurement at MSP centres runs more on bribes than on systems.
- Want an early turn? Pay money.
- Want fake produce weighed? Pay money.
- Refuse to pay? Wait 2–3 days for your turn.
At the Sanchore MSP centre, Bhaskar cameras captured employee Mehararam allegedly accepting bribes during the weighing process.
The findings raise serious questions about oversight, accountability, and the integrity of the MSP procurement system—meant to protect farmers, but now exploited in their name.

92% of paneer samples in Gujarat found to be fake, can cause cancer, heart diseases, warn doctors
Summarized by AI; it may make mistakes. Check important info

In Surat, a stock of 315 kg of fake paneer was seized on Sunday. As per reports, the accused had been selling fake paneer for the past four months.
92% of paneer in Gujarat found fake
The Gujarat Sweets and Farsan Association recently revealed that about 92% of paneer available in Gujarat is fake. Recently, the Food and Drug Control Authority (FDCA) in Gandhinagar conducted a survey of paneer served in more than 300 hotels across the state. In this survey, over 35% of paneer samples taken from different hotels failed quality checks. FDCA sources said these failed samples were either fake or adulterated paneer.
Out of the 300 hotels surveyed, around 100 were found to be serving adulterated or fake paneer to customers. This exposes people to the risk of serious illnesses. Tests on over 100 failed samples showed adulteration with palm oil, soybean oil, and acidic substances. Such adulteration is done for high profits at the cost of public health.
Paneer is generally classified into three categories:
- Standard paneer – with more than 50% milk fat
- Medium-fat paneer – with 20% to 50% milk fat
- Low-fat paneer – with about 20% milk fat
Among these, only standard paneer should be served as food. But to create fake paneer, adulterators mix palm oil, soybean oil, and acetic acid into paneer with only 10–15% milk fat to make it appear like standard paneer. Eating such paneer leads to serious health risks.
Greater risk of disease
Doctors say if a person consumes such adulterated paneer occasionally, they may suffer from short-term problems like indigestion, vomiting, diarrhea, headaches, gastritis, or allergies. But if consumed regularly, it increases the risk of stomach ulcers, stomach cancer, cholesterol build-up, and blockages in the arteries of the heart. It may also lead to kidney disease, liver damage, and diabetes.
How to identify fake paneer
- Real paneer is soft, while fake paneer stretches like rubber when broken.
- To test, boil paneer in hot water. Add soybean powder or flour. If the paneer is fake, its color will change immediately.
- Paneer made with detergent or urea turns red while boiling.
- Boil paneer in hot water for five minutes, then add a few drops of tincture iodine. If the color turns blue, the paneer is fake.

Luxury apartments near Surat airport face demolition threat: Builders obtained NOC using fake building loca... - Bhaskar English
article_text:
- English News
- Local
- Gujarat
- Surat
- Luxury Apartments Near Surat Airport Face Demolition Threat: Builders Obtained NOC Using Fake Building Locations; Bhaskar Uncovers Major Scam
Bhaskar InvestigationLuxury apartments near Surat airport face demolition threat:Builders obtained NOC using fake building locations; Bhaskar uncovers major scam
- Copy link
Many families in Surat are now facing the risk of losing their homes. They bought flats worth lakhs and crores after checking important papers like NA, NOC, and BU permissions. But Divya Bhaskar’s investigation has uncovered a big fraud in the NOC process. Builders and officials gave false information about building locations and heights. As a result, the Airport Authority has now found many apartments around Surat Airport that break safety rules. These buildings may soon be demolished.
Tall buildings around Surat airport are a threat
In the past few years, several apartment towers have been built around Surat Airport. These buildings are now causing problems for aircraft during take-off and landing. Strict rules exist for construction near airports to ensure safety. Builders must get NOC (No Objection Certificate) from the Airport Authority of India (AAI), the Roads and Buildings Department, and the local municipality. But in Surat, fake information was used to get these NOCs.
Fake coordinates used in official papers
According to the investigation, wrong latitude and longitude were shown while applying for NOC. These false coordinates helped builders get approval for construction in the red zone—an area where construction is either restricted or needs strict clearance.
In 2017, the AAI conducted a survey and found that several buildings were built taller than allowed and at different locations than mentioned in the documents.
6 buildings with major location frauds
Six apartment complexes were found to have been built at locations far from those mentioned during NOC approval.
1. Om Icon Apartment (Vesu Area)
- 88 flats in 4 towers, around 440 residents.
- Got BU permission from Surat Municipal Corporation.
- Upper 12.36 metres is considered a danger to aircraft.
- Actual location is 800 metres away from the location on paper.
2. Seven Heaven (TP Scheme No. 7, VIP Road)
- 154 flats in 7 towers of 11 floors.
- Violates height norms by 12.38 metres.
- On paper, the location is 1.3 km away in the opposite direction from its actual site.
3. Happy Glorious Apartment (Shivaji Maharaj Road)
- 6 towers with 12 floors each, about 770 residents.
- Built 8.53 metres above the permitted height.
- Actual site is 850 metres away from the one mentioned in the NOC file.
4. The Evolution Apartment (TP Scheme No. 6)
- 2 towers of 11 floors, around 300 residents.
- Built 12.01 metres higher than allowed.
- Actual location is 1.9 km from the declared one, in a residential area with low-rise houses.
5. The Legend Apartment (TP-29)
- 11 floors with 66 flats.
- Exceeds height limit by 1.48 metres.
- Declared coordinates are 300 metres away from the real site.
6. Green Fortune (Magdalla Area)
- 3 towers with 11 floors, 66 flats total.
- 4.91 metres taller than permitted.
- Location shown in papers is 750 metres from the actual site.
How the scam happened
Builders usually hire consultant agencies for NOC work. These agencies prepare the documents and approach the Roads and Buildings Department. But instead of checking details through site visits, officers approved papers with wrong location details.
The RL (Reduced Level) certificates were issued without any physical inspection. These certificates were then used to get NOCs from the AAI.
Role of government departments
After the AAI gave NOCs based on wrong information, builders got BU permissions from the Surat Municipal Corporation. SMC officials failed to verify whether the buildings were constructed at the correct location.
According to RTI activist Sanjay Ezhava, the Roads and Buildings Department is responsible for issuing incorrect RL certificates. He has filed a petition in court against this malpractice.
He also claimed that the AAI and DGCA (Director General of Civil Aviation) failed to re-check coordinates or building heights for many years. No verification took place between 2006 and 2017.
Builders blame the system
Some builders refused to comment, but Kiran Vahanaka said that a DGCA affidavit in 2020 claimed there was no NOC violation. He blamed changes in technology and errors in measurement.
Shivlal Ponkiya from CREDAI said that the rule of giving NOC based on latitude and longitude started only in 2012. Earlier, NOC was given based on distance from the airport. So the mistake lies in the AAI’s system.
Why height near airport is a risk
Aviation expert Hiten Panchal explained that large aircraft like Code C and D planes need a 3500-metre clear approach. Buildings near Surat Airport make landing difficult due to poor visibility. This is why only narrow-body aircraft operate there.
He said the runway can be extended towards Dumas, but ONGC properties nearby make it difficult.
Timeline of the disputed
- March 10, 2017: Airport Director flagged 12 projects for inspection.
- July 27–28, 2017: SMC and AAI inspected and added 5 more projects.
- August 2017: Re-verification of heights requested.
- October 2017: SMC said site verification is AAI’s job.
- December 18, 2017: Survey found NOC violations in 18 buildings.
- January 2018: AAI authorised to take demolition action.
- February 2018: SMC asked AAI to verify coordinates.
- June 2018: Field survey conducted.
- August 2018: 18 buildings found to exceed height limits.
Fresh survey in 2025
From 22 July 2025, a fresh joint survey is underway. Teams from AAI, the Collector’s office, SMC, and Roads & Buildings Department are inspecting buildings again. Early signs suggest that some buildings still pose risks. A final report is expected soon.
What lies ahead
Many homeowners in these luxury apartments are now in trouble. They bought these flats with loans or life savings. But due to fake NOC data and government negligence, their homes could be demolished.
Officials and builders blame each other, but ordinary families are paying the price.

title: Rs 11,613 crore lost to tax evasion via bogus billing in Gujarat - The Times of India
article_text:
AHMEDABAD: After overcoming initial challenges with
GST implementation, efforts have been made to improve the ease of doing business, attract new taxpayers, streamline the return filing process and meet tax targets. However, a formidable challenge remains for the state and the country: massive tax evasion.
Nearly seven years since GST rollout, Gujarat has witnessed a staggering Rs 94,761 crore in bogus billing turnover, leading to Rs 11,613 crore in evaded taxes. Data from the state commercial tax department, spanning FY 2017-18 to FY 2024-25, reveals this alarming trend. SGST officials have arrested 113 individuals, including key masterminds behind major tax evasion scams.
Despite numerous rule changes, fake billing scams persist, causing substantial tax evasion and significant losses to the exchequer. According to sources, only about 5% of the evaded amount, roughly Rs 550 crore, has been recovered by the department. In FY 2024 alone, 2,729 cases of bogus billing were recorded, involving fake GST registrations to dodge taxes. The number of cases has surged by 50%.
SGST officials reported that Rs 22,680 crore in fake billing transactions were made during the year to evade Rs 3,730 crore in taxes.
While the bogus billing turnover decreased by 37% compared to FY 2024, tax evasion increased by 30% in just one year.
In a statewide drive, both state and central GST departments are cracking down on scammers to curb fake billing. Gujarat also implemented a pilot project requiring biometric verification for new GSTINs, addressing the critical issue of no physical verification at the time of issuance. This mandatory biometric verification has led to a sharp decline in new registration applications in Gujarat.
“A number of changes proposed by the SGST department here have now been acknowledged at the national level and are being implemented in several other states facing similar issues,” said a source. The SGST department is also leveraging big data analytics to detect illicitly obtained registrations and prevent further frauds.

title: Man posing as ex-Gujarat MP's son booked for cheating investors through share market scam - The Times of India

Mumbai: The Mumbai Police have registered a case against a man for allegedly posing as the son of a former Gujarat MP and cheating a businessman along with others of lakhs of rupees on the promise of good returns on their share market investments, officials said.
The accused was identified as Vicky Vajubhai Barejia alias Vicky Prajapati, an official of Khar police station here said.

title: Gujarat govt plans to deploy AI to detect ITC scams in GST - A2Z Taxcorp LLP
article_text:
The state govt plans to create an AI defence as rising GST input tax credit (ITC) scams cost the state exchequer thousands of crores of rupees. The models based on AI and machine-learning (ML) will help the govt detect fraudulent entities and transactions.
The commercial tax division of the state’s finance department has tied up with BISAG-N (Bhaskaracharya National Institute for Space Applications and Geo-informatics) to develop a comprehensive system to detect ITC scams. Official sources said that with crores of transactions getting registered every year, the use of AI and ML to identify fraudulent ones has become the need of the hour.
A key govt source said that about 29 crore transactions related to input credit get registered in the state every year. “It is almost impossible to manually check and verify the authenticity of every transaction. The govt has decided to seek the services of BISAG to find a workable solution to malpractices in ITC,” sources said.
“BISAG has already developed a large language model (LLM), which is presently under testing. The AI model will require further fine-tuning. All transactions involving ITC will be run through the model, which will prompt the department on ITC transactions and entities that appear to be fraudulent,” sources said.
Sources in the govt said that using AI and ML will help the commercial tax department to crack down more effectively against ITC scams, as use of AI will identify potential fraudulent transactions.
Govt officials added that the BISAG-developed model will also flag irregularities on the part of govt officials. “In some cases, it has been observed that govt employees have been involved in ITC-related scams. This proposed model will flag irregularities on the part of govt officers as well,” said sources. Sources said that the state govt will start using the AI-based system more aggressively once it is fine-tuned and ready for use.

Over the next three days, between April 12 and 15, the accused persons allegedly kept calling the man asking him to pay the money or face the “love jihad” case.
“The man, who after being released from preventive detention, had gone back to live with the woman in the same house and planned to mortgage some gold ornaments to pay off the accused. Later he decided to approach the ACB,” ACB investigation officer Ankur Prajapati said.

The ACB also seized Syed’s phone in which the agency found a recorded conversation he had with the inspector saying he had received the amount.

He said the detainees used fake documents obtained from West Bengal to stay in different parts of India before coming to Gujarat.

title: Holy Cow! Gujarat Govt Scraps Surat Land Deal - Vibes Of India
article_text:
The Gujarat government has scrapped a land deal and declared the controversial Surat land deal as null and void after reports of large-scale corruption and kickbacks. A Rs 100 crore plus land exclusively reserved for cattle grazing was sold off for a mere Rs 24.31 crores in Surat. With the cancellation of the land deal, the BJP Government in Gujarat has tacitly admitted that the deal reeked of corruption, was wrong and several fake documents were fabricated to facilitate it.
The District Collector has launched an investigation into this land dispute announcing that an order has been issued to cancel the land deed. The order has also mandated maintaining the status quo and prohibited any alterations to the land.
The village committee that managed the land Magob Village Samast Organisation violated conditions and converted the purpose of land. Now, the land deal has been cancelled and the land has been again shown as government-owned.
District Collector Dr Saurabh Pardhi confirmed to Vibes of India that the investigation has been assigned to the provincial officer, with a report to be prepared and submitted to the government following its conclusion.
A 100 crore land reserved for cow grazing was intentionally devalued and siphoned off to private individuals. The 100 crore plus land, which cannot be used for any private purpose as per the government rule was sold at just Rs 24.31 crores in Magob village of Puna taluka in Surat district of Gujarat. Stamp duty documents of Rs 1.70 crore were prepared and paid for this to arrive at the land cost. Sources claim that kickbacks of over Rs five crores could have been offered to two officials for the land scam.
In a meticulously planned conspiracy, which is not possible without the involvement of government officials, the purpose of land, the value of land, fake documentation, undervalued stamp duty imposition was done to facilitate the scam. This caused a huge loss to the public exchequer.
This Surat cow grazing land scam is the latest in the BJP’s long list of land-related scams. Land price in Surat in Gujarat is one of the most costly but fake reports and connivance of government officers with the land mafia has been resulting in huge losses to the government exchequer.
Speaking to Vibes of India, Isudan Gadhvi, the Aam Aadmi Party’s State President said, “BJP leaders, officials, and cadres have allegedly occupied significant portions of land across Gujarat, including attempts to indirectly take over land in Surat. Critics argue that the government cannot claim ignorance of these activities, pointing to instances where Gauchar (grazing) lands have reportedly been handed over to industrialists. It is alarming that such incidents occur in the area of CR Patil, a Union Minister. The recurring reports of land-grabbing cases involving Gauchar lands have prompted calls for accountability and raised questions about the government’s role. It is estimated that a thorough investigation could potentially reclaim lands worth over ₹3 lakh crore across Gujarat.”
The prized land reserved for cow grazing in Magob village of Puna Taluka of Surat district in South Gujarat (survey number 3-B, block number 156) was marked as government land which cannot be sold for anything private.
The 7891 square metre plot originally kept reserved for cattle grazing was first “acquired ” by the government to construct a canal. After the purpose of the land was changed, later, it was devalued and sold to two locals at one-fourth cost. Sources claim they the local buyers could be a facade for some rich powerful land mafia whose name has yet not been revealed.
Two officials from the managing institution and originally, this land was registered under the Magob Village Samast Trust of the government. Then a fake resolution was drafted reportedly by Rajendrasinh Pratapsinh Gohil, a trustee of Magob Village Samast, along with five other members of the trust. This resolution, which was adopted unanimously, first changes the purpose of land and then its sale. This 100 crore plus worth of land was given away for Rs 24.31 crores. The new land deed shows Ketan Fatesinh Gohil and Mahesh Virambhai Barot as the owners of the government land. The new land deal was done on November 3.
“This is nothing new; such incidents keep happening under the BJP government, particularly in Surat and Ahmedabad. With land values rising daily, an internal committee manipulates the system, gambling on land deals and pressuring government officials to finalise them. Over the past 2–3 years, there have been more than seven cases of land scams.” Congress Spokesperson, Surat, Naishad Desai told Vibes of India.
After this dubious land deal was completed, a Town Planning (TP) scheme was announced leading to a price surge in the area.
Sources say culprits had insider knowledge that due to the new TP Scheme No. 64, land prices would soar. The sources added that the entire conspiracy would have taken at least eight months from conception to execution. A local non-mainstream media in Surat exposed this scam first leading others including Vibes of India to probe into it.

title: Fake Hindutva vs Real: Ram Mandir controversy resurfaces in Gujarat - India Today
article_text:
Fake Hindutva vs Real: Ram Mandir controversy resurfaces in Gujarat
Cong leader Paresh Dhanani's comment to help Ram temples in villages immediately draws reaction from BJP calling Congress a 'fake Hindutva' party
Elections or not, Ram Mandir has come to the centre stage of political discourse in Gujarat again these days.
The newly appointed opposition leader, Congress MLA Paresh Dhanani on Tuesday at a rally in Prantij taluka in Sabarkantha district, north Gujarat, said BJP practices 'fake Hindutva' as the party has not even built a Ram temple in Ayodhya despite being in power for 40 months in the centre.
He further added that as an initiative to revive the social culture that revolves around a Ram temple in a gaam no choro (village center square), his NGO Parivartan will distribute kits consisting of a Jhalar, Shankh, Nagara etc (Jingles, conch and drums) to villages that would like to revive their temples.
While Dhanani, an MLA from Amreli in Saurashtra, claimed to have said this in his personal capacity as a social worker, the state Congress within minutes owned it and said its workers will replicate this across the state.
On this BJP spokespersons jumped in and slammed Congress' initiatives. They instead rushed in to claim the mantle of being the real Hindutva party.
BJP spokesperson Bharat Pandya called Congress a 'fake, opportunist' party which is playing with the Hindutva agenda to milk poll benefits. To this, the Congress CLP again retorted on Twitter that the BJP appears to have lost its agenda.
"I will go to a temple, a mosque, a gurudwara and even a church. No one can stop me, because I respect all religions and the Constitution of the country," Dhanani tweeted.
"For years BJP has painted Congress as an anti-Hindu, Muslim party. But when our Congress national president Rahul Gandhi visited temples, they felt they have lost their agenda altogether. They have been questioning why Gandhi went to temples as if he has no right to," Dhanani told India Today.
He reiterated that this particular initiative is not political, but one to spread social awareness about the village's community that traditionally revolves around a temple, where villagers gather and interact with each other.
BJP's senior leader and spokesperson Pandya in a statement said the Congress must stop its ideology of spreading caste, communal discrimination while supporting terrorism.
"The Congress has in the past questioned the existence of Lord Ram and even worked towards ensuring that the Ram Temple is not built in Ayodhya. This is a classic case of hypocrisy by the party, which only worships the Nehru-Gandhi family, who have ruled the country for 38 years. The party has no ideology and suffers from identity crisis," his statement said.
Congress courted controversy over its 'soft Hindutva' policy when Rahul Gandhi visited as many as 25 temples in Gujarat while campaigning for the state assembly elections last year.
Similar allegations flew back and forth all through the four months of campaigning, but this issue has again come to the fore as elections/ by-elections for the 1400 gram panchayats in 32 districts of the state are scheduled on February 4. However, these elections are not contested on party symbol.
Congress is traditionally strong in rural areas. In the 2017 elections, of the 77 seats the party (with allies) won, 71 were rural seats in a house of 182 seats. The BJP meanwhile won only 63 of the 140 rural seats but it continued its urban sweep with 36 of the 42 seats
According to various surveys, though Congress continues to bag a majority of Muslim votes, BJP is also catching up.
In the elections that last happened, it is estimated that up to 64% of Muslims voted for Congress, but the BJP has increased its penetration by about 7%.
However, Congress' big revival is attributed to its penetration within the Patidar community, where the party is estimated to have gained about 25% more votes this time.
Political observers believe the Patidar community is largely wedded to the Hindutva ideology that the BJP has been propagating.
"For the first time, Congress is acting like a strong opposition that actually wants to come in power. It is pulling out the carpet under BJP's feet. For its revival, the Congress needs to gain the confidence of the majority communities and needs to shun the tag of an anti-Hindu party," political analyst Shyam Parekh says.

AHMEDABAD: When the income tax (I-T) department officials started poring through thousands of records of money trail from the registered unrecognized political parties (RUPPs) in the state, they were surprised by the ingenuity of the entire racket. Those who orchestrated it, tried every trick in the book to cover the tracks. What connects all these parties is the near-zero presence on ground and obscure addresses, often in chawls or decrepit buildings where promoters could be autorickshaw drivers, small-time shop owners among others," said sources.
Sources indicated that APMC-based firms were reportedly used to launder money. "If a party - which gets donations of say Rs 1 lakh - shows the purchase of vegetables for lunch organized for 100 persons and offsets the amount, there is no way to verify where the veggies went. Perishables and often bullion which were often showed on the books for years - were used to show the expenses incurred. In reality, all these purchases were made on books of accounts only and the tax rebate was claimed by the taxpayers," said sources, adding that the same modus operandi was used to launder the black money.

title: Habitual offender facing 11 charges threatens media in police station: Held in Surat in multi-crore land gr... - Bhaskar English

Habitual offender facing 11 charges threatens media in police station:Held in Surat in multi-crore land grabbing attempt, modus operandi revealed

In Surat, accused Vinu Haribhai Malviya, who is allegedly known for defrauding landowners and attempting to usurp property worth crores, has once again come under legal scrutiny. He has been arrested by the Economic Cell in connection with a case involving illegal grabbing of a valuable plot in the Vesu area.
Malviya, who is reportedly involved in around 11 serious criminal cases, was produced in court. That time his arrogance and aggressivet attitude towards media drew attention. DCP Karansinh Raj Vaghela described him as a “habitual and cunning” offender. However, Malviya continues to maintain his innocence.
The court has sent him to four days of police remand for further investigation.
Fake exchange deeds created on stamp paper
Vinu Malviya and his accomplice, Pratul Patel, allegedly hatched a major criminal conspiracy to grab land worth crores in New Block/Survey No. 311/2 of Vesu village. Police investigation revealed that the two created forged exchange deeds for the new tenure land, which cannot legally be sold.
According to investigators, the accused procured old stamp papers and fabricated documents on them to make the transactions appear legitimate. The most shocking aspect of the case is that two separate exchange deeds were prepared on the same stamp paper bearing registration number 5062, by inserting two different dates—16 August 2001 and 26 May 2001.
Accused in 11 cases displays high-handed attitude
After his arrest, when Vinu Malviya was brought before the media, his conduct reflected that of a hardened offender. Agitated by the presence of cameras, he said, “Do not disrespect anyone. The investigation is still ongoing. What will you gain by publishing this in the media? This is not a court proceeding.”
Police officials were taken aback by his remarks, noting that despite facing 11 serious criminal cases, he showed no visible fear of the law. Instead, he appeared defiant and was seen lecturing journalists on morality and dignity.
Misled police during interrogation Surat Economic Cell DCP Karansinh Raj Vaghela has taken a strict stance on this matter. He has clearly stated that Vinu Malviya is a well-known and hardened criminal. He is not cooperating at all in the police investigation and is misleading the investigating officers by giving evasive answers to questions. The DCP further added that the accused is so cunning that he is constantly trying to hide his criminal methods, but the police are scrutinizing his background.
11 crimes have been registered against Vinu Malviya so far DCP of Eco Cell Karanraj Singh Vaghela said that Vinu Malviya is a known criminal, a total of 11 different cases have been registered against him within Surat city and his criminal history spans from 2009 till today. Between 2009 to 2026, 11 different crimes have been registered against him, out of which 8 crimes are of similar nature involving fraud and forgery under sections 406, 420, 465, 67, 68, 71. Additionally, one extortion case has been registered against him, one rioting case has been registered against him, and one IT Act case has also been registered against him.
Serious allegations of fraud with judiciary Dr. Shailesh R. Patel - Advocate was present on behalf of the complainant. In the remand grounds submitted by the police in court, it has been stated that the accused not only created fake documents, but also misled the honorable court. In 2002, accused Pratul Patel along with Vinu Malviya had filed a civil suit. In this, without the presence of the original landowners, they submitted a fake 'settlement deed' by using signatures obtained on blank papers. In this way, the accused misused the judicial process to obtain false decrees, which the original owners came to know about years later.
Police presented 12 points to obtain remand Police presented about 12 main points while demanding remand. Police say that original fake property documents are yet to be seized. Investigation is needed to determine where and from whom the stamp with registration number 5062 was obtained. Additionally, there is a strong possibility of involvement of other white-collar persons who helped behind the scenes in this scam. If the accused is not in police custody, they may tamper with evidence, therefore their thorough interrogation is essential.
Role of Stamp Vendors and Forged Signatures During the investigation, it was also revealed that this gang misused stamps obtained from stamp vendors M.A. Valand and Ramesh R. Patel. On 16/08/2001, a simple exchange deed without notary showing a sale value of 600,000 was created. This document, presented as Exhibit-3/2 in List-3 during the judicial process, appears to be completely fabricated at first glance. The accused made representations in court as if all parties had agreed, but in reality, the original owners were unaware of this matter.
Criminal History and Absconding Associate Police informed the court that cases have been previously registered against Vinu Malviya at the DCB police station. Being familiar with police procedures, he does not directly reveal any facts. The main accused Pratul Patel is still absconding in this case, and Vinu likely has information about where he is hiding. Additionally, the disappearance of original property documents from court records is suspicious, which requires separate investigation.
Statewide Scam Suspicion and High Court Proceedings There are concerns that this entire scam is not limited to just one property but could be a statewide stamp paper scam. The Economic Cell is also investigating how old dated stamp papers are being obtained and who all are involved in this. In the honorable High Court, the land owner Vijaybhai Ramanbhai Patel and others have challenged the Civil Court's order through Civil Application No. 2778/2022.
Vinu Malviya's 4-day remand approved Finally, the police had demanded 10 days remand for accused Vinu Malviya. After hearing arguments from both sides, considering the seriousness of the crime and investigation requirements, the court has approved police custody remand for accused Vinu Malviya until 14:00 hours (2:00 PM) on 18/02/2026. Now all eyes will be on how many other key players in this land scam will be revealed during police interrogation in the coming days.
