title: 11 Gujarati charged in US for staging fake robberies to obtain U visas - The Times of India
article_text:
Ahmedabad: Eleven Indian nationals, all from Gujarat, have been charged in the United States for allegedly staging armed robberies at convenience stores in order to falsely claim victim status and obtain immigration benefits under the U visa programme, federal authorities announced on Friday.
According to the US Attorney’s Office for the District of Massachusetts, the accused allegedly conspired to carry out fake robberies at several stores in Massachusetts so that clerks could claim they were victims of violent crime and apply for a U visa — a special immigration benefit granted to victims who assist law enforcement in investigations.
Watch
U Visa Scam Busted: 11 Indian Nationals Accused Of Staging Armed Robberies In United States
The accused were identified as Jitendrakumar Patel (39), Maheshkumar Patel (36), Sanjaykumar Patel (45), Dipikaben Patel (40), Rameshbhai Patel (52), Amitabahen Patel (43), Ronakkumar Patel (28), Sangitaben Patel (36), Minkesh Patel (42), Sonal Patel (42) and Mitul Patel (40).
Investigators said several of them were residing unlawfully in different parts of the United States.
Six of the accused were arrested in Massachusetts and produced before a federal court in Boston on Friday, while others were arrested in Kentucky, Missouri and Ohio. Authorities said they will be presented before the Boston court at a later date.
The investigation found that the accused allegedly paid an organiser to stage robberies at convenience stores, liquor shops and fast-food outlets.
During these incidents, a person posing as a robber would threaten store clerks with what appeared to be a firearm and flee with cash, while the entire sequence was recorded on store surveillance cameras.
Investigators said the clerks would deliberately wait several minutes before informing the police so that the staged crime appeared genuine. The alleged “victims” reportedly paid the organiser to take part in the scheme, while store owners were also compensated for allowing their premises to be used.
The organiser, the man who played the robber and the getaway driver were previously arrested and convicted in the case.
Federal prosecutors said the conspiracy allowed participants to falsely claim that they had suffered mental or physical abuse in a violent crime and seek legal immigration status in the United States.
If convicted, the accused could face up to five years in prison, three years of supervised release and a fine of up to $250,000.
The case is being investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation along with immigration authorities.

title: Cybercrime cases rise by 235% in 5 years in Gujarat - The Times of India
article_text:
AHMEDABAD/VADODARA: While the 'Digital India' push has led to a massive surge in online transactions, cybercrime offences too are growing exponentially. Over the past five years, cybercrime cases in Gujarat have risen by 235%, reveals data released by National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB). During the Covid years, the cases almost doubled.
Against one case of cybercrime every day in 2017, four cases were registered in 2021.
While 458 cases were reported in 2017, 1,536 cases were filed in 2021 - a 235% increase.
In 2019, 784 offences of cybercrime were filed in the state, while in 2020, the pandemic year, the figure stood at 1,283. In 2021, chargesheets were filed in 58 per cent of the offences.
Cyber experts said that many people suddenly began using apps during the Covid-induced lockdown, but most could not differentiate between genuine and bogus apps.
A senior officer from the cybercrime cell said that during the Covid period, people were largely confined to their homes and depended heavily on e-wallets and digital payment apps to purchase even vegetables and groceries. However, lack of awareness about technology makes it a double-edged sword.
Taking advantage of the tectonic shift in buying behaviour, cybercriminals created fake customer support numbers of banks and online shopping sites to defraud people.
The scammers, posing as customer care executives, hoodwinked citizens into sharing their OTPs (one-time passwords) that gave them access to their bank accounts. The detection rate in such crimes was less than 10%, a cybercrime sleuth said.
Police have been organizing online campaigns to make people aware of the different modus operandi employed by cybercrooks and how to avoid getting conned.
"Many ended up clicking on dubious links or scanning QR codes sent by scammers. A lot of people lost their money to such frauds," said Mayur Bhusavalkar, a cyber expert from Vadodara. Cyber criminals have also been devising newer methods to cheat people.
Some of these include tricking teenagers into installing malware-infected porn apps that lock their phones, and seeking money to unlock them.
"Some fraudsters trick unsuspecting victims into sharing their online passwords under the pretext of completing their KYC process while others resort to phishing by creating fake websites to steal information," Bhusavalkar told TOI.

Surat SOG arrests 2 in fake currency racket:Accused sourced money from Bangladesh, codewords used for illegal transactions; counterfeit notes worth ₹6 lakh seized
- Copy link
Surat’s Special Operations Group (SOG) has arrested two individuals attempting to circulate counterfeit ₹500 notes in the Puna vegetable market. The accused, identified as Vijay Chauhan and Suresh alias Guruji alias Chakor, were caught red-handed, and fake currency worth ₹9,000 was seized from them.
Investigations revealed that Suresh, who hails from Lathidadia, has ties to Malda in West Bengal, a region notorious for fake currency production near the Bangladesh border. The police found that Suresh had previously visited Mumbai three times to circulate counterfeit notes.
Codeword 'Mawa' used for fake currency transactions
During interrogation, it was revealed that the accused used codewords while dealing in counterfeit money. They would use the word 'Mawa' to indicate a fake currency exchange, and once the transaction was successful, they signaled completion with the phrase 'Shekela Mawa.'
Raid at accused’s house leads to more seizures
DCP Rajdeepsinh Nakum of the SOG stated that a 15-day surveillance operation had been in place after reports emerged of fake notes being used in paan shops and vegetable markets. Following their arrest, a raid at the accused’s residences led to the recovery of additional counterfeit notes — ₹5,000 from Suresh’s house and ₹4,000 from Vijay’s house.
High-quality fake notes printed in West Bengal
Officials disclosed that the seized counterfeit notes were of high quality, featuring security threads, watermarks, and paper that made them difficult to differentiate from genuine currency.
The accused reportedly sourced fake notes from West Bengal’s Malda region by paying ₹2 lakh to acquire ₹6 lakh worth of counterfeit currency. Each time, they exchanged ₹1 lakh to obtain ₹3 lakh in fake notes, successfully bringing counterfeit currency into Surat on multiple occasions.
Accused Suresh's criminal past and NIA cases
Suresh alias Guruji has a long criminal history, having served six years in jail for similar offenses. He has been associated with counterfeit currency rackets since 2010 and has pending cases with agencies like the NIA, ATS, and DCB.
His record includes cases under NIA Kolkata Special Case No-05/2015 and NIA Ahmedabad Cases No-01/2019 and 02/2019, in addition to cases registered in Junagadh, Varachha, and Surat.
Possible Bangladesh connection under investigation
The police are also investigating a possible Bangladesh link in the case. The prime suspect, Tahir Sheikh from Malda, West Bengal, is believed to be a key supplier of fake currency. A team has been dispatched to locate and arrest him, as authorities suspect the currency could be printed in Bangladesh before being smuggled into India.
Fake currency detector machine found
Among the seized items was a China-made currency detector machine ordered online by Vijay Chauhan. The device, which identifies fake notes by displaying green dots, is similar to machines used in banks. The accused used this to verify fake notes before circulating them.
Catering business as a front for fake currency circulation
Apart from counterfeiting, both accused were also involved in the catering business. This served as a cover to launder fake currency, allowing them to distribute counterfeit notes in markets and daily transactions.
Over ₹6 lakh fake currency circulated in Surat
The investigation revealed that the accused had already circulated counterfeit notes worth ₹6 lakh in Surat and surrounding areas. The police suspect that many others may have unknowingly received fake currency, and further legal action will be taken against those found in possession of large amounts.
Seized items from accused
Following their arrest, the police seized:
- 18 fake currency notes of ₹500 each (Total: ₹9,000)
- 3 mobile phones worth ₹21,000
- Fake Money Detector Machine
- Cash from Fake Currency Transactions worth ₹1,03,830
- Total seized items worth ₹1,25,330
The SOG is continuing its probe into the racket and is working to dismantle the entire network involved in circulating fake currency in Gujarat.

title: Gujarat: Rs 84 lakh shoe swap lands dentist in jail - The Times of India
article_text:
AHMEDABAD: When branded shoes worth Rs 84 lakh were bought online and returned to a firm over nine months, it raised the alarm — and rightly so. The shoes were found to be counterfeit, and the fraud was traced to Kheda, where a 24-year-old dentist was found to be the centre of the crafty caper.
Matar police on Thursday arrested Parth Sharma, a resident of Sokhda, and booked his partner-in-crime, Aryaveer Singh from Maharanibaug in New Delhi, for the con.
Their method of operation was shockingly simple yet audacious. Between June 26, 2023, and March 15, 2024, Sharma and Singh allegedly executed the switcheroo, replacing a staggering 1,073 pairs of branded shoes with counterfeit ones. The pair bought and replaced an average of four pairs a day over the course of those nine months.
Ateeq Ahmed Syed, an enforcement officer with Instacart Services Private Ltd, realized something was fishy on March 21 when he noticed an unusual influx of returned footwear. “The shoes were bought through an
online shopping portal. An inquiry revealed that a man named Parth Sharma had used 500 different IDs on the website to buy two top models of shoes. He would return it, replacing the original pair with counterfeit ones, causing the firm a loss of Rs 84 lakh,” said Syed in his FIR.
Inspector Keval Vekaria of the Matar police revealed that Sharma, who got his Bachelor of Dental Surgery (BDS) last year, was looking for part-time business opportunities. Sharma met Singh approximately a year ago through a social media platform.
“According to Sharma, Singh proposed purchasing original shoes and replacing them with duplicates. Sharma would procure shoes and swap them within 15 days. He intentionally avoided disclosing his exact address. He would meet the delivery personnel at various locations to prevent his residence from being identified,” said Vekaria.
Vekaria added that Sharma created different IDs on the shopping portal using various Aadhaar cards and phone numbers. The police are investigating how he procured them.
Matar police filed a complaint against Sharma and Singh for cheating, forgery, producing forged documents as genuine, forgery with the purpose of cheating, and criminal conspiracy. Vekaria said that Singh is on the run.

title: Engineer held with fake currency notes in Gujarat - The Times of India
article_text:
AHMEDABAD: Gandhinagar police on Saturday arrested an electrical engineer, who was printing currency notes on a colour printer.
The accused was reeling under financial crisis. As he suffered losses in his share market business. Cops of special operations group (SOG) of Gandhinagar have seized fake currency notes worth Rs 9.84 lakh in the denomination of Rs 2,000 from the accused.
Sources in the Gandhinagar SOG said that two PSIs got information that the accused Rutvij Raval, 37, a resident of Elite Apartments in Gota, was printing fake currency notes using a colour printer.
A team of Gandhinagar police went to the spot near Sindhbaad Hotel on the Ahmedabad-Mehsana highway in Kalol. Where Raval was sitting on a scooter and was holding a bag. Police nabbed him and searched his bag. Fake currency notes in denomination of Rs 2,000 were found from the bag.
Later, cops also searched his house and found a colour printer and high-quality blank papers which he used for printing fake notes.
During the preliminary investigation. Raval told cops that he recently had started printing fake notes. He wanted to give those fake notes to Angadia firms, but before he could execute his plan he was caught.
"He holds a electrical engineer degree, but he could not find a suitable job. So, he started working as a stockbroker. He did well for himself for some years. But, from last two, three years, he sustained losses and his income dwindled. So, he decided to publish fake currency notes," said a police officer of the Gandhinagar SOG. Police officers said that Raval was also accused in a cheating case filed with the Mehsana police earlier this year. Kalol police have registered a case for counterfeiting currency notes, for possessing fake currency notes and for possessing instruments to counterfeit currency notes against Raval and have begun investigation.

title: Fake Hospital Busted In Gujarat; Owner Booked - ETV Bharat
article_text:
Fake Hospital Busted In Gujarat; Owner Booked
The hospital running on the sixth floor of Shikhar Avenue Complex in Chiloda was operated on the basis of forged certificates by Amdavad Municipal Corporation.
Published : March 20, 2025 at 12:36 PM IST
Ahmedabad: Authorities have unearthed a fake hospital and booked its owner in Naroda area of Gujarat's Ahmedabad.
ACP of G Division V.N. Yadav said that the fake hospital named 'Three Star Hospital' was being run by its owner Dharmendra alias Sanjay Patel, a resident of New Shahibaug area of Ahmedabad.
Patel, police said, rented a shop on the sixth floor of Shikhar Avenue Complex in Chiloda area of Naroda where he ran the hospital with an ICU and Trauma Center without any legal authorisation through a forged Form C bearing stamp and seals of the Amdavad Municipal Corporation (AMC).
According to the police, the accused operated the illegal hospital through fake case papers, medical reports in the name of different doctors and treatment certificates by misusing the doctor registration numbers issued by the Gujarat Medical Council. Besides, he also levied illegal treatment charges on the patients.
Police have sealed the hospital and booked the owner under relevant sections of law. Further investigation into the case is going on.
In another case of quackery, a fake gynecologist was arrested by the police from Dayapar area of Kutch in Gujarat.
According to the police, the accused Anuradha Mantu Prasad Yadav, originally from Bihar, was running a fake maternity hospital without any medical degree.
A police spokesperson said that a joint team of Dayapar police and Dayapar Taluka Health Officer Dr. KK Patel, TMPHS Ajay Solanki, MPSS Jabbar Sama and Pharmacist Velabhai Buchiya raided Janani Hospital in Maruti Complex in Dayapar and sealed it besides arresting the fake doctor.

Surat police register first case against local dairy owner:Over 754 kg of fake paneer seized, being sold at half price, endangering public health
- Copy link
In Surat, for the first time, a case has been registered against a dairy owner after paneer samples failed testing. After paneer samples taken from Surabhi Dairy failed, the S.O.G. police filed a case against the owner of Surabhi Dairy at Khatodara police station. Police also seized about 754 kg of paneer, which was being sold at cheap rates to different hotels and street vendors.
On November 11, 2025, a slow poison network was exposed in Surat. SOG raided two units of Surat's famous 'Surabhi Dairy' and seized a huge quantity of 955 kilograms of suspicious fake paneer, while this dairy was sending 200 kg of fake paneer to the market daily.
The most serious matter is that the dairy operator admitted in initial police questioning that this paneer is fake. This dairy was dumping around 200 kg of fake paneer daily in Surat's market, which was being sold at half the price of real paneer at Rs 250-270 per kg, using glacial acetic acid to make fake paneer. This acid is suspected to be used for quickly curdling milk to make paneer, which is seriously harmful to health.
755.621 kilograms of suspicious paneer stock
Surat's Khatodara police raided a godown at shop number 434 in Sorathiya Compound located behind INS Hospital in their jurisdiction. This godown was being used as a distribution center by 'Surbhi Dairy'. During the raid, dairy operator Shaileshbhai Chaghanbhai Patel was found present at the godown.
When the police searched the warehouse, they found 755.621 kilograms of suspicious paneer stock, which was valued at Rs. 1,81,343. This paneer was kept ready for sale in plastic packaging. When police strictly interrogated Shaileshbhai, he confessed that all this stock was ordered from their main manufacturing unit, which is located in Sayan, Olpad.
Question - What things should be kept in mind while buying paneer? Answer- When buying paneer, definitely ask for some paneer as a sample from the shopkeeper. After this, keep these points in mind.
- Real paneer is soft and spongy, so when buying make sure to press the cheese slightly. If its texture is hard, it could be fake cheese.
- Real paneer is made only from milk, and has no smell or taste other than milk. If you taste anything other than milk after eating paneer, the paneer could be adulterated.
- Real paneer does not stretch like rubber. It remains soft and tender.

Diamond artisan circulated 5,000 fake ₹500 currency notes in Surat:25% cut tempted accused; same series numbers led to arrest by SOG
- Copy link
A fake currency scam has been uncovered in Surat, where a diamond artisan circulated counterfeit Rs 500 notes worth Rs 25 Lakhs in the market within one year. Lured by a 25% commission, he entered the illegal trade. His operation collapsed after police noticed that all fake notes carried the same series number. Surat SOG arrested the accused and seized counterfeit notes, a mobile phone, and a motorcycle.
Diamond artisan turned counterfeit dealer
The accused, Paresh Hadiya, worked as a diamond artisan in Surat’s diamond industry. He had been employed at Kiran Diamond for six years. His monthly salary was Rs 20,000. Driven by greed and financial pressure, he chose crime as a shortcut to earn quick money.
Rs 25 lakhs circulated in one year
During interrogation, Paresh admitted that he circulated fake currency worth more than Rs 25 Lakhs in one year. He passed the notes mainly at night. He targeted vegetable markets, paan shops, and crowded areas. He received a 25% commission, while the remaining 75% went to the main supplier.
SOG action on specific intelligence
Under the guidance of DCP Rajdeep Singh Nakum, Surat SOG received a tip-off about fake note circulation in Varachha and Sarathana areas. Police kept surveillance based on this input. Paresh Hadiya was caught from Varachha Mini Road.
Rs 5 lakh fake notes seized
During the search, police recovered counterfeit Rs 500 notes worth Rs 5 Lakhs from Paresh. The quality of the notes initially surprised officers. A mobile phone was also seized from his possession.
Same series number raised suspicion
Investigation revealed that advanced printers and special paper were used to print the notes. However, all the Rs 500 notes had the same series number. The notes also lacked a security thread. These flaws confirmed they were counterfeit.
Living in Surat for 10 years
Paresh had been living in Surat with his family for the last 10 years. He appeared to be an ordinary diamond worker. For one year, he managed to evade police action before being caught.
Goods worth Rs 5.55 lakhs seized
Police seized items worth Rs 5.55 Lakhs in total. This included fake notes worth Rs 5,03,500, a Motorola mobile phone, and a Honda Shine motorcycle (GJ05LU5480) used for the crime.
Mastermind identified
Police identified Raju Kanubhai Vaghmashi of Savarkundla as the mastermind behind the racket. He supplied the fake notes to Paresh. Police are searching for Raju and trying to locate the printing press used to produce the counterfeit currency.
Police appeal to public
Surat Police have urged citizens to carefully check currency notes, especially during large transactions. Further investigation is ongoing.

Fake trustees construct shops, flats on Waqf land in Ahmedabad:Illegally collect rent worth lakhs; 5 arrested for exploiting trust property worth ₹100 cr
- Copy link
In a major fraud case unearthed in Ahmedabad’s Jamalpur area, five individuals including Salim Khan have been arrested for illegally constructing shops and houses on land belonging to the Glass Mosque and Shah Bada Kasam Trust and collecting rent worth lakhs of rupees over the years.
The land, which was given by the Waqf Board to the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation (AMC), was misused by the accused, who falsely claimed to be trustees and exploited the property for personal financial gain.
Fake trustees build shops on school land
According to a complaint filed by Mohammad Rafiq Ansari at the Gaekwad Haveli police station, all original trustees of the Glass Mosque Trust have passed away. Adjacent to the mosque is a plot of land which was handed over to AMC years ago. A school was constructed on this land, but it was damaged in the 2001 earthquake.
Taking advantage of the situation, Salim Khan and others falsely presented themselves as trustees in 2009 and demolished the dilapidated structure. Instead of reconstructing the school, they set up around 10 illegal shops. Salim Khan opened his own office, Sodagar Construction, and rented out the rest of the shops. None of the rent collected was deposited with AMC or the Waqf Board.
25 shops, 200 houses built without authorisation
The extent of the fraud goes beyond just the shops. DCP Bharat Rathod, Zone 3 in-charge, said that Salim Khan, along with Mohammad Yasar Sheikh, Mehmud Khan Pathan, Faiz Mohammad Jobdar, and Shahid Ahmed Sheikh, had also illegally built about 25-30 shops and nearly 200 houses on trust land.
This included two unauthorised six-story flats. Rent collected from around 100 houses ranged from ₹5,000 to ₹7,000 per month, and around ₹10,000 per month from each shop. Additionally, they were collecting rent from 15 residential units and misusing donations from the Shah Bada Qasim Trust’s collection box, which generates ₹50,000 monthly.
Rent collected for 20 years using false affidavits
The accused have allegedly been collecting rent from trust properties since 2005, falsely presenting themselves as trustees in affidavits submitted to the Waqf Board, including one in Gandhinagar dated July 23, 2024.
Despite never being officially appointed trustees, they continued this illegal activity for nearly 20 years. Salim Khan, who also has prior cases including murder and rioting against him, is believed to be the key conspirator.
All 5 accused arrested
The Gaekwad Haveli police have registered a case against all five under multiple charges and have launched a thorough investigation. Authorities estimate the total value of the illegally exploited trust property at approximately ₹100 crore.

title: Ex-employee, associate booked for duping Ahmedabad jeweller of ₹7lakh with fake gold chains - GujaratSamachar English

Ex-employee, associate booked for duping Ahmedabad jeweller of ₹7lakh with fake gold chains

The Vatva police have registered an offence against a former employee of a jewellery shop and his associate for allegedly duping the shop owner of ₹7 lakh by pledging counterfeit gold chains over a prolonged period.
The alleged fraud took place between October 1, 2015 and February 5, 2021, at a shop named Zanzar Jewellers, near Mamta Society in Vatva area of Ahmedabad.
Babubhai Devaji Mali (50), who runs Zanzar Jewellers and a licensed money-lending business, stated that Jagdishbhai Hakmaji Mali had been employed at his shop for nearly five years and had gained his trust during that period.
As per the complaint, Jagdishbhai lives in Vatva and is a native of Banaskantha district. The second accused has been identified as Sanjaybhai Vinubhai Thakor, also from Vatva.
In his statement, Babubhai alleged that during his employment, Jagdishbhai began introducing customers to the shop for pledging gold chains in exchange for loans. Trusting his employee, the complainant said he sanctioned loans against what were presented as genuine gold ornaments.
On October 1, 2015, a customer allegedly brought a gold chain weighing 37 grams. After assessing its market value at approximately ₹50,000, the shop advanced a loan of around ₹30,000 in cash against the pledged ornament.
On subsequent occasions, including in September 2018 and December 2020, other customers pledged gold chains weighing 136 grams and 32 grams, respectively. Loans ranging from ₹1.5 lakh to ₹2.5 lakh were reportedly sanctioned at prevailing interest rates under the complainant’s money-lending licence.
However, the complainant stated that several such borrowers failed to return to redeem the pledged jewellery. When attempts were made to contact them on the mobile numbers provided, there was no response. Upon closer examination of the ornaments, the complainant alleged that the chains were found to be counterfeit and not made of genuine gold.
On February 22, around 6 pm, a man visited the shop seeking to cut a gold chain. Suspecting irregularities, Babubhai stepped outside and noticed Jagdishbhai, who had by then left employment at the shop, standing nearby.
Growing suspicious of a larger conspiracy, the complainant contacted the police. Officers from Vatva Police Station arrived at the scene and brought Jagdishbhai in for questioning. During inquiries, the name of Sanjaybhai Vinubhai Thakor allegedly surfaced as an associate.
Babubhai alleged that after gaining his confidence, Jagdishbhai conspired with associates to send individuals to the shop with fake gold chains, thereby inducing him to disburse loans. He has claimed that the total loss incurred due to the fraudulent pledging of counterfeit jewellery runs into ₹7 lakh.
Based on the complaint, Vatva police have registered an offence of cheating, criminal breach of trust and criminal conspiracy against the two named accused and other unidentified persons who may have been involved.
Police officials said right now the two named accused have been arrested in the matter and further investigation is under way to ascertain the exact amount involved, identify other accomplices and verify the financial transactions carried out during the period in question.

MD drug laboratory found running in Surat mall:3 youths caught making drugs in food testing lab; mastermind financed operation from London
- Copy link
Surat SOG has busted a high-purity crystal mephedrone drug factory operating under the guise of a food testing laboratory inside a commercial mall in the city’s Parvat Patiya area. The operation shocked investigators after an international London connection came to light. Acting on the confession of Jil Thummar, who was caught with 236 grams of drugs in Amroli, the police raided a lab at Polaris Shopping Center and arrested three persons, including the senior technician who was manufacturing the narcotics.
In this conspiracy to produce intoxicating substances within the city and trap the youth, the accused were allegedly acting on the instructions and financial backing of a mastermind based in London. During the raid, police seized drugs, flammable chemicals, and other materials worth ₹2.92 lakh, and have intensified further investigation into the wider network.
Shocking confession came to light during Jill's strict interrogation The entire incident began on January 1, 2026, when the SOG apprehended 21-year-old Jill Bhupatbhai Thummar with 236.780 grams of MD drugs on Amroli Chhaprabhatha Road. During Jill's strict interrogation, a shocking confession came to light that these drugs did not come from an outside state, but were prepared in a private laboratory within Surat city. With this fact coming to light, different SOG teams were formed, and the scope of the investigation was expanded.
Raid conducted at 'Dikriya Food and Pharma Analytical Laboratory' The investigation led to the Polaris Shopping Center, located on Parvat Patiya Vesu Canal Road. Here, SOG raided 'Dikriya Food and Pharma Analytical Laboratory' based on a tip-off. Upon searching inside the lab, police found modern machinery and chemicals, which were used to prepare high-purity crystal mephedrone drugs. This lab, operating under the guise of food testing, was actually proven to be a large drug manufacturing unit.
The mastermind of the drug factory operates the network from London The most shocking twist in this racket has emerged as the 'London Connection'. Police investigation has revealed that the real mastermind of this drug factory is operating the entire network from London. Financial assistance and guidance required for this lab were provided from London itself. It currently appears to be an international conspiracy to push the youth of Surat into drug addiction from abroad, and 3 more accused have been arrested in connection with it.
Lab Technician, Drug Supplier, Chemical Expert Arrested Police have arrested the main mastermind behind drug manufacturing, Brijesh Vrajlal Bhalodiya (age 28), who is a senior lab technician. Along with him, Khushal Vallabhbhai Ranpariya (age 27), who supplied the drugs, and Bharatbhai alias Bhano Damjibhai Lathiya (age 32) have also been arrested. Accused Brijesh misused his chemical knowledge to prepare high-quality Mephedrone, which was sold in the market at the behest of a London-based handler.
Property worth lakhs, including prepared MD drug, seized from the laboratory During the raid, a large amount of property was seized from the factory. This includes 200 ML mixed chemical (worth ?20,000), 1 liter HB chemical, 5 liters of H2SO4, and flammable chemicals like Methyl Amine. In addition to this, a total of ? 2,92,050 worth of property has been seized, including 1 unit Vacuum Oven (worth 25,000), 1 unit Vacuum Pump (worth 20,000), an Overhead Stirrer, and a digital weighing machine. This also includes 16.950 grams of prepared Mephedrone drug, worth ? 50,850.
Currently, the police have initiated strict action against all these accused under the NDPS Act. To reach the mastermind based in London, the police are examining digital evidence and 3 mobile phones (worth 1,15,000).

title: FAKE ALERT: Video of stone-pelting on Gujarat Police shared as one from Delhi - The Times of India
article_text:
CLAIMBJP member and former Indian army officer Major Surendra Poonia shared a video in which a violent mob can be seen pelting stones at police vehicles. He claimed that the video is from Delhi.
Taking to Twitter, Poonia posted the video and tweeted -- “They have brought
Kashmir to Delhi. They are not just throwing stones but they are breaking India. All this will not be shown by the likes of Barkha, Ravish, D'Souza, Rajdeep, Wire, Quint, BBC, Scroll, Rana Ayub, Arfa, NDTV.
This is not anti-CAA movement but terrorism and its control room is in Rawalpindi!”
Here’s the archived
version of the tweet.
TRUTHThe video that Poonia tweeted is actually from Ahmedabad, Gujarat. This video is more than two months old and it is from the time when the protest against the Citizenship Amendment Act, 2019 had turned violent with people throwing stones.
VERIFICATION AND METHODOLOGYAfter watching the video carefully, we spotted a chemist shop which has its name board written in Gujarati language. The translation of the text reads ‘medicines’.
Since the name of the shop is in Gujarati, we used keywords 'Stone pelting on Gujarat police' on Google and found a YouTube video uploaded uploaded on December 19, 2019 by TV9 Gujarati channel.
Anti CAA protest turned violent in Ahmedabad; ACP injured in stone pelting incident | TV9News
Titled ‘Anti CAA protest turned violent in Ahmedabad; ACP injured in stone pelting incident’, at 0:3, the video had the same visuals as in the video shared by Poonia.
In the video by TV9 Gujarati, a shop named 'Famous Chicken Suppliers' can also be seen at around 0:48. The same shop is also visible in the video shared by Poonia.
VERDICTTimes Fact Check has found that a two month old video of stone pelting on Gujarat police vehicles is being falsely shared as stone-pelting done on
Delhi Police.

Ahmedabad City Crime Branch has booked a man for allegedly selling counterfeit Tirupati brand cottonseed oil after raiding a shop in Khokhra and seizing fake oil cans worth over Rs 61,000.
According to the FIR filed by Bhushan Mahendrabhai Shantilal Dani, a representative of NK Proteins Pvt Ltd, the company had authorised him to file complaints related to trademark violations. Acting on a tip-off, a joint team of the crime branch and local police raided a shop named Kohinoor Store near the Madrasi Mandir in Khokhra on Friday.
During the raid, police found 26 cans of duplicate Tirupati cottonseed oil with counterfeit labels that closely resembled the original company's branding. Officials also recovered 15 empty duplicate cans and a small quantity of unsealed oil containers.
The shop owner, identified as Farooq Salimbhai alias Rajubhai Gafurbhai Syed (40), a resident of Jyoti Park Society in Maninagar, was found allegedly repackaging oil from other companies into old Tirupati cans purchased from scrap dealers. Ahmedabad cyber sleuths bust Nigerian-led online fraud network, 6 held from Mumbai, Bengaluru

Summarized by AI; it may make mistakes. Check important info
In a breakthrough against transnational cyber fraud networks, the Ahmedabad Cyber Crime Branch has arrested six individuals, including a Nigerian national from Mumbai and Bengaluru, for allegedly operating a complex online scam that duped an Ahmedabad resident of over ₹32 lakh under the guise of a homoeopathic medicine trade.
The arrested accused have been identified as Nigerian national Madufor Steve Uzochi, along with Krishnamati Chaudhary, Mahesh Chaudhary, Salim Shaikh, Trijugilal Kurmi, and Rajeshkumar Saroj — all residents of Mumbai and neighbouring areas.
The police said that the complainant, Nihar Verma, a resident of Maninagar, Ahmedabad, was contacted online by individuals posing as representatives of an African pharmaceutical company. They claimed to be looking for an Indian supplier of Eupatorium Mercola Liquid, a homoeopathic medicine reportedly used in the treatment of malaria and dengue in Africa.
The accused lured Verma by offering him a lucrative business proposal to purchase the medicine from an Indian vendor, Sharma Enterprises Manufacturing, at $6,500 per litre and resell it to the 'African buyer' at $11,000 per litre.
Initially, Verma was made to believe the deal was genuine after he received a one-litre parcel of the liquid from a person named Jaydev, who introduced himself as a sales representative of Sharma Enterprises. He even met a supposed African lab scientist in Delhi who 'approved' the sample.
Convinced, Verma placed a larger order and transferred ₹27 lakh as an advance payment to the account shared by the accused. When he visited Bhilwara, Rajasthan, to collect the consignment, he discovered that the purported company did not exist. Realising he had been duped, Verma complained to the Ahmedabad Cyber Crime Branch.
The modus operandi
Investigations revealed that the scam was orchestrated by a Nigerian-led cybercrime syndicate that used social media and online communication to contact victims with false offers of international trade. Once the victims agreed, they were tricked into transferring money to multiple Indian bank accounts created under fake enterprise names.
The Nigerian national Madufor Steve Uzochi allegedly coordinated the financial transfers through associates Salim Shaikh, Trijugilal Kurmi, and Rajesh Saroj, who recruited people across Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Nepal to open fake bank accounts under names such as Shree Ram Enterprises, Star Enterprises, Laxmi Enterprises, and M G Enterprises.
The police said that Krishnamati and Mahesh Chaudhary, a Nepali couple based in Navi Mumbai, played a key role by operating multiple bank accounts and transferring the fraudulently obtained funds to other gang members in exchange for a commission.
The accused allegedly opened 12 to 15 accounts per firm and used them for fraudulent transfers. They would relocate to another city whenever a complaint was raised against their accounts.
Investigators further revealed that Salim Shaikh, the Mumbai-based mastermind, had earlier worked with another handler who provided Indian bank accounts to Nigerian nationals for financial fraud. After his death, Shaikh began running the racket independently. He is suspected of having provided bank accounts not only to cyber fraudsters but also to operators of illegal betting and gaming apps in Dubai.
Seizure and further investigation
During the operation, the police seized 14 mobile phones, seven SIM cards, 33 debit cards, and multiple diaries used for maintaining financial records. The seized debit cards were linked to accounts in Bank of Baroda, Canara Bank, Yes Bank, Central Bank of India, Indian Bank, Saraswat Bank, and several cooperative banks.
Police said that over 112 complaints have been traced to bank accounts used by this network across Karnataka, Punjab, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Tamil Nadu, and Kerala. Further investigation is underway to identify the remaining Nigerian members and Indian collaborators involved in the syndicate.

Table of Content
▼Ahmedabad: The Gujarat government announced on Monday that the owner can keep a registration number even after the car is sold or canceled, and can transfer it for a stipulated fee to a new vehicle purchased by him or her. Gujarat Transport Minister Purnesh Modi has announced that such a system already exists in Delhi, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal and has been introduced here after representations from vehicle owners.
"People are attached to their car registration numbers for several reasons, such as religious beliefs or numerology. Now, owners in Gujarat can keep the number even after the vehicle is sold or getting it scrapped," he said.
"The retained number can be transferred to a new vehicle purchased by the owner. However, it cannot be used for an old or already registered vehicle. Also, the owner and make of both vehicles must be the same. Therefore, the retained number of cars cannot be transferred to a newly purchased bike by the same person," he said.
He explained that vehicle numbers that have already been scrapped cannot be retained now, furthermore, the applicant must have owned the vehicle for at least one year to qualify for number retention.
The process of keeping the old number and transferring it to a newly purchased vehicle must be finished in 15 days.
The fee for number retention for two-wheelers is Rs 8,000 for ' golden category' fancy numbers, Rs 3,500 for 'Silver' fancy numbers and Rs 2,000 for all other numbers.
The fee for cars and four-wheelers starts with Rs 40,000 for golden category, Rs 15,000 for silver, and Rs 8,000 for all other numbers.

AHMEDABAD: Gujarat ATS has cracked a major arms smuggling conspiracy involving bogus licenses originating from Uttar Pradesh, exposing a dangerous network operating across Ahmedabad and beyond.
Acting on intelligence inputs, ATS arrested seven accused from Vastral, Meghaninagar, Maninagar, and Adalaj, while two others remain absconding but are expected to be detained soon.
The arrested Sholesinh Sengar, Vedprakash Singh, Mukesh Singh Chauhan, Rajendrasinh Sankhla, Vijaysinh Sengar, Abhishek Trivedi, and Ajay Sengar had procured fake arms licenses by paying varying amounts, enabling them to buy and possess illegal firearms. ATS seized seven weapons, comprising three revolvers with 187 live cartridges and four pistols with 98 cartridges, totaling 285 rounds.
The racket’s mastermind, Devkant Pandey of Etah district, UP, orchestrated the creation of bogus arms licenses between 2019 and 2022. Pandey, aided by Rajesh of Etah, Mukesh Singh Chauhan, and Shyamsinh Thakur, fabricated these licenses in exchange for money, fueling illegal arms circulation in Gujarat.
SL Chaudhary, Deputy SP of Gujarat ATS, told the media, "Various individuals paid large sums to obtain bogus arms licenses: Mukesh Singh Chauhan spent Rs 7 lakh, Abhishek Rajdev Rs 5 lakh, Vedprakash Singh Rs 11 lakh, Rajendra Singh Rs 7 lakh, Ajay Singh Sengar Rs 7 lakh, Sholay Singh Sengar Rs 11 lakh, and Vijay Singh Sengar Rs 5.5 lakh. These licenses were issued by the Etah district authority in Uttar Pradesh, yet none of these individuals visited the government office themselves. Instead, they collected the licenses wherever Devkant Pandey directed them.”
"The accused admitted the licenses were secured solely by paying money, without submitting any documents or proof of domicile. A preliminary investigation is ongoing against those who issued the licenses, and further inquiries are being coordinated with the Uttar Pradesh office." Said Chaudhry.
Gujarat ATS registered Case under Sections 336(2), 337, 338, 339, 341(2)(4), 54, and 61 of the Bharatiya Nyay Sanhita, 2023, along with Section 25(1-B)(a) of the Arms Act.
All seven arrested are currently in ATS custody, with their remand extended until July 16. Authorities are actively pursuing the two absconding suspects to dismantle the entire network behind this alarming arms license fraud.

Currently, there is discussion across the state about the scam of purchasing weapons based on fake licenses from Manipur and Nagaland. Around 23 accused have been arrested in this case. The accused caught by Gujarat ATS had manipulated licenses that were not renewed before UIN (Unique Identification Number) became mandatory for weapon licenses in northeastern states. They had tampered with these licenses by adding people's names. Gujarat ATS has uncovered the entire network, from document manipulation to obtaining rental agreements from other states.
Left loophole to get weapons without UIN number The illegal weapons racket may operate in any way, but those running it are clever. When weapons were purchased based on licenses from other states, this gang collected data of licenses from before 2016 when UIN numbers became mandatory, by finding a loophole. Especially in handwritten licenses, agents and players from Gujarat had systematically set up an entire system. They kept a loophole where weapons could be obtained without UIN numbers. After UIN numbers became mandatory, they created fake licenses by putting Gujarati names and photos on old handwritten and non-renewed licenses.
Most licenses are handwritten Regarding this, ATS DIG Sunil Joshi said that our investigation is ongoing. As different states were notified about this, the process of canceling licenses and taking action has begun. In our investigation, most of the licenses were found to be handwritten. The Manipur authority has started canceling weapon licenses and taking action against those responsible.
Two persons from Haryana were preparing licenses from Nagaland-Manipur During interrogation of the accused, it was revealed that these weapons and weapon licenses were obtained through seven previously arrested accused, and the seven accused had gotten licenses prepared from Nagaland and Manipur through individuals named Saukat Ali Faruk Ali Sohim Ali and Asif located in Nuh, Haryana.
Criminal history of 6 out of 16 accused Currently, among the 16 accused, 6 accused have criminal cases registered against them, including 2 cases against Arjan Viha Bharwad, 1 case against Janak Balu Patel, 1 case against Jagdish Reva Bhuva, 4 cases against Manish Ramesh Raiyani, 2 cases against Ramesh Bhoja Bharwad, and 1 case against Viram Sonda Bharwad.
16 accused paid money through Angadia or bank These 16 accused came in contact with each other during religious and wedding ceremonies, where they were impressed by seeing weapons with these seven accused and discussed obtaining license permits for themselves. Due to this, these 16 accused paid amounts ranging from 5 lakhs to 25 lakhs to obtain weapon licenses and weapons from states outside Gujarat. Gujarat ATS investigation has revealed that these 16 accused made payments through Angadia or bank transactions.
How was the entire scheme uncovered? Earlier on April 3rd, the scandal of issuing weapons licenses on rental agreements in Manipur, Nagaland, and Mizoram reached Ahmedabad. During the investigation of Bharat Bharvad, who was caught with a pistol by the Crime Branch a few days ago, it was revealed that this racket had been operating in Ahmedabad for 3 years. Mukesh Bharvad, who lives in Nana Chiloda, is the main mastermind of the scam. He had given Bharat Bharvad an all-India permit weapons license on rent for Rs. 7 lakhs. Mukesh Bharvad from Ahmedabad was selling gun licenses for 10 to 15 lakhs.
During the investigation, the Crime Branch revealed that in 2022, when Bharat Bharvad talked about getting a weapons license with Mukesh Bharvad who lives in Nana Chiloda, he offered to get an All India Permit License from Manipur for Rs.7 lakhs, claiming a rental agreement showing residence in Manipur. The accused Bharat Bharvad, who had never been to Manipur, got a rental agreement made in Ahmedabad showing he lives in Manipur and runs a vegetable cart there. He wrote that he needed the license for self-defense due to Naxalite threats in Manipur. Mukesh Bharvad along with his associate from Haryana helped obtain the weapons license.
Arrested Bharat Bharvad bought pistol for Rs 25,000 Bharat Bharvad purchased a country-made pistol for Rs. 25,000 from Soma Gamara who lives in Bharvad Vas on Pedak Road in Rajkot. Somabhai, from whom the pistol was purchased, has died. The Crime Branch has launched an investigation and filed a complaint regarding the illegal weapons license. Correspondence has been made with Manipur for verification of the license.
Criminal history of Bharat Bharvad Accused Bharat Bharvad, who has a criminal history, has a rioting case against him at Naranpur Police Station. He was arrested by Paldi Police in 2018. In 2022, he was arrested for attempted murder by firing at Sardarnagar Police Station. Satellite Police arrested him in 2024 under Arms Act, and Anandnagar Police arrested him in 2024 under GP Act. Out of 3 weapons possessed by the accused, one is in custody of Sardarnagar and another with Satellite Police Station.
Licenses made on Dimapur, Nagaland addresses Licenses were issued on addresses in Dimapur, Nagaland. title: ‘Biological attack’ plot probe: UP, Gujarat ATS search accused home at Kheri; multi-city strike foiled - The Times of India

LUCKNOW: A joint team of the Uttar Pradesh Anti-Terrorist Squad (UP ATS) and Gujarat ATS on Saturday carried out searches at the residence of Mohammad Suhail Saleem Khan (23) in Lakhimpur Kheri’s Singahi area in connection with an alleged terror conspiracy involving plans for a “biological attack”.
According to investigators, Suhail is accused of being part of a module that was allegedly plotting attacks in multiple Indian cities, including Lucknow, Delhi, and Ahmedabad. The probe began after the arrest of two others—Azad Suleman Sheikh (20) from Shamli and Ahmed Mohiyuddin Saiyed (35), a Hyderabad-based doctor with an MBBS degree from China. Saiyed was earlier detained near Ahmedabad on November 9.
Officials said Suhail is suspected of conspiring to mix poison in temple ‘prasad’ and ensure its distribution at religious sites in the three cities. Following his alleged role surfacing during the interrogation of the arrested accused, Gujarat ATS expanded its investigation to Uttar Pradesh.
A six-member Gujarat ATS mobile investigation team reached Jhala village under Singahi police station limits, where Suhail’s family resides. The team questioned his relatives and collected details about his local contacts, activities, and movement patterns.
The presence of ATS and local police triggered discussions across the village, with officers confirming that the search was part of an ongoing, multi-state investigation.
Officials said further action will depend on evidence emerging during the continuing probe.
According to information received, Suhail Khan, a resident of Ward No. 1 in Singahi and son of tractor mechanic Saleem, was arrested from Gujarat. Suhail went to Muzaffarnagar three years ago to pursue Hafiz studies. It is reported that he travelled to Gujarat around 15 days ago, where he was taken into custody by the Gujarat ATS.
Officials said that some documents and flags have been seized, which will be analysed by forensic experts. However, no explosives or arms were found till the last reports came in.
Suhail’s mother, Rukhsana, and other relatives insist he is innocent and deny any possibility of his links with terror networks. “Suhail is of very simple nature. He has no connection, near or far, with Pakistani terrorists,” she said, breaking down repeatedly. The family claims they assumed his phone was switched off because of low balance.
Last Visited Home During BakridAccording to his mother, Suhail last came home during Bakrid in June. He left again in July, moved to Muzaffarnagar for his studies, and travelled to Gujarat a week before his arrest. The family spoke to him four days ago, after which his phone remained unreachable.
Religious Studies in MadrasasSuhail completed his early education at a madrasa in Singahi Jhala and later pursued Tablighi studies at another madrasa in Salimabad under Majhgai police station. He shifted to Muzaffarnagar to continue his Hafiz studies and was staying there until his recent travel.
His father, Saleem, around 50, is a tractor mechanic who supports the family on modest earnings. Their mud house remains unfinished, lacking plaster. Villagers said the family avoided speaking to the media and even asked reporters to leave.
Suhail is the middle child among three brothers. The eldest, Summim Khan, works in Tamil Nadu selling clothes, while the youngest, Waseem, repairs air-conditioners in the Singahi area.
UP ATS to Interrogate Suhail and Co-Accused AzadUP ATS teams will soon reach Ahmedabad to question the two Uttar Pradesh-based accused arrested by Gujarat ATS—Suhail from Lakhimpur Kheri and Azad Suleman Sheikh (20), a sanitation worker from Kairana, Shamli.
According to Gujarat ATS’s preliminary interrogation, the accused allegedly admitted to conducting reconnaissance in Lucknow, Delhi, and Ahmedabad for planned attacks. Investigators claim they arranged weapons from Hanumangarh, Rajasthan, reportedly delivered via drone from Pakistan. Their alleged handler, Dr Ahmed Mohiyuddin Saiyed (35) of Hyderabad—an MBBS graduate from China—was also arrested for purportedly directing them to prepare a chemical ‘ricin bomb’.
Officials said the investigation is ongoing and ATS teams from multiple states are coordinating to verify the extent of the suspects’ activities and overseas links.

title: Gujarat ATS busts arms licence racket, arrests seven | India News - Hindustan Times

Gujarat ATS busts arms licence racket, arrests seven
Gujarat ATS uncovered over 100 people buying firearms with fake licenses from Manipur and Nagaland, leading to seven arrests and ongoing investigations.
The Gujarat Police has detected over 100 people who bought firearms on the strength of counterfeit arms licences purportedly issued in Manipur and Nagaland, a senior officer of the state’s Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) said on Tuesday.
Gujarat ATS deputy inspector general Sunil Joshi told reporters that seven people have been arrested in this connection.
The ATS has been investigating the case along with crime branch teams in Ahmedabad and Surat apart from special operations group (SOG) of several districts, he said.
Joshi said the ATS started the probe when ATS deputy superintendent of police SL Chaudhary received intelligence that there were six people from Gujarat who got weapons from some arms dealers in Haryana on the strength of arms licences purportedly issued in Manipur and Nagaland. Police Inspector N.R. Brahmbhatt led a team that conducted inquiries across multiple states to verify this information.
“Our investigation revealed that approximately 108 individuals from various districts of Gujarat had managed to acquire weapons through fraudulent means using fake arms licenses allegedly made in Nagaland and Manipur,” said a senior ATS official.
The arrested individuals Shelabhai Boliya, Vishal Pandya, Arjun Algotar, Dhairya Jariwala, Sadam Hussain, Brijesh alias Bittu Mehta, and Mukesh Bamba were all found carrying forged arms licences.
The investigation revealed that arms dealers from Nuh, Haryana, including Saukat Ali Chhotukhaan, Faruk Ali Chhotekhaan, Asif, and their associates, had been creating fake arms licenses for Gujarat residents for the past six years. These dealers reportedly sold revolvers, pistols, 12-bore guns, and ammunition to individuals possessing these fraudulent licenses, according to a statement issued by Gujarat ATS.
During the operation, Gujarat ATS formed teams that were dispatched to Nagaland, Manipur, and Haryana.
The teams have recovered three twelve-bore guns with 70 rounds of ammunition, two pistols with 59 rounds of ammunition and one revolver with 6 rounds of ammunition, it added. In all, 6 firearms and 135 rounds of ammunition have been seized, and a case has been registered under the Arms Act.
“We have identified the different modus operandi employed by this gang, including creating completely fake arms licenses, tampering with licences issued to other individuals, and manipulating old licence records,” the official said, adding that more weapons are likely to be recovered as the probe expands.

The Gujarat Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) has uncovered an international drug trafficking network with the arrest of three youths from Surat. The accused were allegedly smuggling Etomidate, a chemical commonly used in anesthesia, by disguising it as products such as aloe vera powder and exporting it to foreign countries.
According to investigators, the three accused managed to export around 125 kilograms of the substance abroad by misleading customs authorities. The seized material is estimated to be worth around ₹6 crore in the illegal market.
ATS officials said that WhatsApp chats recovered from the mobile phones seized during the investigation have revealed that the network had links with narco cartels operating in Malaysia and Thailand.
The accused were reportedly sending the prohibited substance through air cargo shipments from Mumbai airport, using false declarations to evade detection. The ATS is now investigating the wider network and trying to identify other individuals involved in the international trafficking operation.
Exported with fake Aloe Vera powder labels to two companies During the interrogation of Nikunj Hareshbhai Gadhiya, a resident of Katargam area, it was revealed that he had created companies like 'DWN Bioscience' and 'Neutral Pharma'. After registering on India Mart, he came in contact with Malaysian customers. The accused was exporting Etomidate powder by applying fake Aloe Vera powder labels. He has admitted that so far he has sent about 50 kg of Etomidate powder abroad in this manner, which is worth crores in the international market.
Chat Reveals Tracking of 4 kg Parcel
WhatsApp chats recovered from Nikunj Gadhiya’s CMF by Nothing mobile phone have revealed details about the tracking of a suspicious parcel linked to the drug network.
On February 23, 2026, a photograph of a 4-kg box was sent to a Malaysian number saved as “TH ETM.” Along with the image, a tracking number (37301788425) was also shared in the chat.
Investigators also found a reference to a person named “Mr. Chua,” who is suspected to be associated with a Malaysian narco cartel.
According to officials, the chat records indicate that the accused were not only dispatching the parcels but were also actively monitoring the shipment through tracking updates until it reached its destination. This evidence suggests a well-coordinated international trafficking network operating through courier and cargo channels.
Drug trafficking in the name of Aloe Vera powder by deceiving customs In another chat during January 2026, a foreign person asked Nikunj Gadhiya what name he would use for customs clearance. Nikunj clearly replied that he would use the name 'Aloe Vera Powder'. The accused also confessed that he regularly sends these prohibited drugs under the name of Aloe Vera or Carbomer powder. This way he was deceiving the security agencies and customs officials present at the airport.
Export chat reveals details about Sri Lanka and Malaysia In a chat from February 2026, Nikunj was asked if he could send Atomidate to Malaysia and Sri Lanka as well? Nikunj confidently said 'yes'. When the other person asked what name would be written on the parcel, Nikunj stated that their export team would decide. This chat proves that this was not the work of a single person, but an entire team was working in the backend, managing documents and labeling.
Black market pharma trading behind garment office facade The second accused Chetan Kanubhai Vavadiya, who is a resident of Mota Varachha, had an iPhone 16 Pro seized from him. He was running a garment office called 'Rudra Enterprise', behind which he was conducting pharma trading business. His WhatsApp chats also revealed discussions about customs clearance by changing product names. Chetan has also confessed to purchasing goods from Century Pharma and sending them to Malaysia, for which he was charging 5000 USD per kilogram.
Used to send Etomidate as 'Gynopol-24' powder A conversation with an American number (+1 628...) was found in Chetan Vavadiya's mobile chat from February 8, 2025. In which the other person asked, how will you send the package? Chetan had replied that we will send it after changing the name. Chetan used to refer to Etomidate as 'Gynopol-24' powder. Investigation has revealed that he has also supplied about 50 kg of powder to foreign cartels in the same way.
Exchange of courier tracking numbers with contact named 'JTT THAILAND' A Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra was seized from Bhautik Damjibhai Padmani of Amroli. He is the owner of 'Jani Pharma'. His chat shows exchange of courier tracking numbers with a contact named 'JTT THAILAND'. The shocking detail in this chat is that Thailand Police Investigation Unit had seized some parcels on February 23, 2026, information of which Bhautik received through WhatsApp.
Smuggling preparation in Taiwan and revelation in chat In another chat with Bhautik Padmani, a person from Taiwan warned him that this product (Etomidate) is illegal in Taiwan, so it would need to be sent differently. Bhautik immediately agreed and assured that he would send the goods under a different name. This criminal mindset shows that the accused knew that the substance they were sending falls under the category of banned drugs in other countries.
What is Etomidate? Why is it smuggled? Etomidate is an anesthetic substance (API) that doctors use to make patients unconscious. However, it is also misused for intoxication. In Thailand, it is placed in 'Psychotropic Substance' category-2, while in Malaysia it is placed in Group-B under the 'Poison Act'. Higher doses of this substance can be lethal, which is why these countries have strict controls on its sale and import, which these young men were violating.
Aramex Courier's Parcel Seized at Mumbai Airport During ATS investigation, a parcel sent by Nikunj Gadhiya was held at the Aramex Courier office in Andheri, Mumbai. This parcel was labeled as 'Aloe Vera Powder'. When it was tested through Raman Spectography machine, it was proven to contain Etomidate. Along with this, its invoice and Certificate of Analysis were also found to be fake, where the goods were shown as Aloe Vera powder.
Three Companies and Multiple Fake Documents Investigation has revealed that these three accused were running this illegal business under different company names - DWN Bioscience, Rudra Enterprise and Jani Pharma. They were purchasing goods from companies like Century Pharma and Velores Pharma. Under the guidance of a Malaysian person named 'Mr. Chua Zhi Xuan', they were committing customs fraud through mislabeling and misdeclaration. A case has been registered against them under various sections of the BNS.
Selling at 4-5 thousand US dollars per kilo The accused sent it to various countries at an estimated price of 4-5 thousand US dollars per kilo. Which amounts to approximately 5.75 crores. All this quantity has been seized by Thailand Police. Currently, a case has been registered against all three and further proceedings have been initiated.

title: Ahmedabad Cyber Cops Bust VoIP Racket Behind 65,000 Daily Scam Calls - The420.in
article_text:
The Ahmedabad Cyber Crime Branch, with inputs from the Gujarat ATS, dismantled a sophisticated Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP)-based cybercrime ring operating from a building near PERD Centre in Thaltej, Ahmedabad. The gang impersonated Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) officials to defraud victims by issuing fake SIM deactivation threats.
Victims were told that their SIM cards would be blocked within two hours due to alleged regulatory violations. This created panic, which the criminals then exploited to execute digital arrest and fake investment scams, extracting personal and financial data from unsuspecting individuals.
The scam had been running since 2021, with VoIP calls originating from countries including Thailand, Malaysia, Vietnam, Cambodia, Iran, Iraq, China, and Hong Kong. These calls were routed through German servers and redirected to Ahmedabad servers, giving them the appearance of legitimate Indian mobile numbers due to Ahmedabad’s STD code ’79’.
Arrests, Global Ties, and Expansion Plans Uncovered
Two key accused — Lovekesh Kumar, previously arrested in Delhi, and Anubhav (aka Anurag) Gupta, arrested in Uttarakhand — have been identified as the masterminds. They were allegedly in direct contact with Chinese national Cindy Wan, who provided operational instructions and connected them to international criminal gangs operating in Iran, Iraq, Malaysia, and Thailand.
The gang used Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) lines, initially operating with 500 sessions, and later scaling up to handle 4,500 concurrent calls across India. According to Cyber Crime DCP Lavina Sinha, the infrastructure allowed them to place approximately 65,000 calls daily between April 20 and 24 alone.
The cyber cell’s technical and field surveillance, led by ACP H.S. Makadia and Inspector J.P. Thakor, led to the identification and seizure of three servers at the Thaltej location. These servers were used to spoof legitimate numbers and evade detection by security systems.

Shell Company, Prior Cases, and Legal Action
The cybercriminals operated under a shell company formed by Lovekesh Kumar and Taruna Wadhwa, which masked their illegal VoIP setup as a legitimate business. Kumar, a resident of Karnal, Haryana, already had a visa fraud case pending against him. His accomplice, Anubhav Gupta, a telecom expert from Dehradun, was out on bail since March 2023 after being arrested in a similar cybercrime case in Sonipat.
Police officials said that the Ahmedabad hub was only the beginning. The duo had planned expansion to cities like Indore and Bangalore, replicating the VoIP scam using similar setups.
Legal proceedings have been initiated under IT Act, Indian Penal Code (IPC), and the Indian Telegraph Act, and further arrests are expected as the investigation expands.

Licenses based on fake documents from Nagaland

Widespread network across Gujarat

Operation Mule Hunt 2.0: Gujarat Police trace Rs 2,562 crore in cyber fraud proceeds

Gandhinagar, June 13 A statewide review meeting chaired by Gujarat Deputy Chief Minister and Home Minister Harsh Sanghavi ...
Gandhinagar, June 13 A statewide review meeting chaired by Gujarat Deputy Chief Minister and Home Minister Harsh Sanghavi earlier this month set the stage for what has become one of the state's largest coordinated crackdowns on cybercrime-linked financial networks.
Held through video conference and attended by the then Director General of Police (DGP) K.L.N. Rao, city police commissioners and district police chiefs, the meeting directed law enforcement agencies to intensify action against mule bank accounts used by cybercriminals to receive, transfer and launder proceeds of online frauds.
The operation, named 'Operation Mule Hunt 2.0', was launched across Gujarat on June 2 following the review exercise.
Data accessed by IANS shows that between January 16 and June 13, the exercise resulted in 118 FIRs being registered across Gujarat and 238 accused being arrested.
Investigators initiated action against 1,326 mule accounts and identified 5,124 cybercrime-linked acknowledgement numbers across India, of which 540 were linked to Gujarat.
The total amount traced through these accounts stood at Rs 25,628,282,988, or about Rs 2,562.83 crore.
The Cyber Centre of Excellence (CCOE) in Gandhinagar recorded the largest financial exposure during the operation. It registered 11 FIRs, arrested 55 accused, took action against 198 mule accounts and identified 1,117 acknowledgement numbers, including 69 from Gujarat.
The accounts were linked to transactions worth Rs 802.28 crore. Anand district emerged as another major hotspot, with two FIRs, eight arrests, action against 150 mule accounts and identification of 722 acknowledgement numbers, including 75 linked to Gujarat.
The amount traced there stood at Rs 770.38 crore. Patan district registered one FIR but recorded one of the most significant financial trails.
Police arrested 14 accused, acted against 14 mule accounts and linked them to 228 acknowledgement numbers, including 20 from Gujarat.
The amount involved was Rs 398.43 crore. Gir Somnath district identified two mule accounts linked to 290 acknowledgement numbers, including 20 from Gujarat, with transactions worth Rs 319 crore.
Amreli traced approximately Rs 107.48 crore through 22 mule accounts and 87 acknowledgement numbers. Navsari uncovered transactions worth around Rs 94.08 crore linked to 12 mule accounts and 112 acknowledgement numbers.
Kutch East reported approximately Rs 13.97 crore through 105 mule accounts, while Valsad traced approximately Rs 2.12 crore, and Tapi identified Rs 12.75 crore.
Surat City recorded the highest enforcement activity in terms of criminal cases, registering 58 FIRs and arresting 77 accused.
Investigators acted against 132 mule accounts connected to 339 acknowledgement numbers, including 82 from Gujarat. The amount traced was Rs 23.25 crore.
Mehsana registered 12 FIRs and eight arrests while identifying 872 acknowledgement numbers linked to 12 mule accounts, one of the highest acknowledgement-number counts in the state.
Ahmedabad City registered four FIRs and seven arrests, Vadodara City recorded six FIRs and seven arrests, while Rajkot City registered two FIRs and four arrests.
Ahmedabad Rural acted against 411 mule accounts linked to approximately Rs 76.68 lakh; Bhavnagar identified 141 mule accounts and transactions worth Rs 8.49 crore; Mahisagar linked one mule account to Rs 82.95 lakh; Morbi traced Rs 22.44 lakh; Narmada detected around Rs 59.37 lakh; Surat Rural traced Rs 2.31 lakh; and Aravalli identified transactions worth Rs 1.85 crore.
Several districts, including Banaskantha, Bharuch, Botad, Chhota Udepur, Dahod, Dang, Devbhumi Dwarka, Gandhinagar district, Jamnagar, Junagadh, Kheda, Kutch West, Panchmahal, Porbandar, Rajkot Rural, Sabarkantha, Surendranagar, Vadodara Rural and Vav-Tharad, did not report action in the data period.
The second phase follows the conclusion of Operation Mule Hunt 1.0, which Gujarat Police described as one of its largest cybercrime crackdowns.
Official figures released at the end of the first phase showed that police registered 565 FIRs, arrested 638 accused, initiated action against 913 mule accounts and identified 4,052 cybercrime-linked cases across India, including 491 connected to Gujarat.
The operation uncovered cyber fraud transactions worth Rs 2,289 crore. Police have defined mule accounts as bank accounts knowingly or unknowingly handed over to cybercriminals for receiving, transferring or laundering money obtained through online fraud.
Investigations conducted during the first phase found that account holders often provided passbooks, ATM cards, cheque books, SIM cards and internet banking credentials to organised networks in return for commissions.
The accounts then became transit points for funds generated through investment frauds, digital arrest scams, phishing attacks, task-based frauds and other cybercrimes.
The latest figures indicate that the ongoing second phase of the operation has already surpassed the Rs 2,289 crore uncovered during Operation Mule Hunt 1.0.
In less than five months, investigators have linked Rs 2,562.83 crore to 1,326 mule accounts across Gujarat, highlighting the scale of the financial infrastructure supporting cyber fraud networks operating across the country.

title: Gujarat police apprehend 166 'Bangladeshi nationals'; over 150, including children, being interrogated - The New Indian Express
article_text:
AHMEDABAD: A statewide crackdown on illegal immigration in Gujarat has led to the identification of 166 Bangladeshi nationals in Ahmedabad alone, while parallel operations in Surat, Rajkot and Vadodara have exposed an alleged network of unauthorised settlements, identity manipulation and cross border financial transactions.
What began as a coordinated search operation on June 2 has evolved into one of the largest crackdowns on illegal foreign nationals witnessed in the state in recent years.
At the centre of the operation was Ahmedabad, where joint teams from the Crime Branch, Special Operations Group (SOG) and local police conducted raids, detentions, interrogations and verification drives across multiple localities throughout the day and late into the night.
Police detained nearly 300 suspects during the operation. Following intensive scrutiny of documents and identities, 166 individuals were confirmed to be Bangladeshi nationals.
The group comprised 41 men, 95 women and 30 children. Investigators are continuing to verify the identities of several others who remain under questioning.
The crackdown focused heavily on Chandola, Gulabnagar and Khodiyarnagar in Danilimda, areas that have remained under the scanner following previous operations.
Officials believe earlier police action in Chandola forced many illegal immigrants to disperse to different parts of Ahmedabad, where they assumed new identities and moved into rented houses, slums, labour colonies, hotels and commercial establishments to evade detection.
As the operation gathered momentum, Ahmedabad Police Commissioner G.S. Malik personally visited the Crime Branch headquarters to review the investigation.
He questioned detainees about their arrival in India, the routes used to cross the border, the duration of their stay and their places of residence. He also interacted with officers leading the operation and commended the teams for carrying out the large scale drive.
Explaining the findings, Police Commissioner G.S. Malik said, "The operation was conducted under the supervision of Ahmedabad Crime Branch Joint Commissioner Sharad Singhal. Around 300 suspects were detained, out of which 166 have been confirmed as Bangladeshi nationals. These include 41 men, 95 women and 30 children. Some entered India only a few months ago, while others have been living here for several years. We are investigating the agents who facilitated their entry. Preliminary findings show that several women were engaged in spa related and prostitution activities, while many men were working as daily wage labourers."
The investigation has also revealed a financial trail extending beyond Gujarat. During questioning, several detainees told investigators that money earned in Ahmedabad was routinely transferred to Kolkata through the angadia network before being routed to Bangladesh.
Investigators have also found that certain mobile applications were being used to transfer funds across the border, prompting a deeper probe into possible hawala style channels and digital money transfer routes.
Police sources said the financial aspect of the case is receiving special attention as authorities seek to identify individuals and networks facilitating these transactions.
Investigators are also attempting to trace agents who arranged border crossings and helped immigrants settle in various cities using forged or manipulated identities.
The crackdown was not limited to Ahmedabad. In Surat, police launched an extensive verification drive that led to the identification of more than 100 suspected Bangladeshi nationals.
Following document verification and background checks, authorities confirmed that more than 50 individuals were Bangladeshi nationals.
Surat Police have completed the identification process and initiated legal proceedings against those found to be staying illegally.
Officials said further action is under way to complete deportation formalities and facilitate their return to Bangladesh in accordance with legal procedures.
Meanwhile, Rajkot Police launched a parallel operation at 1 a.m., deploying 10 dedicated teams across the city.
Acting on information received from the Home Department, officers questioned 272 individuals believed to be of Bangladeshi origin.
Preliminary findings in Rajkot indicated that many of those questioned were legally residing and working in the city with valid work permits.
However, scrutiny continues for individuals who failed to produce Aadhaar cards or other identity documents.
Police said strict legal action would be taken against anyone found without valid visas or mandatory immigration documents.
In Vadodara, police carried out a late night search operation targeting suspected illegal Bangladeshi immigrants across multiple parts of the city. Teams conducted intensive verification drives in areas including Sayajiganj, Fatehpura and Navayard, where officers checked identities, documents and residential records.
During the operation, nearly 150 people were verified by police teams. Following scrutiny of documents and background checks, seven Bangladeshi nationals, including one woman, were detained for further investigation.
Sharing details of the operation, the Vadodara City Police Commissioner said the verification drive formed part of the statewide crackdown aimed at identifying foreign nationals residing illegally in Gujarat.
With simultaneous operations under way in Ahmedabad, Surat, Vadodara and Rajkot, Gujarat Police have signalled a broader statewide strategy.
Officials believe illegal immigrants are increasingly avoiding concentrated settlements and are instead blending into different neighbourhoods under altered identities.
As a result, law enforcement agencies have expanded their focus beyond traditional hotspots and are now conducting citywide and state level verification drives.
The ongoing investigation is expected to reveal not only illegal immigration routes but also the networks that provide shelter, employment, forged identities and financial channels to those entering and residing in the country unlawfully.
For Gujarat Police, the operation has evolved from a routine verification exercise into a far reaching probe into an organised ecosystem operating beneath the radar.
